reviews.title: Perfect size!
reviews.body:
I was inspired to find a 'mini' backpack AFTER a trip where we stood in line significantly longer than expected, resulting in me getting sunburned because I didn't have anything to conveniently carry sunscreen in. When you're going to be under a flimsy plastic cover at a Niagara attraction, expecting to get soaked, you don't want to be trying to carry an expensive purse. Well, at another attraction, we saw a young girl with an adorable little backpack whip out her sunscreen.
Hence my quest for the perfect size for the very important sunscreen (and the husband's inhaler) that adjusts to my or his arms/shoulders. This fits the bill. Spray and cream sunscreen, inhaler, lip balm, and an interior pocket for the passports/money/wallet. The mesh side pockets are a stretch for a water bottle.
Too early to speak to its longevity, but perfect for the tourist's important items to have on hand.

reviews.title: Straps too short at 26-27 inches
reviews.body: This is a great little bag, looks exactly as pictured in the pictures and I got a good deal on it. Unfortunately I have to return it because the straps only go to about 26-27 inches when adjusted to the longest option. The straps are not soft, they are stiff polyester or nylon or something similar so the tight fit was not comfortable even just trying it on for a moment let alone taking it traveling. I was looking for something to carry around the Smithsonian on a trip to DC and this would have been perfect except for the straps not fitting. I wish there had been info in the ad about the maximum strap length. Luckily a return is as easy as dropping it off at my local UPS store no box or anything needed so no harm no foul. If the strap length isn’t an issue I say get the bag. It’s super cute and the front pocket is big enough for my IPhone 13 Pro Max even with a Otterbox case and a Popsocket wallet on it. The side pockets are nice and tight against the bag so you can put chapstick or hand sanitizer there and not worry about it flying out of the bag is tipped on it’s side. The inside has a little zippered mesh area for your smallest odds and ends. Great little bag, just too little for my back.

reviews.title: Cute but Questionable
reviews.body:
Once I got home and opened my package I just laughed at how small it is (sorry boys if a girl has ever done that to you).

It is much smaller than I expected and definitely the sample image of it on the guy's back in the listing should be way smaller. I'm a small person and this looks like it's sized for a child!

It is still very cute, but the material is questionable. Definitely doesn't look or feel like a 30$ mini backpack and I know it only costs that much because of adidas brand name printed across it.

The tag also says 100% polyester. This is definitely not 100% polyester. It feels like a polyester/nylon mix with a cheap fleece lining inside. Because of that, I'm questioning the durability and sturdiness of it even before I get to use it and ONCE I start using it, I'm hoping it lasts and doesn't break on me.

I was looking for something a tad bit smaller to use and just carry my essentials and this seems to be somewhat fitting.

reviews.title: Comfortable and Stylish
reviews.body: Backpacks are an essential part of life and if you get a good one it should last you from Middle School threw college. This bag is plenty big to carry textbooks large and small through the halls or on campus, or for whatever use you need to carry stuff around.  There are plenty of nooks and crannies to keep you organized,.  Going front the back, there is a small pouch in the front for all your small nik-naks like calculators and the like..I have a small date book where I store here.  Next is a very small pouch where you can store louse change or other small valuable items.  Next there is a bigger comportment where you can store smaller books, notebooks, and the like.  There is mesh pocket inside here for pencils or other things too small for the smaller front pocket.  Then at the back is the largest compartment for larger textbooks or maybe a laptop (my twenty-two inch laptop fits easily).  There is padding on the back to help your back but there is not much in the way of padding in the front if you do plan to lug your laptop around in this you might want to add your own padding to the front of it for extra protection of your laptop.  Then on both sides there are mesh pockets that you can put water bottles in.  Other features include a loop at the top to hang the bag up.  And of course the straps are adjustable so you can loosen them as you grow.  And for those who do not know what to do with your hands when you are walking with your backpack, the bottom of the straps have thumb loops to put them in.  So in the end, this backpack is comfortable (as long as you are not carrying too much) and stylish with plenty of places to put everything you need inside and have them nice and organized.

reviews.title: Great shoe, relatively low arch, inside posting
reviews.body:
I ordered these for my husband who runs a great deal (80+ marathon completions). The feedback below is from him.

The shoe fits nicely and as expected. I do wear running shoes a couple of sizes larger than everyday shoes to protect my toenails. They do include a top wrap which hugs your foot nicely as advertised. Running shoe fit is very personal for everyone, but these match my need perfectly. They include a bit of extra posting on the interior which helps with my overpronation. They do not include a really high arch and I find this very comfortable. The shape of the lower back of the heal is perfect for foot strike runners to roll through each stride. The cushioning is excellent without being too soft for comfortable running.

The uppers breathe nicely to keep your feet cool. The laces with the top wrap hold them securely on your feet without binding or slipping.

This is a first class running shoe. After having run for years in a different shoe, there is a good chance I will switch to this entirely.

reviews.title: Premium price , poor product. No volume control buttons.
reviews.body:
So disappointed in these second generation Apple Airpods that I bought as a gift, the recipient could not use them (bad fit, volume control issues) so I tried them.
They do not sit well in the ear, they are advertised for use during sports, among other things, but are really poorly thought out , the Airpods frequently fall out making them unsuitable for cycling. They leak sound really badly , making them unsuitable for use around other people or in quiet locations. The battery life is terrible at 1-2 hours. The sound quality is OK, on a par with earphones like the ones airlines give away.
Definitely not worth the price and to top it all Apple appear to be limiting the compatibility with other wearables (or are doing something with licensing fees) for example the Airpods do not work with Fitbit Versa devices (no volume control) . Even with the iphone there is no way to adjust the volume without getting out the phone or invoking Siri. Just imaging having to say ,hey Siri turn the volume up/down during a flight or similar.
Purchased a set of TaoTronics bluetooth headphones, better fit, battery, have a volume control and work with the fitbit Versa, oh and a fraction of the price.

reviews.title: After 2 years, still going strong!
reviews.body:
I was an AirPod skeptic in the beginning but im so glad I gave them a whirl. They work so much better than I ever expected and i have kept up with them without any issue unlike I thought I would!

A little embarrassed to admit but just a couple days ago about 20 minutes after starting my clothes in the dryer, it sound like rocks were the only thing drying! I look, oof. Loose AirPod. Keep digging, then the case. Dang. Keep digging more till finally the last pod was recovered. I was sad. Heart broken thinking I ruined my pods in the washing machine and knowing I wasn’t going to reward myself with a replacement anytime soon especially after being so irresponsible. I knew I was back to the dongle days IF I could even still find it along with some old lameo headphones. Babing* as soon as I put it in my ear! It’s a miracle! The other was dead at the time but after charging the case and both pods, they seem good as new! In fact, I’m using them right now! Phone calls work flawlessly and the tap controls too. Siri and I still have our share of issues though but that’s nothing new as she hasn’t and probably never will do what I want her to do without it becoming a hassle. I’m confident that’s just user error. 5 stars. If you aren’t sure, just do it. You won’t regret it.

reviews.title: It's Amazon that's the problem
reviews.body:
I've bought these twice. First purchase, upon arrival & opening the amazon package, I noticed that the seals on the Apple box were missing (and to mention, no plastic wrap around it). First red flag! Upon opening, everything's missing except for the charger and ear piece!! Reach out to Amazon's customer service, send pictures and basically they are next to no help.

So I risk it and place a second order. Same deal -- box is not sealed, but the product is in the box. Try to connect the device to my phone and I get a warning that the earbuds can't connect with the charging pod and are mismatched. The rest of this review is an order directly from Apple!

The Airpod Pros themselves are amazing! There's definitely some features Apple should implement that other, cheaper brands have but that seems to be the 'Apple Design Pattern' ; they know they can/and how to implement these features, but how else would they release the next gen?! But alas, I am sucked into the Applesphere for now...

The Gen 2 Airpod Pros come with XS tips. Thought maybe I'd be an XS, but upon using, noise cancellation was significantly decreased so back to S tips. Nice to finally have that option, and also gives the user the choice to mix-and-match if ears are different?

Noise cancellation is top-notch, leading the pack -- other brands are either in comparison or next to the level that these in-earbuds produce. I wear these at the office with noise cancellation on and no music to keep me focused.

Connecting to non-Apple devices is a breeze and shows no issue.

Battery life is typical of an Apple product with degradation overtime. Out of box, battery life seems to be lasting over 5 hours (I haven't drained the battery yet before my use of them is over).

Charging time appears to be fast. Of course, this is all dependent on the charging devices you are using. Are they Apple products/have the same specs of Apple products? This is important to note when choosing how to charge/power *any* electronic.

I would recommend these. However, if you aren't hard-pressed to exclusively Apple Airpods, you can find comparable noise-cancelling earbuds for cheaper

reviews.title: Buzzing and Static - Apple Won't Stand By Product
reviews.body:
These headphones were great at first, but after about 2 years of owning them, static started to develop. I brought them to the Apple store to see if they could replace them. They said the headphones were out of warranty, but that this is a known issue for a certain set of serial numbers. Unfortunately my headphones were not among those serial numbers.

Well clearly this is an issue for airpods with my serial number. It's just that apple won't stand by their product.

They then encouraged me to buy another set of airpods.

Why would I do that, knowing that they will just develop static two years from now, and Apple won't stand by their product?

I am moving on to another brand. Sorry, Apple.

Worst of all the battery life. The case wants to charge the pods even though they don't need more charging. Could be a design decision to wear them out or a defect.

Not gonna lie these saved my life on a plane a few times but for the price, very disappointing

I have an iPhone 11, and I was super happy to see that the charger for my phone was the same as my AirPods! Now its one less charger to worry about bringing on trips! The noise cancellation works amazing (keep in mind, noise cancellation doesn’t mean you hear absolutely nothing) , and I absolutely love the transparency mode option for when I’m on walks but still want to be aware of my surroundings. Overall, I do love them, my only grievance is the battery life, if you don’t have earbuds in for super long periods of time (multiple hours a day) then these would be great for you!

reviews.title: very comfortable
reviews.body:
I am delighted to provide a glowing review for the Apple AirPods Pro (2nd Generation) Wireless Earbuds. These earbuds are an incredible piece of technology that provides an amazing audio experience like no other.

The standout feature of the AirPods Pro is the active noise cancelling technology. With up to 2x more active noise cancelling than the previous generation, these earbuds provide an incredibly immersive audio experience. I was amazed at how effectively they blocked out background noise, making it easy to fully concentrate on my music or podcasts.

But what really sets these earbuds apart is the adaptive transparency feature. This feature allows me to hear important external sounds, like traffic or a person speaking to me, while still enjoying my audio content. It's an incredibly useful feature that ensures I stay safe and aware of my surroundings while still enjoying my audio.

The sound quality of the AirPods Pro is top-notch as well. The bass is deep and rich, while the mid-range and treble are crisp and clear. Whether I'm listening to music or podcasts, the audio is always balanced and enjoyable.

The earbuds themselves are also comfortable and easy to wear. The silicone tips fit securely in my ears and the earbuds stay in place even during vigorous exercise. And with the wireless charging case, I never have to worry about running out of battery.

Overall, I highly recommend the Apple AirPods Pro (2nd Generation) Wireless Earbuds. They are an incredible piece of technology that provide an immersive audio experience and a comfortable fit. If you're in the market for high-quality earbuds, the AirPods Pro are definitely worth considering.

reviews.title: Really subpar compared to Jabra 75t
reviews.body:
I've had Jabras for years - Elite Active 65t and now 75t - and I tried to branch out into AirPods thinking it could be good to have a second pair of headphones around as I often misplace or forget to grab my Jabras. I was disappointed and surprised at just how subpar and inadequate the AirPods are by comparison.

CONS:
- default eartips did not fit (Jabra's did); all extra eartips also did not fit (never had to try the others from Jabra because the default ones fit)
- perhaps because eartips don't fit, AirPods constantly feel like they're going to fall out, and don't at all seal out external noise, requiring me to turn the volume up louder
- white eartips (AirPods) vs. black eartips (Jabra) show considerably more ear wax, which looks gross
- carrying case's lid's magnetic fastener is quite weak; if you drop AirPods in a case from even a minor distance, they pop open and scatter; Jabra's physical fastener works much better to keep them shut
- lack of physical buttons really limits controls on AirPods - found it very complicated to adjust volume, and this often made the right AirPod fall out of my ear

PROS:
- if you're bought into the Apple ecosystem, there are some bonuses that come with AirPods that other headphones can't do - AirPods will read your notifications (which I found annoying), allow you to pair two pairs to a single device for co-watching, locate your AirPods in the Find My app (although Jabra has its own app which provides some ability, albeit lesser, to find your AirPods)

All in all, I was highly disappointed. The Jabra Elite Active 75t is by far the better choice as far as fit, comfort, and audio quality. I somewhat appreciated the AirPods' enhanced features when paired with Apple devices, but they are not even close to enough to get me to come over from Jabra land.

I only imagine using the AirPods as a backup if I'm desperate, and I may just give them away as a gift.

reviews.title: Exemplary Sound & Comfort
reviews.body:
Navigating the vast ocean of wireless audio options, Apple's AirPods Pro Generation 2 emerges as a beacon of technological brilliance and user-centric design.

The sound quality is, simply put, breathtaking. Each note, from deep basses to crisp highs, is rendered with pristine clarity. Music, podcasts, or calls, the experience is immersive and pure. The active noise-cancellation feature is nothing short of magic, offering a personal bubble of sound, whether in a bustling subway or a windswept park.

But what truly astounded me was their performance during workouts. Be it an intense HIIT session, a serene yoga flow, or a long run, the AirPods Pro Gen 2 remained securely in place. No more constant adjustments or the fear of them falling out during a crucial moment. It's evident that Apple has invested significantly in ensuring these earbuds are as adaptable to active lifestyles as they are to relaxed listening.

Ergonomically, they're a dream. With customizable ear tips, prolonged listening is a joy, not a chore. Ear fatigue is a thing of the past.

Seamless connectivity, impressive battery life, and the spatial audio feature further elevate the experience. Movies feel cinematic, and shifting between devices is smooth and intuitive.

Although priced at a premium, the blend of top-tier audio quality, comfort, durability, and especially their workout resilience, make them a worthwhile investment. The Apple AirPods Pro Generation 2 showcases what is possible in the realm of wireless audio, and it's magnificent. They're a must-have for both audiophiles and fitness enthusiasts.

I listened to a song and thought they just sounded a tad bit better than my earbuds with less bass. But i kept listening, and noticed that these produced almost the same amount of bass as things that i plugged IN my ears. And these are On Ear headphones. After listening to some more songs, including my own, I heard things i never noticed, and what i had noticed before, was much warmer and brighter than with the earbuds. These definitely were NOT as good as i expected due to some reviews, but i'd probably have to spend 2x as much for what i expected. Because i probably had unreal expectations. Back to the headphones, they give the exact sound of the music, they don't have overwhelming bass, but it's definitely there, just not going to make your head vibrate. They don't get that loud, but they have excellent sound quality. Im happy with my purchase and recommend these headphones if you can't spend big bucks on a pair. And beware, the cord is upwards of 6ft.

reviews.title: Good for the price but not worth the hype.
reviews.body:
Qualifications

I've owned several of the well rated under $50 headphones and used the M20X's bigger brother, the M50X for a couple years.
I'm not getting paid by anyone or receiving anything for my review; I bought the headphones completely with my own money.

Considerations

Pros
Undeniably high quality sound for the price compared to many others.
Metal inserts result in an over all sturdier product than all plastic designs.
Thick cord resists cuts.
Ear pad material isn't the type to flake allot over time.
Headphone jack is flexible for better durability.
Isolation is decent enough to soften outside noise and does a very good job at keeping sound from leaking out.
Bass is balanced; definitely there but not overwhelming.
The headphones can get loud without distorting.

Cons
Ears quickly become sore and sweaty after only an hour of wearing with average sized ears at room temperature.
Obnoxiously long non detachable cord gets in the way constantly.
Can't fold for ease of transport.
Exposed loops of wire on the back could get snagged on something and break.
Certain highs can be painfully harsh; for instance chimes and highhats.
Headband can't adjust enough to be comfortable for people with large heads.

Conclusion
Over all I regret my purchase, as these seem to have all the worst traits of the M50X and few of the good ones.
I actually like my previous pair better, the $40 Edifier H840, because even though they were much more cheaply made, they were at least comfortable and I personally preferred their sound to these ones.
I find it strange that people would suggest these for mixing, as the sound signature makes me feel very removed from what ever I am listening to, as if there was a blanket between me and what's going on, and the bass seems too colored to be called accurate.
That said, I do enjoy that loose, oomphy bass that the M series is known for when it comes to entertainment purposes as I find it perfect for allot of the music I listen to, melodic dubstep, 80s/90s rap and R&B, house, trans ETC.
But the lack of comfort ruins the enjoyment for me and it's hard to game or edit sound with these.

reviews.title: Fantastic headphones, was not disappointed.
reviews.body:
These headphones are absolutely fantastic, possibly even richer quality than the pair of 100$ Sennheisers i used to have. There is a lot of depth and bass but also seem very clear in the high end, and you can really pick out subtle details really well, even those sitting below the noise floor. I am hearing all sorts of subtle things in my music i never noticed, because i did not have good enough headphones to pick them up, which makes it feel like i'm listening to the music for the first time. I have not used them for audio engineering yet, but definitely will and have no doubt that they will be perfect for mixing and mastering.

Definitely worth the money, and then some. There are only two downsides i can see, and one is potentially an upside, depending on the person. Other people have mentioned how long the cord is. However, what they failed to describe is HOW long. If you are holding your smartphone up in your hand while standing, it will still touch the floor, it is actually enough to trip over. Which could be good in a large studio environment where you need to move around a lot, but i find the extra length to be unnecessary.

The other downside is the metal parts for adjusting the fit of the headphones. The rest of the headphones are built with a high degree of quality, but this appears to be the cheapest part. It seems that if someone were to sit or step on these headphones, there is the possibility that the metal could get bent, like a paper clip. It is not too flimsy, and that thankfully has not happened to me yet, but i would not chance it by being ultra rough with it. However, i generally keep these headphones around my neck for most of the day, as the sound quality is addictive.

I used them maybe two hours a day for the first week I had them, then put ‘em up on the shelf for about two weeks. Went back to my corded m30x with amp/dac for this period. Thought I would give 20’s another try and for whatever reason, they just grew on me. I was loving the no cord thing, but the sound actually started to really grow on me as they burned in. For this price point they are really awesome and the battery life just keeps going. Pretty damn comfy and lightweight as well. Yes, take the time for these. You won’t regret it.

Update: These have absolutely grown to be my favorite set of headphones. I have owned both Beats Studio and solo 3, Bose quite comfort 25, Sennheiser hd 569, and audio technica ath m30x, 40x, and 50x. I have to say, using the 20xbt for the last almost 2 months now. They have become my go to headphones, they have actually ruined me. I have been trying to listen to all of the others I own, and I can’t. The soundstage for close back phones is phenomenal. reviews.title: Very, very balanced soundstage/reference sound, entry level quality.
reviews.body:
Build quality: You can't tell from the images, but the build quality is not as solid as it looks. It looks like a big, heavy set of studio reference cans. In fact, it's very plasticky and a lot more fragile than that. It imitates the professional grade gear visually. I don't mind this, as the lightness helps it stay comfortable on the head, but be aware that you may feel let down by the build quality at this price point.

Comfort: the design is rather old-school, like the DJ cans of the 90s a lot of the weight goes over your ears and not onto the headband so after a couple hours it is noticeable. Not uncomfortable but if you are sensitive to this kind of thing it might bug you.

Interface/pairing: Haven't had any problems with lag on the low latency setting in Zoom calls

Microphone: very basic. You can make yourself heard on a Zoom call, but I found the mic performance to be similar to that as tested by sound guys dot com. Go listen there and see what I mean. It's not really what these things are for, but it works, and I will have to rely on it sometimes which isn't optimal but they will do.

Sound: I'm not 100% sure what these things are for. They seem to be a jack of all trades, master of none. The sound is extremely "balanced" as in flat, I imagine an EQ program could help if you have one for your PC, or phone somehow. They have no noise canceling, so they're not really great for personal music listening on the subway or something. They're not water resistant, don't fold, and and are therefore best kept at home. The low latency helps with media consumption but you might notice lag. I'm not really sure what the intended use case for these is. If you need reference cans for audio production, don't get these, get a wired set. Maybe get these if, like me, you wanted to support a real audio company instead of Anker, and you need a basic wireless set that is okay for teleworking. They're not much good for any specific purpose.

reviews.title: For the people confused about the mixed reviews.
reviews.body:
The most important thing to know about this product is that it works good for the targeted costumers, the ones that know how to use Apple Cider Vinegar.
The people who are leaving the bad reviews either have over used it or should never have bought it to begin with..
If you have dry hair you should NOT use this product.. Try the Aveeno rose water & chamomile blend.
Now while ACV DOES balance your scalps HP levels it also can dry your hair out if you use it to much or have dry hair to start with.
ACV is a great benefit to your hairs & scalps over all health if you have greasy or combination hair, if you have dry hair all this product will do is dry it out further. I recommend you look elsewhere for a treatment.
Now if you have greasy or combination hair, then this shampoo will work for you.
However kept in mind that it is not meant to be used every day, I bought this for my Mom who detests the smell of ACV my sister and I use ACV straight from the bottle 100% pure. It is much cheeper than buying a shampoo like this.
My sister has very greasy hair and so can use it everyday, where as my hair is not so greasy and will get dry if I was to use it everyday. I use ACV about 3-4 times a week..
ACV strips off all the build up on your hair making it silky and balances your HP making your scalp healthy, excessive oils are cut down.
Over all ACV is great heath boots for your hair and this product will do just that.. If used correctly.
I hope this helps clear up some of the mixed reviews, and you will be able to decided if you should use this blend or other Aveeno blends.

reviews.title: Gave me headache + hurt inside of ears
reviews.body:
UPDATE:
I gave the headphones another shot, still don't like the buttons. The pain in my ears is seeming to subside so I guess my ears just needed to get used to it. I've been trying to "pop" my ears while wearing them to get my ears used to being at a normal level while wearing them in quiet mode.

The quality of the headphones themselves seems fine and durable, but the buttons are at a weird location and hard to find for a bit. The three buttons don't feel that much different in terms of height so its easy to pick the wrong one. The buttons also don't put the volume down quickly, I had to press them one at a time to lower or increase the volume instead of in quick succession.

Within minutes of putting the headphones on and getting them set up the insides of my ears began to throb and in under 10 minutes, I had a raging headache. This was while the volume was extremely low. I'm someone who can't deal with loud noises so I got these to help me not lose my mind in certain places but they don't seem to be a good fit. I'm sure not everyone would have the debilitating pain I did but for me, these were a no-go. It might be due to the noise canceling being decently good that my ears feel like they're going to burst so I'll be trying some cheaper options to see if it will fix it. I did get them on sale but even at $250, it doesn't seem worth it at the end of the day.

reviews.title: Decent hardware, but awful software!
reviews.body:
The software is SUPER buggy, and there are several terrible design choices. If it weren't for that... these would be quite good headphones!

Bugs:
1. Right side sometimes becomes MUCH quieter (1/4 as loud?), so then it feels like only the left side is working.
2. There's a mode to keep your noise cancelling mode from the last time you used the headphones - simply does not work!
3. Often does not connect to devices - you need to restart the headphones or reset the bluetooth on the device to connect.

Terrible design choices:
1. Unlike QC35, THERE IS NO WAY TO TURN OFF NOISE CANCELING. This is super annoying in quiet environments where you get "ear suck" or windy environments where the wind will always brush the outside mic and it'll "cancel" noise that isn't there, generating a lot of wind noise. It doesn't even have to be that windy - a fast walk in an airport will generate this "wind" noise.
2. The button to turn on the headphones is on the flat of the earpad, so pressing it creates a huge pressure increase on your ear.
3. The voice assistant will interrupt your music/book to say "battery low, please charge now!" many times, and this can't be disabled. The voice is also super low quality and annoying in tone.

reviews.title: No auto pause, no quick manual pause. Otherwise better than Sony.
reviews.body:
I am a long time LG neckband user and i always had to think what I'll do when taking calls. Had airpods for that but also some cheap taotronics were ok. In-ear earbuds are just too bothering while headphones are also inconvenient. I never cared about the noise cancelation even with airpods

Recently, Galaxy Buds Live came to the rescue due to their unique design and good microphones.

However, due to the increased noise in my new home office i decided to try these and Sony mx4.

As stated elsewhere, these are more comfortable and also the calls are better. Just tried next to the blower and really Bose is better. I also find noise canceling to be more pleasant.

Now, Sony has lots of advanced features i don't care about but the problem and they they also have too many firmware issues. Certain things are hard to execute and Bose decided to take a safer approach. But that cannot charge this money for a bit improved QC35 II noise cancelation. Some very important things actually take very little effort:

1. Auto pause when removing the headphones. Really, this is 10yr old tech. it's cheap and really improves the usability. It's not there.

2. Quick manual pause - no touch controls, no large buttons. Quick to access is the lower volume button, and from there you work your fingers to find the pause button. Really bothering when kids show behind me with a question and it takes me couple of seconds to pause.

Now, why 3 stars. Well, QC35 II is 5-stars but cannot just copy it, charge 330$ and still get 5 stars.
Probably would give them 4 stars but cannot since they removed the equalizers from the app. They simply wanted to leave some features for the more expensive headphones (NC700). Well, this is not a premium feature, cannot play people like this.

reviews.title: Strange product feature compromises
reviews.body:
I bought and returned these headphones after finding them borderline unusable. I have wired Bose QC35s that I like just fine. They do their job and act like headphones. I figured QC45s would be more of the same, with improvements. Instead, with the QC45s, the audio more or less delivers, but there are some pathological product features that deviate from what you might intuitively expect headphones to do. Every potential buyer should know:
(1) they can't charge while you are using them (how is this acceptable in 2022!)
(2) they lose charge when you are not using them (I swear they were off, but it is possible the controls mislead me and they were on all the time, but there was no power indicator light and the switch was in the right position)
(3) there is no real way to use them in a passive mode (your options are either noise cancelling or piped-in outside sounds and if you don't have power for those, you can't use the headphones)
(4) When you use a wired sound source, the volume is lowered to be virtually audible and you have to turn it back up * every time*.

So imagine charging them 2 days before, taking them out of their case at the beginning of a long flight, and finding them dead. OK, at least wired sound will work ... nope. OK trickle charge via the plane's flaky usb port for a half hour and then use them wired with low charge. Neighbor needs to get up, unplug the cord to let them pass, plug back in, but they have switched to your phone's bluetooth and wont go back to wired. Turn the headphones off and back on while plugged in to re-establish the wired connection. Oh no! No sound. Is the battery dead? No, you plugged in the audio cable, so the volume level reset to inaudible.

A lot of people seem to like the headphones, but these product design decisions are crazy to me. Wireless headphones should just work, including as a backstop all features that wired ones provide. I didn't even know I had to check whether they could carry wired sound with noise cancelling off or whether they could charge while in use. It is totally obvious that they should do these things, especially for the price.

reviews.title: Aware mode failed me when playing instrument to music
reviews.body:
I'm a long time user of the QC35ii and a conga player.
I was very excited to learn about the Aware mode of the QC45 thinking I will finally be able to hear and play with Bose sounds quality and while sparing my ears a bit as the AirPods are quite harsh on your hearing.

I purchased a QC45 headset and am returning it. Whenever I drum, especially on a lower bass conga (tumba), the sounds are converted by the QC45 to some artificial electronically generated noise - very loud too, which would have been fine if only it sounded like a drum. --- Aware mode proved useless for my particular case.

When drumming along with the QC35ii and noise cancellation off you can hear the conga but the sound is
still muffled and artificial. That why whenever I want to enjoy both the music and the conga sound I'll continue to use the Apple AirPods Pro, and replace my broken QC35ii with another set of the same.

reviews.body:
I just received these today. I'll write more once I start using them.

But number one thing to note:

• I immediately threw these on a scale and weighed them:

The headphones, by themselves, weigh 8.3 ounces.

I've seen specs in reviews and comparison articles that are all over the place, saying they weigh either 8.5 or 15.5 ounces (a pound!). This was a huge factor for me when debating whether to buy QC 35 II or QC 45. If they really weigh a pound, then that would have been a total deal-breaker, but I had to see for myself.

They weigh only 8.3 ounces.

Another decision factor for me was ear cup comfort. QC 35 II: pleated vs QC 45: smooth. I've used the old, wired QC 2 for like a decade. Pleated cups, and comfortable for non-stop 15 hour plane rides. How do the QC 45's smooth cups compare? They're really comfortable. I don't notice any immediate difference in comfort. They seem good.

So, 2 for 2: Weight: check. Ear cups: check.

I'll write more about sound quality, bluetooth connectivity, etc., as I start to use them.

reviews.title: Better than Quiet Comfort 35 ii
reviews.body:
I was hesistant to purchase the new 45's after reading the reviews. After years of using Quiet Comfort 35 ii's, I can safely say these have better sound quality. No doubt about it, using these back to back with a pair of 35's, these were significantly better. Were they massive better? I would say easily better sound, not massively better sound. With the high's of the 45's you hear more, you here more sound, more crisp highs, and that's where the difference is. Bass was the same between the two headphones, the difference is the highs.

The quality of the head phones is a bit better all around too, better buttons, better head cushion, no Bose emblem to damage or rub off. Bluetooth 5.1 way way better than 4.0. I can listen to these headphones from severall rooms away, in comparison, 35's are not reliable from only 15 to 20 feet away.

Even if everything with the 35's and 45's were equal (which they are not), the bluetooh 5.1 is massive upgrade over 4.0. Only negative, is using two devices at once, I have some problems with the headphones from transitioning to one device to the next. That's possibly because other devices I am using are not bluetooth 5.1 (but are 4.0). That's really the only negative about these headphones. Easily forgiven, since everything else on these headphones is superior. Also, USB C, much faster charging is nice, easy to connect over mini USB. Noise canceling is way way better. Cannot even hear a person next to you when listening to music at a decent volume level. Bravo Bose, Bravo!!!

I was highly skeptical at first, wasn't going to purchase... Glad I did. Highly recommend over 35 ii's, worth the extra money easily. I couldn't even go back to the 35's after using these.

reviews.title: Comfortable, great sound, some minor annoyances
reviews.body:
I've had the QC45s for about a month. I got them because my roommate has had a pair of QC35 IIs for many years, and I wanted a pair of my own and wanted to see if the reality was as bad as some of the reviews.

Overall, the negative reviews are a bit exaggerated - I think these are great headphones. Super comfortable, great noise cancellation, pretty solid battery life. The ability to edit the quality of the sound in the app (more/less bass, treble, middle, etc) is really nice and has made a noticeable difference in the quality. Based on what I've read, this was a very recent addition to the QC45s and was much needed.

However, there are a couple of issues.

One of the most annoying things that was proven TRUE from the negative reviews is this: whenever I'm connected to both my laptop and my phone, if I'm listening to my laptop audio through the QC45s, there are little lapses/missteps in audio every couple of minutes. They are quick, but they are annoyingly noticeable because they are frequent. And this is a consistent problem. THE SOLUTION is to disconnect your phone through the Bose Music app if you plan to use your computer audio for the day (i.e. a long workday). If you disconnect your phone, you'll eventually have to reconnect (of course), but it will stay connected to your laptop and the audio has been perfect with this strategy. Small, but annoying nonetheless.

Another thing: it's not easy to switch between the laptop and the phone audio through the Bose Music app. It seems like my laptop takes 'precedence' when I turn on the headset (it remembers both), so if I want to switch to my phone audio, I have to go into the app and turn off the laptop connection manually. I wish the headset was more intuitive/there was a quicker way to change.

Sound quality is very comparable to the QC35 IIs (perhaps because of the ability to manually edit the different levels of sound in the app), just as comfortable, and honestly look a lot better.

TLDR; I think these are bit overhated, I've liked them and look forward to continuing to use them (and hopefully to Bose continuing to update them and improve the QOL and usage). I do agree that if you don't care about the aesthetic (QC45 looks much better than QC 35 II in my opinion), you would have a very similar experience with both of these.

The first day I had them I listened to them in the car for about 10 mins and they sounded great. The next morning I used them for a morning walk/light jog and literally every time my feet would make contact with the ground there was a loud bang in the headphone speaker (yes it was on silent mode). I changed all the settings and could not get it to go away I even turned them on and off numerous times. Yesterday was the second time I wore them and there is a constant buzzing in the left ear and only goes away when noise cancellation is off. I’m returning these and going to back to beats.

reviews.title: Mediocre sound quality but excellent ANC
reviews.body:
Was really expecting better sound for the cost. The bass is not satisfying and boosting the EQ does very little. The rest of the sound is about average. I would classify the overall quality to be in the upper portion of "standard", if that makes any sense to anyone. I don't feel the audio quality is anywhere near MSRP.

But I decided to keep this product anyway for several important reasons.
The latency over Bluetooth is minimal. This product will connect to a PC just fine and play audio without delay.
The battery life is exceptional. I can wear them all day just fine. Easily well over 16 hour battery life with high volume and continuous use. I even forgot to charge it some days ago there is still plenty of power left.

The ANC is great. I live in an area with phenomenal noise pollution. This cuts well over 90% of it away. By far the most useful feature for me.

But overall though I feel as if I'm settling with an inferior product. I don't necessarily feel satisfied with it.
Bose is using a cheap audio driver in what is supposed to be a premium product. It just doesn't sit well with me. Feels like something fraudulent.
But unfortunately this is only good ANC you can actually wear all day. Don't even get me started on the Sony WH1000 XM5.
It's pure garbage with flat muffeled audio.
The entire audio industry seems to be generally corrupt. There is virtually no information on how audio speakers are produced and what makes them expensive. I did plenty of research on this, it's a very limited market with very few engineers. Seems like a conspiracy to me!! Haha

reviews.title: This is the best cup of coffee I have made at home
reviews.body:
I have recently begun working from home and found myself having a really hard time finding a quality coffee that I could make at home. Everything was mostly too weak or didn't taste great--granted it could have been the maker. (My previous employer had coffee stocked and made for employees)

I have gone through multiple types of coffee and had seen Cafe Bustelo--I finally did today and I am LOVING IT! I did my normal 4 cups of water, saw in other comments/threads that Cafe Bustelo was stronger so did 2.5 tbsp and this is the best cup of coffee I have made at home! It definitely rivals the stuff they used to hand out at my old job and I am just so happy I don't feel like a coffee making failure anymore. I love the flavor and the almost sweet notes at the end. I recommend this and the price is the cherry on the cake.

It just didn't pack the punch I was expecting. I actually was a little nervous using this as I was worried the espresso ground would clog the filter, but when I pulled the cork the coffee poured out. reviews.title: Don't be scared by the low price -- this is the best coffee on the market!
reviews.body: Don't be scared by the low price -- this is EXCELLENT coffee!  This is far and away my favorite, and the only one I buy anymore. I like good, strong, high quality coffee and most coffee shops and most store brands just don't cut it. I've worked in gourmet coffee shops, and am surrounded by people who pay a fortune for swill from big name stores. I'm not there. I want really good coffee, no fuss, and I'd rather not pay a fortune for it. Café Bustelo is the undersung hero of the coffee world. This is really dark and always really fresh. The coffee I make at home with this is so good that I seldom buy coffee at local coffee shops because it tastes watery and bitter by comparison. Cafe Bustelo is rich without being greasy, dark without being bitter. I use a stove top espresso maker and the coffee comes out perfect every time. Two shots of this make the perfect latte, cappuccino, bullet proof coffee, Americano or whatever else. I like it shaken with coconut oil for vegan bulletproof, and then I don't crave coffee for the rest of the day. But it doesn't really matter what you do to it or with it, it's just plain good. And super cheap, so it's like an added bonus each day - delicious coffee and knowing you're not paying out for it.  I'm not into the commercialization of coffee culture and using your drink as a measure of status. I just want good coffee with no hassle. And this is that.

reviews.title: Love my Cafe Bustelo :)
reviews.body:
I used to drink Starbucks Americanos every.. single.. morning at $3/pop! Now I use 6 teaspoons of Cafe Bustelo in a 3 cup french press (I use one from IKEA, but really, any french press will do). I do use filtered water, which I'm sure helps the flavor of the coffee. It is almost comparable to Starbucks Americano.. with LESS of an acidic element. I have much less heart burn with Cafe Bustelo, and my wallet is happier. I'm spending closer to $3/week, rather than $3 a day. I do have more of a caffeine 'hit' with the Starbucks, but overall, I'm getting enough caffeine with the C.Bustelo. I do NOT get the awful caffeine headaches that I get when I am drinking Starbucks for several days, and then miss a day.
Overall, YES, I love C.Bustelo. Now I just use Starbucks medicinally, for when I need to do some serious housecleaning or work on a project with extreme focus :)

reviews.title: Excellent coffee at an excellent price
reviews.body: Compared to most ground coffees out there, this is a terrific value. Though a dark roast, it has none of the "burnt stick" flavor of so many others. You can brew it very strong indeed, if you want to, but it will remain smooth tasting. I make mine pour-through and French press. The former is a little hit and miss in terms of the strength, but whether it comes out too weak or too strong, it still tastes good. If I hit it just right, it tastes far better than most Starbucks and Caribou grinds I've had; almost chocolate-y rich. Moreover, for me 10 oz. of Bustelo goes further than 12 oz. of most anything else, because I can use a smaller quantity to get to the flavor I like.

I always dive into the reviews before buying anything. Something is going on with Amazon. They are slipping in their own fecal intentions. Boxes arrive late, or not at all. Alot of broken items. Alot of Amazon happy belly items leaving me less than satisfied. Alot of items are too close to their expiration date. I ask for a specific item and get either the wrong one x 3, a smashed jar or nearly outdated product. It seems to me that Amazon is on its way out. Sad too. I used to really like them, but just like a socialist manifesto, its all promises and a cover up of how bad things really are with no hope of actually ascribing to the ads. I really don't want to spoil it for everyone but the truth is that if you buy this washed out coffee, expect less of the company that used to give you more. Sorry folks, just telling the truth.

reviews.title: Works well for me
reviews.body:
How one enjoys one coffee over another, is about as subjective as the feel of a bicycle saddle. What feels good for one, might not feel so good for another. Caribou coffee ground medium blend works well for me as part of that morning ritual. Especially here in NE Minnesota, coming back in the morning after that cold dog walk to a hot mug of coffee is wonderful.

I don’t make it particularly strong, but I get the little pick-me-up as well as the warmth without feeling jittery. The taste is smooth, the effects don’t push me over an “edge”, and it’s just a mellow wake up to begin the morning rituals.

reviews.body:
We went on a quest to find a coffee we could live with that was less acidic than Starbucks but still tastes good.

This was not that coffee.

It reminded me of the coffee I drank at low paying jobs. It's one virtue back then was that it was free.

Seriously, though, some people prefer this sort of weaker muddy brew and that's fine. They might call it smooth and earthy, lol. But I dislike it.

We settled on Eight-o-clock brand coffee after our taste tests. If you love Starbucks but need to go less acidic for an everyday brew, try that.

reviews.title: Takes me back to my youth! ❤️
reviews.body:
I lived in Manhattan in the late 1970s. I was never really a coffee drinker, I’m still not that much, but there was a Chock Full o’Nuts diner at Columbus Circle, which I frequented after trying their coffee just once. I’ve had coffee since, definitely not a Starbucks fan, but I never really enjoyed any coffee flavor as much as those days and Chock Full o’Nuts.

So two days ago, I was sitting watching television and for absolutely no reason my mind said, “I wonder if they still sell the tins of Chock Full o’Nuts?“ I went to Amazon, and sure enough they still did! I had thrown out my coffee maker ages ago because it just wasn’t getting used. So I ordered the tin of coffee and a coffee drip gizmo that you put in the cup and pour hot water over the grounds; since I’ve never really been a whole pot of coffee person. The coffee maker was a loss and I’ll be returning it but the Chock Full o’Nuts is like being back at Columbus Circle in the 1970s and those were really good memories for me. I’ll be buying a coffee press through Amazon and enjoying the rest of my Chock Full o’Nuts coffee.

If you’d like Starbucks, you probably won’t like Chock Full o’Nuts original and if you’re a coffee connoisseur, you probably won’t like any of the Chock Full o’Nuts flavors because it’s just regular, down to earth, ordinary coffee. It’s not bitter and it just has its own flavor, which I really enjoy. So I do recommend it, but take those comments I just made to heart if you’ve never had it before.

The first time I bought a women's boot, the second time I bought a men’s boot as I thought the sole would be sturdier and last longer. This was not the case. They are very comfortable to wear straight out of the box and it feels like you are walking on cushions, however, the foam sole disintegrates and wears down within weeks of use. A thin outer sole made of sturdier materials last only weeks before the foam sole is exposed. As soon as the foam is exposed the sole wears down very quickly, often in chunks. Buying new boots every 2 months isn’t reasonable. I’m very disappointed with these boots.

If you're putting in ten miles a day on the Appalachian Trail, yes, you'll probably wear these out in short order. reviews.title: My second Dakine backpack... And I love it
reviews.body:
[[VIDEOID:aab679a8b080161644e5e6f7571974b7]] My last Dakine backpack finally quit after 7 years of daily use going to and from work and school and quite a lot of traveling for work and personal purposes. That is the plan with this one (minus school. I graduated lol).

This is a replacement and man can this thing fit A LOT more than my last one.
There are two main pockets. One for regular stuff and one for a laptop. Then several smaller pockets for organization and chargers etc. It also has two waterbottle holders (one on each side).
I fit two laptops, my giant sketchbook, a medium notebook, a coloring book, some watercolor postcard paper, paint, drawing utensils, a candle, a switch, various chargers, and some odds and ends with space to spare. It did not look overly full and I love that.
Here's to another 7 years of this pack!

reviews.title: This backpack can make a tough hike a picnic
reviews.body:
As retirees, my spouse and I are doing more hiking around our state, and we wanted a way to take along food and drink for the two of us without toting a traditional cooler and without having to cut hikes short to get back to our car. This backpack is a great fit for our needs. It allows us to stow enough food and beverages to start a hike in the morning, have a picnic lunch, and continue hiking into the afternoon.

We love that it has an insulated compartment for food and drink, and we were able to enhance that by buying some very slim refreezable ice packs to slip in easily here and there. The backpack also includes a small blanket that is plastic on one side, good for us when we pause before the morning dew dries. The backpack comes with plates, plastic cups, and a few utensils, enough for the two of us. The shoulder straps are adjustable, and I've worn the pack for several miles without ever feeling uncomfortable hauling it.

Buying this, we felt like we were maybe taking a chance and may get a product we wouldn't like, but we're very pleased with it.

reviews.title: Smells great but flavor is very burnt
reviews.body:
I'm including a photo because sometimes I've ordered items that stated it was for multiples and then only received one item from Amazon/company. This is indeed for 3 cans of the coffee which seemed like an incredible bargain.

A work colleague introduced me to this coffee. She had the Keurig capsules and it was DELICIOUS. The taste was great - I'm not great at describing what I eat or drink - but I'd say really full, rich and just flavorful all around. I didn't even need cream - it was that good. And the scent - so aromatic.

However the cans don't yield the same coffee. The scent is still amazing. When you peel that aluminum seal off, the scent envelops you in that warm, cozy toasted hazelnut scent. I was excited to get brewing in what I consider my better coffee maker. So excited that I brewed a cup of coffee at 6 in the evening.

However the coffee tasted bitter and not as flavorful.

I'll experiment with my pour over and reduce the temperature to see if I can get rid of the bitterness but right now I have 3 cans of coffee that I may have to donate.

p.s. tried several different methods and all yield the same burnt tasting coffee.

reviews.body: Since moving to 100% remote work in March, I have gone through probably close to ten of these giant 36 oz bags. Just for myself, to be clear. But somehow the few people that do drop by (family) always ask me to make them coffee. This is not fancy hipster stuff, but neither is it cheap "I just need caffeine and I need it now, I don't care how bad it tastes" bulk coffee that the office used to supply me with. It tastes great, and brews well in my cheap $15 Mr. Coffee machine. I don't think I've gone through a single workday morning without a few cups of this stuff; it's definitely the highlight of having to wake up so early in the morning.  A true, great-tasting workhorse. One thing I do, though, to try to preserve freshness is buy some of those rubber-sealed glass jars to keep the ground coffee in. I think it does make a difference. I've noticed with other brands of coffee that I've bought in the past, the coffee goes from smelling delightful to smelling stale in just a couple of weeks if I don't keep them in sealed containers.

However, I decided to return this product and order the Kanken No. 2 15" Laptop model. However, I think this backpack is great option if you are not planning to use it to carry a laptop very often OR just carry a small tablet or similar. reviews.title: Not recommended for dry hair
reviews.body:
I have 3c/4a multi-racial (Black, Spanish) hair. I try to stick with moisturizing shampoos because anything less dries my hair out severely. My hair is naturally dry and curly so I have to be careful. This shampoo had that drying effect that was not pleasant. It smells nice, and suds up to a very rich lather for the first wash, but after the rinse I couldn't fathom giving my hair a second wash because it was so dry. And this is with a lot of moisturizing products I use on my hair. Quite a few years back there was a TV commercial for some shampoo and they said that their brand "passed the squeak test." Meaning, if you could press a finger down on your wet hair after washing, pull down your finger hard and hear a squeak, then it was purely clean. Well, this shampoo did pass the squeak test, but I fear it's because it was stripped of not only my moisturizing products but the hair's natural oils as well.

The reason for four stars is because the shampoo specifically says, "for normal to oily hair." Since my hair is dry and it got even drier, I think this product is ideal for hair that is more oily than normal. It did do the job -- my hair was "squeaky" clean -- but it really does have some kind of drying agent that oilier heads will probably love.

reviews.title: Why Change A Winning Formula?
reviews.body:
The original Pure Clean was an excellent shampoo. The scent was great, it was very effective and it leant body. Then Garnier decided to change the formula and add aloe. Now the shampoo robs hair of all body and literally makes it look like it's been plastered to your head by some maniac with a glue stick. I have curly hair, so I don't need much encouragement to achieve body, but I've never known a shampoo that turns my hair straight and clumpy.

So, if you're looking for a shampoo that'll make your hair look good. Maybe give this one a miss. But if you're looking for a shampoo that'll turn your curly hair into a limp lank mess that can best be described as "the bedraggled look," then these guys have got the shampoo for you.

reviews.title: Great shampoo!

I have since purchased the Pure Clean Conditioner and been equally satisfied.  For fine hair used to being weighed down by products, this is an enthusiastic recommend.

I threw this bottle in the cart one day when money was tight, and my hair care life was never the same again. This shampoo cleanses the hair perfectly, leaving my scalp and I feeling squeaky clean after a wash. I usually shampoo my hair every other day, but because I do modern dance that entails a lot of rolling around on the dirty dance studio floors, I sometimes wash my hair two days in a row. This shampoo allows that. It doesn't build up in the scalp and is very lightweight. I pair this with the same conditioner, usually, but other conditioners work perfectly well with this shampoo, at least in my experience. 10/10 highly recommend! And you can't beat that price.

reviews.title: Favorite Shampoo and Cruelty-Free
reviews.body:
I love nearly everything about Garnier Fructis. It smells utterly amazing. It leaves my hair clean, silky smooth, but not flat. It has vitamin E and argan oil, which helps nourish the hair and prevent frizzies. It's also paraben-free and vegan. The only negative is that it isn't sulfate-free, although some of their conditioners are. I find that I rarely need to condition my hair after using this product -it's just not necessary.

As of 2021, Garnier no longer sells in China and is now Leaping Bunny certified -it means that it is cruelty-free, not tested on animals. I encourage every person who is an actual human being and not a selfish monster to try their best to avoid any/all beauty products that test on animals. I eat meat (mostly organic and pasture-raised) and concede that doing so is unfair to animals, especially given the cruel industry practices widely found in the USA. However, most humans on earth do eat meat and animals do eat other animals. You know what they don't do? They don't torture them to death in a lab so someone can look pretty with the resulting products. I don't care if you are vegan or a meat eater like me... if you knowingly buy beauty products that torture animals in a lab for what in today's world mostly amounts to highly unnecessary testing, you are a monster. Now you read this and you know... if you don't know... go and google pics of animal testing and read up more. Again, I know that eating meat sometimes results in cruel practices as well, but I try to buy organic, pasture-raised whenever possible to mitigate support for animal cruelty in that industry. For beauty products, however, I alway check if it's cruelty-free -there is zero justification for torturing an animal so you can have less wrinkles or silky hair. You should check, too, and can do so on Ethical Elephant's website; there you can type in any popular brand and some lesser known ones as well and can details on whether or not they test anywhere (including third-party testing for the rights to import/sell in China).

Bottom line: Garnier Fructis is wonderful for my hair, a healthier option for me (just wish it didn't have SLS), and bunny approved as cruelty-free! Buy/try... you will love it.

reviews.title: I like my coffee with cream/no sugar and many coffees are ...
reviews.body: Delicious!  I'm very particular about coffees and this one definitely makes the cut. I like my coffee with cream/no sugar and many coffees are too bitter without a touch of sugar--not this one!  For years I brewed Starbucks' Guatemala Antigua.  I still love it but it is pricey.  The Gevalia Columbia (for me) has a similar taste profile to Starbucks' Guatemala Antigua--both are very smooth with almost no bitterness.  I highly recommend this blend from Gevalia; I like it much better than their house blend and it is very affordable.  My only complaint is that the only subscribe and save option available is for 6 12-oz bags ;+(  I'd love to have a 3-bag option available for S&S.

reviews.title: Maybe my perfect morning brew at last.
reviews.body:
As the ad says, medium bodied and bright. Perfect for my morning cuppa.
While a one-shot espresso would certainly be a wake up call, I prefer to linger
over a full mug of coffee. I don't want my coffee to yell me awake.
The grind is very fine. Not quite espresso fine. This is what makes this work
for my morning cup of Americano.
I use the Mr. Coffee espresso machine ... the cheap one ... no, I am not a
coffee snob. I use the 2 mark for the grind and the 4 mark for the water.
(Use good water.) This results in a cup of Americano that's good all the way
to the bottom of the mug. The coffee is bright and full flavored with no bitterness.
Not as oily as most I have had in the past. Brews almost completely dregs free.
Not lacking at all in wake-up attention getting power.
So now I relax on the patio in this beautiful fall weather and slowly but brightly
snap my day on. Love it. Cost is reasonable as well.

reviews.title: FINALLY, SOME RELIEF!
reviews.body: I've dealt with an itchy, oily scalp for a decade. I couldn't go even a day or two without itching and greasy flakes. Tried everything including expensive organic "Scalp Treatment" and hypoallergenic "tea tree" shampoos. Then COVID-19 hit, and I decided to go cheaper (since the expensive stuff was lukewarm at best). Accidentally went a week without washing (horribly busy week) and NO ITCH WHATSOEVER. The shampoo didn't "tingle" or anything on contact. It had a surprisingly "normal" feeling, no instant gratification. But after that week, and the weird realization that I hadn't shampooed in so long, it dawned on me: I was a whole week flake- and itch-free with only ONE wash. Can't beat that.

reviews.title: Would use again
reviews.body: I should preface this by saying I have a fungal scalp issue (most people do- dandruff is caused by fungus but also general hair dirtiness/ oily/ smell that won't go away- not always flakes). In my case, Nizoral happens to have the right medicine to combat it. In the past, in my search to overcome this issue, I tried some older similar lemon-lime version of Head & Shoulders and it was so bad that I immediately threw it out, out of fear that I would find it under my sink and use it again a year later, forgetting how horrible it was. I rarely hate a product enough to do that. So not that H&S is "bad"... just that it didn't work for me. This version is much nicer and improved, but it still scared me because after I used it, I had flakes that weren't there before - which is suspect and makes me think this is one of those products that causes the user to keep having to use it because it creates more problems than it solves. It didn't let me extend much time between washes, although it was slightly less oily on day 2. On a positive note, I have been reaching for this shampoo lately when I feel like I need a clarifying shampoo- even over my beloved Neutrogena, because this product works to clear buildup and is creamy, and sometimes that feels like a better move than these transparent shampoos that sometimes feel as harsh as dish soap. On a "neutral" level, my colored red hair didn't fade too much when using it. No more than any other standard shampoo not designed for color-treated hair. I got this product for free from bzzagent and Head & Shoulders!

reviews.title: Improvement over the Citrus Breeze Fresh Scent Technology Shampoo, but not the best solution for fine/oily hair
reviews.body:
This H&S Instant Oil Control is better than the last version of Citrus Breeze, but it is still not a great shampoo for fine/oily hair. For perspective, I have used Head and Shoulders almost my entire life. Most renditions have been pretty good. Occasionally there has been a particular product that I didn't care for. I do not like any added conditioners to fine/oily hair shampoos because folks with our type of hair don't need conditioners. But usually you could find ones without conditioners.

I really liked the original formulation of H&S Citrus Breeze. It left my hair feeling clean and kept dandruff at bay. However, the formulation changed with their "New Fresh Scent Technology" and that shampoo is worthless. You can lather, rinse, repeat until the cows come home and never get that squeaky clean feeling. I stocked up on the original Citrus Breeze but finally ran out. I have been alternating the new formula Citrus Breeze with Tresemme Deep Clean Shampoo, which leaves my hair feeling clean but dries my scalp out. With this new Instant Oil Control H&S, I hoped to get the right balance as before. Unfortunately, though it is a step in the right direction, it still does not provide the oil control that I require. After the second rinse, my hair feels fairly clean but not perfectly so. I still use the Tresemme about every 3rd day. If anyone reading this has found a great cleansing shampoo for fine/oily hair, please leave me a comment. Overall, this product is an improvement (and may be fine for those with only light oil issues), but it is not as good as some of H&S's earlier products.

reviews.title: Better than the old-fashioned kind. Cleans well, fairly pleasant scent, and does its job.
reviews.body:
It's been years since I've tried Head & Shoulders, but I figured I would give this variety a shot. My previous experiences tended to include an unpleasant scent, so-so cleaning, and either stringy or staticy hair (similar to various 2-in-1 shampoos), so the promise of a better smelling, better cleaning, and still effective version seemed appealing.

While I wasn't totally blown away, I liked the results. It seems effective and leaves hair clean and lightly conditioned without being too frizzy. The scent is also light enough that it doesn't linger too much. It did a good job of cleaning, though I found that washing/rinsing twice was still necessary to thoroughly remove extra oil and build-up of other products.

The bottle recommends using it at least twice a week, or as directed (as often as every day if desired). I probably wouldn't use it every day, but I think a couple or three times per week would work well, especially if using other products that are prone to leave build-up. I found that to be the case with another brand 2-in-1, so I might alternate with that.

Overall, I'd likely buy more, especially if I see it on sale. It has largely eliminated my old negative perceptions of Head & Shoulders, and anti-dandruff shampoos in general so I would recommend it to people who want some help controlling dandruff and oily hair without some of the typical drawbacks.

reviews.title: Use with Caution
reviews.body: I used this shampoo and the corresponding conditioner for 6 months. I have VERY oily skin/hair and needed something that would help manage it. At first, I loved it. It smelled great and made my hair feel super soft. I even noticed less oil build up in my hair. However, has time went on, I noticed my hair was appearing dull and dry AND just as oily. I believe 6 months of continuous oil removing is just too much for your hair. Your hair needs some oil to stay healthy. Since I was stripping so much oil, the shampoo caused my hair to dry out which then cause my scalp to produce more oil. This product is fine if you use it every once in a while to remove excess oil buildup. But, I do not recommend it for daily use.

reviews.title: Works well and smells refreshing! UPDATE ADDED
reviews.body:
This smells amazing and works VERY well at getting my hair super clean with just one wash and rinse, even after a sweaty workout. I have long hair and usually need to wash and rinse twice to get it clean after going to the gym or working in the yard; I have fine hair, but a lot of it, so it can become a tangly gross mess.

After one wash and rinse I noticed it felt smooth and clean and smelled great. I don't have dandruff but my husband does, it is so nice to have one shampoo we can both use without sacrificing manageability and silkiness. I have tried several of the new Head & Shoulders shampoos and I love what P&G has done to the brand! They feel and smell like good shampoo, not just a pasty chemical wash to rid your scalp of flakes like it used to be. You don't have to suffer through cruddy shampoo if you have dandruff.

I only need to condition the ends, since this shampoo really does get all the oil off your hair and scalp you may want to make sure you have a light conditioner to use on long hair to ease out the tangles. My hubby has oily hair too and his hair looks great but he needs no conditioner, I guess it is just needed if you have dry hair or if it is past your shoulders.

UPDATE: My toddlers and I were sick for more than a week. The showers we took did not include shampooing because of the cold weather and zero desire to blow-dry. After almost 10 days of no shampooing this amazing shampoo brought my hair back to perfectly clean with ONE cycle of wash and rinse. Zero grease or yuck left behind. Without conditioner my hair felt great too.

reviews.title: No better, and no worse than the original
reviews.body:
I've been using Head and Shoulders shampoos for about 25 years or so. I've tried several of their varieties and have to admit that they all work well at what they do, that is, they control dandruff and flakes, and they do it well. I would wish however that the marketing department would stop trying to promote fluff. That is to create additional versions just for the sake of creating them, or for getting a larger portion of the shampoo aisle, or to confuse the customers. This shampoo is no better than the classic, and no worse. It controls flakes and cleans hair just as well as the original one does, and thus, fills no need except to create confusion in the already crowded supermarket aisle.
Really, how many versions of the same product do we need?

reviews.title: Cooling sensation and great cleaning
reviews.body:
One of the best among head and shoulder shampoos.

Pros:
- Cooling feeling in the scalp (citrus cool)
- Cleans hair well
- Helps with dry scalp (not just dandruff)

Cons:
- The citrus means, it's extra harsh on your eyes. Definitely not kid friendly.

Overall, I recommend this to any adult. I don't have dandruff issues, but sometimes my scalp gets dry and this helps with it. The cooling feeling is nice (though not as strong as the "mint" shampoos if you've ever used those) and it gets the job done.

reviews.title: Clears up Dandruff: Delicate Smell
reviews.body:
I was surprised at how creamy this shampoo is and the small is refreshing. Some of the dandruff shampoos I've used are runny. This one stays in your hand and works into your hair and scalp very easily.

I don't usually have a problem with dandruff, but in the winter with forced air heating my hair and scalp get dried out. This shampoo takes care of the dandruff and my scalp feels really clean. I have long hair so to avoid tangles I do have to use a conditioner. My hair felt as silky as when I use other shampoos that are designed specifically to leave your hair smooth and silky.

I had avoided Head and Shoulders for years because the products available then smelled so medicinal. However, this shampoo is different. The smell is light and citrusy I will continue using it. I highly recommend it, particularly if you do have a problem with dandruff.

reviews.title: Weird Feeling
reviews.body:
My family has been using H&S products for years. It seems, however, that every couple of years H&S tries to re-invent itself. Now we have 'instant relief' shampoo.

At first, without reading the small print, I thought I would get 'instant relief' from my dandruff. Instead I got instant 'cooling' relief. I'm a bit confused about the cooling effect.

Does my dandruff really feel better about itself when cooled down a bit?

After a couple of showers my hair feel a bit flatter. Not like I have huge hair anyways.

The scent is okay. Not very manly. I doubt I'll use on my next hot date with Mrs. Wrong.

reviews.title: Smells Nice But Had No Effect
reviews.body:
We recently had a family member stay the night and I saw that she was using this shampoo. I felt like I’d might’ve tried this shampoo in the past and had simply added it to the endless list of things that make no difference.
I suffer from scalp psoriasis as well as an oily scalp. It’s been a very hard thing to balance. I’ve managed to go 10+ years with no winning product in sight. I had high hopes that my memory had served me incorrectly or at least that this had possibly been reformulated, when I purchased this at the store. However, I was left disappointed for probably the second time. It made absolutely no difference to the amount of oil in my hair (in fact, it actually looked worse than it does with the hydrating shampoo I was using before). It did not touch any of the itch or flakeage, either. I didn’t really expect it to help my psoriasis but that would’ve been a redeeming quality, at least. Sad to say that my journey for the winning product continues on.

reviews.title: It actually works!
reviews.body:
Head&shoulders provided me with a bottle of their Head&shoulders oil control 2in1 so that I could try and give me opinion.

I’ve been using it for quite a few weeks now and I can say that I’m impressed.

Let’s start with the basics:

Smell. Head&shoulders oil control 2 in 1 has a citrusy scent which is gentle and not over powering. You can still smell the medicinal ingredients but it’s not overbearing and doesn’t linger on the hair.

This shampoo is actually perfect for anyone with scent issues.

Consistency: Head&shoulders oil control 2 in 1 has a wonderful smooth consistency that lathers well and doesn’t require you to use too much of the product so it could last you longer. If you go a while between washings, I find that shaking the bottle helps a little but I’m not sure why.

Claims: Head&shoulders oil control 2 in 1 claims that it will help fight dandruff and oil as well as leave you feeling fresh and clean. It does. My scalp felt cool all day with less oil and itch.

If you’re looking for an inexpensive shampoo that helps with both dandruff and oil control look no further than Head&shoulders oil control 2 in 1. Definitely recommend and it’s readily available at Shoppers Drug Mart

reviews.title: By December BOTH of the bags were falling apart and we sent pictures of the faulty bags and Herschel acknowledged the faulty bag
reviews.body:
I purchased this bag for my son in July, another for my nephew in August.
By December BOTH of the bags were falling apart and we sent pictures of the faulty bags and Herschel acknowledged the faulty bags and would replace - IF WE SHOW EVIDENCE THAT WE HAVE RENDERED THE BAGS USELESS BY CUTTING THE STRAPS OFF AND SLICING THE BAG UP. That is the most ridiculous policy I have ever heard. What happened to reduce reuse recycle???? We have been inconvenienced twice and rather than just standing behind the product and sending replacements they basically want to ensure I don't make a second claim on the same bag. As if I would file a second claim. My receipt for both warranty claims would ensure I could not. I googled this on the internet and many people feel the same way I do.
SHAME ON HERSCHEL!! - Not only do they sell poor quality products but their policy is ridiculous.

reviews.title: Minor flaw in manufacturing but overall good
reviews.body:
Overall, this backpack fit well. It's definitely smaller than some previous backpacks I've owned, but it still fits everything I need for college (books/notebooks/etc. as well as a water bottle and laptop) so size is not a problem. It's also much more aesthetically pleasing than my previous backpacks, which have been Jansport (those were good for high school--held a lot but didn't have a laptop compartment).

Do be careful when purchasing a bag with a laptop sleeve; not all laptop backpacks can fit all sizes of laptops. I was looking both here on Amazon and on eBags while shopping for mine; eBags has a wonderful little tool on the product page of each laptop-carrying bag in which you can input your laptop model and be told whether or not the laptop and the bag are compatible.

The rectangular Herschel logo was poorly attached to the main fabric of the backpack, though. It was only partly stitched on when I removed the backpack from its packaging and was pulled off easily by a couple tugs at the stitching. I haven't experienced any problems with the rest of the backpack, though. Other than the cosmetic glitch just mentioned, it functions beautifully.

reviews.title: Great college bag
reviews.body: I use this to lug my crap around campus 3 days a week, and then for various other activities that require a zip-up backpack, like going to the beach. Needless to say, my bags see some abuse. They get thrown in the car, dragged on the floor, spilled on at lunch, and crammed with junk. I have never had a problem with any ripped pockets or straps, busted zippers, or holes after a year of use. I appreciate the reflective zipper tape on the front pocket and the little bit on one of the shoulder straps, especially as I got a black backpack, making it otherwise difficult to find in the dark. The padded laptop sleeve is great, and with a computer/charger/mouse in the main compartment, there is still enough room for two 1" binders, a handful of folders, a pencil case, a skinny Hydroflask, and some snacks. I really like the organizational pockets as well, and the pocket for my sunnies on top, which I use often. This backpack is slim-looking on the outside, has not faded in the year I've had it, and is comfortable to wear as well.
