reviews.title: The bag is too deep and there are no small pockets for storing easily accessible items (such as keys
reviews.body: I truly regret spending money on this backpack. It is bulky. And not at all convenient. It somehow manages to be large and yet store very little. I can carry more in canvas tote bags. The only positive is the straps are padded which adds comfort and weight is distributed evenly. The bag is too deep and there are no small pockets for storing easily accessible items (such as keys, wallet, etc.) the pocket on the outside can't hold much more than a tube of chap stick or a card. Not really functional for a city dweller. And I took it on a travel/hiking trip and it was challenging that way too as you had to pack everything on top on itself, though it again doesn't hold much. It has the padded laptop sleeve, but easily gets bent into the body of the bag. I don't understand why it has a compartment for a laptop as nothing else about this seems to be designed for city life.

reviews.title: Pink Lemonade and Unicorn Tendons?
reviews.body:
First of all, I'l admit that purchasing this bag was a fluke. There. I said it. The two things that made me choose this bag were the nifty mesh holders on the side that are so happy to hold water bottles, and…the price. I had been shopping for a new backpack for quite some time (I ordered one from Roxy and the colors are way off. Not to mention it's made of cheap nylon and lies.) and I knew that the only feature I had to have was the side holders. So I stumbled upon this backpack while surfing the web during my anatomy class (I also got a 95% on the quiz so don't judge me). Not only did it have my necessary water bottle holders, but it had a laptop sleeve and a couple of cute patterns available. I selected Butterflies/Pink Lemonade and placed my order.

When the backpack arrived, I opened the box to a flood of heavenly light and a hallelujah chorus. The colors are even brighter and more attractive than in the picture. And I like attractive backpacks. But beauty is not the only reason I love this bag, so don't think I'm shallow.

First, OH MY GOODNESS THE ROOM IN THIS BAG. My first day toting it to class, I carried my laptop, a binder, a textbook, some chapstick, several writing utensils, a water bottle, a compass, a fire starting kit, two MREs, an extra pair of shoes, my car keys, a handheld radio, and a kitten.
Okay, so maybe I didn't ACTUALLY have all these things in the bag. But believe you me, they could definitely all fit. I'm actually suspicious that this bag may be one of the doors to Narnia. Last time I tried the zipper got stuck in my hair, so you may want to oil yourself up before you go jumping into it.

The bag also features a nifty handle at the top, so you don't have to carry it around by the straps if it's not on your back. It's also useful if you need to hang it on the horns of your dragon if you're flying to class and you're late. Just make sure that you tell your trusty steed first, because he may or may not rear up and squish your neighbor's house with his tail. And then of course you're a fugitive and you don't get to show off your new backpack. Nobody wants that.

Once, when I was little, my mother made a scavenger hunt for me on a friend's farm. I'm glad I have that experience under my belt, because I'm fairly certain there is more acreage inside this pack than on that farm. There are zippers and pockets galore. The pockets have pockets. And those pockets have dividers, which is basically like having pockets. Pocketception. My favorite pocket is the small, cloth section that is the third zipper on the bag. It's the perfect place for eyeglasses, car keys, or the hearts of the enemies you banish on the way to wherever it is you go.

Have you ever had the pleasure of petting a rhinoceros? No? Neither have I. But my cousin knows a rhino personally and he said that the George (isn't that a cute name for a rhino?) often wears High Sierra Swerve Backpacks as fashionable body armor. According to George, he has survived a shotgun blast, a butcher knife, another rhino's horns, and napalm, all due to this high-strength nylon. Or maybe it isn't nylon. Maybe it's dragon hide, and that's the real reason your dragon might freak out if your bag is swinging from his face. It could be his aunt Linda. He never really liked her anyway, but being made into a super stylish backpack isn't a proper burial.

Straps. Let's talk about these straps. I'm not one to point fingers, but someone at High Sierra is either practicing an advanced level of sorcery, or is harvesting the tendons out of unicorns for the Suspension Strap System. You can load this bag up, and in between the time that you close the zipper and the time that you swing the bag up on your shoulder, about 50% of the weight will disappear. And I kid you not. This is literally the most comfortable bag I have ever carried. Which makes it tough to decide if I'm upset about the unicorn slaughter or not. I mean they're cute but heavens to mergatroid, this pack is comfortable! It's like wearing a dragonskin bag full of helium and stuffed with the down of the goose that laid a golden egg. Only better.

I've only had this bag for one week, so I will return and write more about how well it holds up to my adventures. Unless of course, I die in the heat of battle fighting the forces of evil for the freedom of the world. In which case, I love you, Mom and Dad.

reviews.title: It looks like the company has tried to modify the zipper design
reviews.body: While I read many reviews of this pack before purchasing, I found a common theme, which was complaints about the zippers.  After using it for a week on a daily basis, I now get it.  There are several openings, and only have ongoing issues with the main top zipper.  It looks like the company has tried to modify the zipper design, probably due to complaints, but it's still an issue.  The top zipper is just kind of difficult to work.  Due to it's positioning and the curvature of the top of the bag, you really have to apply opposite pressure (pulling the material tight), for the zipper to slide as expected.  But if you remove the somewhat required two-hand zipper operation for the top zipper, this bag is an excellent buy.  Fairly lightweight, very durable, excellent straps, and plenty of space with many pocket options.

there's a small comp, on it i store my plastic glass cases. easy in/out

reviews.title: Best Bag Ever
reviews.body:
I am a connoisseur of backpacks. I am VERY picky about my backpacks and it takes me forever to pick one out and then adjust to it. I've used a lot of different kinds and a lot of different brands and styles. I had never tried High Sierra before, but this backpack looked decent for the price so I decided to try it out.

I recently started college after a 5 year break to start a family. This backpack is big enough to carry my college books and notebooks. I love that the pen-holder pocket has a built in organizer - it's got several little zippered pockets within the organizer too - perfect to hold staplers, white-out, index cards, etc. My planner fits in there perfectly. I like that this pocket opens up ALL THE WAY - it makes your junk easy to access. My favorite part is the key-ring attachment. It has a buckle so you put the buckle part on your key-ring, and then you can attach your keys inside the backpack so you don't have to hunt for them as you're freezing in the snow. Perfect!

There is a soft zippered compartment on the top of the backpack in between the largest section and the middle section which is perfect for holding earbuds, phones, MP3 players, and I put my wallet in there too. It's nice because it's pretty well camouflaged in the backpack which makes your stuff harder to steal.

The straps are extremely comfortable and the bag is very lightweight. This is probably the most comfortable bag I've ever used. The fabric seems very durable and heavy-duty. I like that it has 2 bottle holders - one for my water, one for my Diet Coke!

One of the big pockets has a very small zipper opening, which I think is kinda dumb. It's still useful, but only for smaller books. The bag also smelled REALLY BAD when I first got it. I put some of those fabric softener pellets in it and it cleared up the scent after a few hours but it was really stinky. I also don't really care for the separate laptop compartment and wish it was detachable, but I don't carry my laptop with me anyway.

Some backpacks are really big, which can sometimes be a pain as it gets more difficult to pull your stuff out with the fabric folding in on itself. This backpack is the perfect size and the fabric is thick enough that it doesn't flop all over itself.

Overall, I LOVE this bag. It's sturdy, comfortable, and bright and cheerful (I have a color not listed here.) It's different than the 9,000 other bags on campus. It's the perfect size for all my junk and I love all the separate compartments to keep everything organized. I foresee it lasting for most of my college career, definitely.

I used to be a fan of only JanSport bags. This bag pwns my JanSport by about 1,000 points. All hail High Sierra!

reviews.body: I ordered this backpack while studying abroad in Spain for a semester, and I needed it for a two-week trip.  It arrived in 2 days, and I was really impressed by both the quick delivery and the great quality.  It had the perfect number of pockets and expandable space to carry everything I needed for two weeks, and the straps were strong and cushion-y.  The outer material was durable and waterproof.  The support system in the straps made it easy to carry a good 26lb of food, clothing, and other necessary things (quick-dry towel, toiletries, contacts, water bottle, umbrella, hand sanitizer, tissues, etc.) without the backpack feeling too heavy.  It traveled through Rome, London, Paris, Lisieux, Lourdes, Hungary, Spain, and Ireland with me, fitting perfectly into the "Ryanair size checkers" even when stuffed.  I highly recommend the High Sierra Swerve pack to anyone looking for a durable companion!  Thank you Amazon for your quick and reliable service!!!

reviews.title: ALMOST perfect backpack..
reviews.body:
When I got this backpack I LOVED it! It's cool looking, has suspension things on the straps to lessen the loads of college, nicely padded, and has tons of room! So what's not to like? Two MAJOR things.

One-
It's extremely difficult to zip/unzip. For whatever reason there's just too much material too close to EVERY zipper! You can still zip/unzip but it's unnecessarily difficult to do since they get caught every inch or so every single freaking time! You'd think that would be something such an "advanced" backpack wouldn't have a problem with but it certainly does and it sucks. Very annoying to be reminded of the zippers' suckiness every time I have to zip/unzip.

Two-
The reinforcement material used to hold the backpack together better is a little over-kill. This backpack WILL eventually ruin the backs of all your shirts, sweatshirts, jackets, etc because the edges of the reinforcing material juts out too far and constantly rubs against your back. Again, not something you should have to deal with every single day, every single class. C'mon Sierra!! You're so close to having the best backpack around! Until these problems are addressed, I'd stay away.

reviews.title: Not Very Durable - Didn't Last One Year
reviews.body:
Bought 2 pair of these on November 8, 2017. Xmas gifts for my two Boys so they actually started using them on December 25th, 2017. SHORT LIVED! One pair was used for a PS4 (8th grader) and the other pair on an Xbox One (7th grader). Both pairs now have sound only in one ear unless you wiggle the end of the cable that connect to the controller. After wiggling cable, you will get audio in both ears just for a short moment and then back to one ear of sound. While the headsets are very comfortable and sound good for $60, I would recommend buying the Cloud Alpha ($40 more dollars) which has the replaceable cable. Kingston does warranty the headsets for 2 years so I am in the process of getting replacement sets. Kingston Customer support was good and above average. Once I stated that I tested both headsets on my phone with the same results, The Kingston Rep processed a RMA for me. I requested a prepaid return shipping label so I will see if they do that or not...They should since they are still under warranty. Kingston stated that the replacement sets will be brand new and not a refurb. I will try and update this review when the whole process is complete.
Update...Kingston approved replacement headsets after uploading receipt from Amazon , but shipping will be out of my pocket. Very upset about this! Last Kingston purchase I will ever make. Will try and comment again once all said and done :(
9/14/18 - Dropped off pkg at USPS to return defective 2 pair of headsets. Cheapest shipping option (USPS Retail Ground) with $120 insurance and tracking cost me $24.87. Priority 2 day s&h would have cost almost double. More to come.
Update...Received replacement headsets on 10/1/18. Replacement sets were new and not a refurb as Kingston stated. Both units have been tested and are 100% functional. Make sure to save all of your packaging and in the event you have to send them to Kingston, be sure to include the cable that connects them to the PC as well. Hope this review helpful to Someone.

reviews.title: Very disappointed
reviews.body:
I have been using the HyperX Cloud Core for the PS4 and I have been very underwhelmed. I want to start with the cons because there are more cons than pros. My first major gripe is because of its stronger aluminum frame the headset constantly feels like it is squeezing your head as you wear it for anytime longer than 2 hours. The top pad also feels like it it putting slight constant pressure on your head. I have had cheaper headsets that are more comfortable. The second thing that annoys me is there is no inline controls for volume and no way to mute your mic without unplugging it. I have children at home who can throw tantrums at times and I dont need to share that with my party or randos I am playing a game with. Also, when it gets late at night and you dont want max exposure to volume you have to open the mic settings via the PS4 because you cant control it with the headset itself. 3rd the 3.5mm jack which makes it compatible with the PS4 is a straight jack instead of it pointing downwards away from you which shoves the cord into your lap and can interfere with your hands at times causing the cord to contort in strange ways at times. I find these things unacceptable since much cheaper headsets have some or all of these features.

Another thing I dont care for is the leather-like material on the earmuffs. I must admit it is pretty effective at blocking out surrounding sounds but can get pretty warm. I also have a preference to hear a bit of my surroundings since I like to be able to pay attention to my surroundings back in real life but I wont dock them for that since it is just a personal preference. Another personal preference is that the headset isnt loud enough for me. At times I would really like it to be louder but alot of headsets have this problem to me so again I wont hold it against them but since this one costs more I was expecting more volume. Also the idea of a detachable mic is a mixed bag. “Hey Im not using the mic so I can unplug it and get it out of my sight and away from my mouth... BUUUT at the same time every-time I unplug it I risk it being lost forever.” Overall, I prefer having a fixed mic.

The nice things about the headset is since they are aluminum, theoretically they shouldnt break or snap around the head band region although I am concerned with the jack since it is a straight jack and I suspect that is this headsets weak spot. The headset looks nice and has a bit more style than your lower ends headsets. The thing I like the most about the headset is the sound quality. These arent going to show ranges and clarity like a high end set of headphones but for gaming these are well above average. The sounds are clear. Directions are easy to decipher, tones and tenors are sharper, basses are pretty comparable to most (since most headsets focus on bass) and overall the sound quality is much higher than your entry level headsets.

So these are not a bad set of gaming headsets, but for the mid level price I have had better headsets that are much cheaper with better options with slightly reduced sound quality. I would personally reccomend the PS4 Afterglow 6 which has much better options, less outside sound reduction, much more comfortable but a cheaper plastic frame which will break over time. However I have my suspicions the HyperX Cloud Core is not invincible either and will find a way to break in a different way. The AG6 is half the price of the HyperX Cloud Core so if it only has half the longevity of the Cloud Core you could buy a second one and still pay less.

The microphone pop filter is very slanted and the microphone is very quiet. What happened with the pop filter facing towards the one side is it came like that when it shipped. The microphone got very quiet after about 2 days. I sneezed it to it and since then it has been very quiet and annoying. I've been using this in discord and I would get complaints saying, "Raise your microphone!" Which I did seeing in the second picture. If you are having problems with the static in the microphone, I would suggest lowering the DB all of the way. That can cause a very distorted/static microphone. Also if this is possible, would you guys be willing to send a new microphone? I overall love the product, but the microphone is fairly annoying having to hear complaints by various users.

reviews.title: Great FPS headset
reviews.body: Very happy.  About 10 years ago I was a semi-professional PC gamer.  Traveled to many tournaments and played competition at the highest levels in N.A.  Age, life, work, maturity, and the fact that I was never good enough to go "fully pro," I moved on.  However, at 33 I still find the time to play CS:GO a few hours a week, along with the occasional BF4 or Rust gaming.  I've been using some $20 Walmart headset for the past 4 years, and to be honest completely forgot what it's like to have a quality headset.  The directional sound is a godsend in FPS games.  I used to have to turn my character in-game frequently with my crappy headphones to determine the location of noises, gunfire, or footsteps.  No more.  These are great cans.  Highly recommend, especially if you can get them on a $50 sale like I did.

reviews.title: Great bang for buck gaming headset.
reviews.body: These are actually not that bad for what you pay for them, they are very uncomfortable for the first gaming session, your ears get incredibly hot and sweaty but the second use and beyond it breaks in and is great. The detachable mic (Which by the way is quite decent at it's price point) was the biggest selling point for me on account of being able to replace it for less than it would cost to get a whole new headset. The braided cable is also wonderful and I am never paranoid if the cable will end up getting torn if accidentally rolled over by my chair or slammed in my desk. The headphone sound itself however is only good for gaming, it is not to good on audio but maybe that is because I own Hi-Fi headphones (I.e Ath mx40s and Sennheiser HD 800 S). However, even though this are a great bang for buck gaming headset, I ended up returning these because I bought a desktop mic stand and a refurbed at2020 and interface for only 40 dollars since I already have really good headphones.

reviews.title: Great Headset
reviews.body:
Honestly did expect much out of this headset, it's on the cheaper end, so I was expecting cheaper materials.

The inner frame is metal and the cups themselves have a metal shell as well, the ear pads seem sturdy (been using for 3 months so can't actually tell yet). The mic is a simple plug in mic that can be removed to just use the headset.

Sound quality is great, but don't expect audiophile sound out of these. They are loud enough and isolating enough that it makes you feel like you are in the game though. Maybe the best part of these headphones is how great the mic is; it isolates sound around you so that only your voice can be heard, and very clear at that.

Overall: can't beat these headphones for the price.

reviews.title: Illy is actually my favorite (Italian point of view)
reviews.body:
Never have I ever drank a better coffee than illy in my life. In Milan I tried the coffee in an official illy bar and the taste of their espresso was insanely good. Their moka blend is also exquisite, but all of illy’s coffee need expensive coffee machines (create high pressure) to truly bring out the flavor, so I actually do NOT recommend this coffee to regular coffee consumers.
Also a common misconception to those struggling with the packaging: the coffee comes sealed in a can, similar to a can of beans, to retain freshness, so as soon as you open it, you won’t be able to close it back in the same packaging. I personally use mason jars which seals the coffee air tight, which helps the grind coffee stay fresh and aromatic. This coffee is really expensive (nearly double the price to your average coffee), so unless you have a decent espresso maker, I would not buy illy.

reviews.title: Deceiving with "passive noise cancellation"; otherwise OK
reviews.body:
"Passive noise cancellation" is same as "can be used to hold a door if you put it on the floor". Marketing seems to me, deceiving. "Passive" means it covers your ear.
I purchased an Evolve 30, dual (not through Amazon, but this is a good forum to review as I am searching for replacement).
Unhappy with what is a clear misguiding of consumers. In all the marketing in their website they refer to "The Jabra Evolve series helps you create your own concentration zone with premium active and passive noise cancellation technology", they leave it to consumer to "realize" where it is not true.
While it becomes clear that when you go deep in the comparison charts that the 20, 30, 40, 65, 65t (at least) do not have "active noise cancellation" they also do not confirm which models do have some form of "active noise cancellation" (at microphone level) I called Jabra and they would not confirm. Also no confirmation if it is the little base that manages it or if it requires the Jabra software.
If you do not care about picking up background noise while having a call (or use for speech recognition), then they are good, comfortable. Microphone turns off when you rise it (good). Plugs in and sets up easily.
The 30 headset (compared to the 20) allows for using the headset on 3.5mm BUT you can't connect any 3.5mm to this the base it comes with. The plug-in USB dongle is designed to only be used with the Jabra headset via a modified 3.5mm plug length/shape (making it "proprietary").
Active Noise Cancellation, only in 75 (and other higher models) but then you are comparing to other high quality brands that are more forward in their advertising, for same or even lower price.
Thus, will buy another headset that clearly states this features.

reviews.title: Great office or home office headset without breaking the bank
reviews.body:
I was demo'ing headset for work. We needed to by price conscience within reason, and seemed to be limited to a few brands. Tried this Jabra Evolve 30 II. Like them, so recommended them to the powers-at-be. Now our department of 100+ each is using them. I work from home often, so ended up getting myself a 2nd pair to use at home.

That pair, had a small piece snap where the speaker swivels. It was out of warranty, so out of luck. But I still went back and purchased the same pair. They just work. Well.

Pros:
- usb connector or 3.5mm connector
- can be used as headset plugged into mobile phone
- while not TOP gaming quality, I've used them as gaming headset on a PlayStation4
- comes with neoprene case
- they look professional
- inline mute/volume control
- Allows some ambient noise (a good thing), 100% noise cancelling then you cannot hear anything around you (not a good thing)
- price

Cons:
- warranty length
- pin that hold earpiece/speaker and swivels could be stronger

I have recommended these (100+ strong in my department). I bought them twice from home. I'd buy them again.

Each are very lightweight, portable and easy to maintain. I can hold all of my stuff in each of them. I think both would make for a great gift. I can see this being part of a gift basket for someone!

I was not compensated in any way for my review on this product. I like to give open, honest and transparent feedback on products I like to try. I hope you found this review to be helpful. If so, please click the 'Helpful' button to let myself and others know that it has helped you.

I have been on the lookout for a backpack purse that isn't girly, blingy, or tacky - and my options were very slim. When I found this on Amazon I was excited! I purchased it in black and it is perfect. It's small enough and it has plenty of room. I usually keep a planner, small notebook, my huge Galaxy 5S, wallet, keys, and a bunch of randoms. It's very versatile and I've been getting compliments on it!
UPDATE:
After using this as a purse for a few months, I've noticed a few things that are slightly bothersome. The straps aren't padded, which does provide discomfort if you pack the bag. Secondly, I think there should be some padding on the inside whereally it lies on your back. It you carry a bunch of small things in it, which are all going to be smaller than a foot long because of the bag's size, they will shift to the front of the bag when you have it on, causing an awkward gap between the bag and your back. reviews.title: Simple yet Sturdy
reviews.body:
This backpack has lasted me for over 2 years now, and I have not had a single problem with it. Zippers are still working perfectly, and straps are still as comfortable as they'll ever be. It's a perfect backpack for college and beyond.

Now, I don't toss and drag my backpacks across asphalt and concrete (like I used to in elementary school :P), but I have stuffed this bag many times with textbooks, paperwork, clothes, etc, until the seams seemed (hah!) like they were going to burst. Much to my satisfaction, the bag still held strong each and every time.

Only issue I have with this bag is that it's almost too commonly used! So make sure you personalize your backpack before you accidentally switch it with someone else!

reviews.title: Careful with that zipper, Eugene
reviews.body:
Durable as all heck, made of the same “I’m not sure what this fabric is but it’s tough as nails” material Jansports have had since the dawn of time. Neato.

The only issue is the little flap of fabric meant to cover the zipper “track” has a tendency to slide into the zipper and mess up your whole backpacky world if you’re not super careful about it.

And you know who aren’t careful? Children. You give this bag to a child and they will zip that flap into the track in five minutes flat.

I bet if you left this bag with a child, unattended, for a long enough period of time… He/she would inadvertently send the bag to some alternate dimension by zipping the zipper into another zipper made of zipping zippers. It would be like dividing by zero.

reviews.title: Uncomfortable
reviews.body: I got this to replace a worn old L.L. Bean bag. I chose it because I loved the color and because Jansport has a good reputation. Unfortunately, within ten minutes of trying it out, I knew I had to return it. (And I never return things). The straps were extremely uncomfortable. Even with nothing in the backpack, they were noticeably less comfortable than my old bag's straps, and with a heavy book in the bag, they were downright painful. I didn't realize how much I rely on a curved strap for weight distribution when carrying heavy loads. This bag's straps are straight, padded but narrow, and not smartly placed. There is also no padding along the back, so if you are carrying anything hard or pointed (like a book), you can feel every pokey corner. There was no reinforcement in the bottom, and the material felt thin and flimsy. I'm doubtful this bag would stand up to much hard use. I returned this and got a North Face Vault, which I'm happy with.

reviews.title: Better than Sony buds
reviews.body:
I love the sound quality of my cheap 9.99 sony buds more than any $100-199 pair that I've ever tried. But the sony buds break in two seconds. I didn't care because the sound quality was just so good and they are so cheap. At some point though, it became ridiculous how often I had to replace them. Sometimes once a month with barely any use. Then if I didn't have a spare pair, I had to go all night/day without my headphones because I can't stand when the sound goes out in only one bud. These JBL buds are just as good, maybe better, on sound quality. They are not made of the cheap plastic that sonys are, seem much sturdier and higher quality. I'm impressed with how well the buds stay in my ears as well. That was another design flaw with the sony buds where they would fall out just a bit after some wear time and I would have to constantly push them back in to get the sound I wanted. If these last, they are my new go-to.

UPDATE: I sent them back twice, both had an earbud go out in under a month. Useless.

reviews.title: Good for small ears

Most in-ear headphones are too big for me to get a fit snug enough to keep them in place while running.  The smallest covers for these JBL headphones are a great fit for my small ears and these headphones are not budging during a run.  I have been shocked at how secure they are despite not having any other mechanism to secure them to the ear (and I'm wearing them in a straight configuration, not looping the wire over my ear which doesn't actually seem to make much of a difference).  The noise cancellation properties are very good and the sound quality is also pretty good.  I wouldn't hesitate to recommend these to fellow women runners with small ear canals.

reviews.title: Better than I thought they might be
reviews.body:
Wanted to replace an old pair of wired ear-buds I have been using. I do a lot of walking outside and like to listen to audiobooks, podcasts, and music while doing that. I prefer using wired earbuds - as they tend to have control buttons that I can use without taking the headphones off.

Looked at several brands of these and picked these JBL ones because they looked to have earpieces that might actually fit in my ears and stay - plus, they were pretty inexpensive. I was really impressed at the packaging these came in - something I would more imagine for a more expensive product. The earbuds are pretty nice too. They fit my ears well, and you get some of the silicone pieces in different sizes. The ones that came one the earbuds fit me perfectly. The sound quality is good - course I'm mainly listening to audiobooks - but the few times I've listened to music I wasn't disappointed. The silicone earpieces do muffle outside sounds - but not totally. The control button works well.

If I were to have a complaint - it would be that you don't get a case/bag to store the earbuds in when not in use. Something simple as a small nylon bag would have been nice. Maybe cut back on spending so much money on the product packaging - which gets thrown out and instead include a bag/case. But other than that - I'm happy with the new earbuds and with my purchase.

reviews.title: Awesome sweatproof sound at a bargain price!!
reviews.body: I have purchased professional earbuds costing hundreds of dollars but don't want to wear them during workouts and rain.  It's so hard to find simple (old-school) earbuds that simply plug into a player - no wireless, no phone, no Bluetooth, just great simple plug and enjoy sound.  I also do not like all of the extra "framework", the wrap-around your ear, the extra "wings" to secure the earpiece - just a simple earbud.  I read all the reviews and bought 3 different sweat-proof, water resistant simple earbuds, then tried them back to back.  I was IMMEDIATELY IMPRESSED with these.  The sound was immediately superior to the others and even comparable to my pros.  Though I was weary of the additional fit-in-your-ear attachment, they fit perfectly and never moved -  even in the high wind of high speed cycling.  It's hard to gauge reviews but if you've read this far, you WILL NOT BE DISAPPOINTED WITH THESE!  I gave the other two away and bought another pair of these.  P.S.  the earbuds stick together with magnets - which is definitely gimmicky - until you see that it's a nice feature.

reviews.title: Best headphones for the gym!
reviews.body:
I used to have Beats Solo and the JBL Tune 510BT give them a run for their money.

Every Youtube review has raved on the sound, and I agree. I listen to a lot of 90’s R&B and the quality is amazing. It reminds me of Sony MDRv150s out of box.

Out of the box, the fit and comfort feels super cheap. It reminds me of Sony ZX110s or MDR-V150. But if you replace the ear pads with memory foam replacements, they almost feel like Beats Solos. They have great noise isolation (not to be confused with noise canceling).

I got mine for $30 at a Ross, and they’ve been my daily driver for the gym. I love them.

If I were to nitpick, however, the location of the charging port is annoying. It’s hidden until you fold the cans. There’s no aux port, so these would make terrible travel headphones. It’s purely bluetooth. Also, the noise that I get, when the volume is too high, tends to sound off when I’m idle.

Otherwise, they’re solid gym headphones, especially if you’re not trying to pay more than $50 for quality sound and headphones you’re eventually going to break.

reviews.title: Best of everything including price
reviews.body: I've owned a few brand name wireless headphones over the years. Since my new phone had no audio jack, I was faced with the decision to find a in-ear and over the ear headphone that didn't feel uncomfortable and sounded great without breaking the bank. I own Sonys silver then gold edition headphones, but the pain after an hour was too much. I felt like my head was being crushed. I tried other brands as well, but they either didn't sound good or fit right. Having owned many JBL products, and knowing their awesome sound I gave these a try. Freaking amazing is an understatement!! I listen to hours of YouTube content every night, and I find myself falling asleep often as these are so comfortable. The charge on my BT-510's will last more than a week on average, and are fully charged in an hour. At first I thought the price was too low compared to other brand names of equal or better quality, and these would not last or sound as good but I was wrong. Good job JBL. Another satisfied customer.

reviews.title: Review from an adult with a small head

I am an a petite adult with a smaller head (I often wear kid sized glasses). These fit on the smallest setting but just barely. If I wear them to the gym they stay on, but if I were to shake my head vigorously they would fall off.

In short, I LOVE these headphones. They are super comfortable, with great sound quality for what I use them for (podcasts, music and calls at work and home) I wear these all day with my glasses, and my ears never hurt. Battery life is exceptional. I think I get about 6-7 hours most days for a week before I need to recharge. I'm back to buy a wired pair for use with my digital piano.

Yes, Yes and Yes! I found ALL the above with these headphones. I have wireless Bluetooth earbuds I often use for long runs where I sweat a ton, and on-ear wireless headphones just don't make sense for me on long runs. I use these for lifting weights, doing laptop work, Zoom calls, work calls where I need my hands, etc. They have worked out great! I will say, the material used to cover the ear pieces is on the low-quality side and I would not suggest these for use where they are exposed to sweat for long periods of time (1+ hours) because I think the material on the ear pieces will deteriorate faster as they don't appear to be made to holdup against too much moisture and wetness. Overall, above average product for the price.

reviews.title: making getting them on my feet down right painful. Driving is not possible because you cannot move ...
reviews.body:
The only thing this shoe does right is keep the water off your feet.

If you plan to get your foot in this boot without physical exertion, size up. If you plan to wear socks, size up more. I was unable to return these, but I would have in a heart beat if I could have. Despite having these for a year, the rubber still has no give, making getting them on my feet down right painful. Driving is not possible because you cannot move your foot at all. Wearing them for more than a few hours will make your legs sore because you constantly have to flex your foot.

The major issue I have with these is the fact that they are not made with a woman's body in mind. Unless you have very small calves, you'll have trouble getting them on. I'm 5'4", take a size small shirt, and a size 4 in pants. My point is, I'm not a very big person. Not super skinny, but not overweight either. I run, so my calf muscle are slightly bigger than average. I don't typically need a wide calf boot. These boots are a struggle to get on, though. For someone who would normally need a wide calf boot, they would be impossible to get on. It's frustrating to see this blatant disregard for diversity in sizing. I would not recommend.

reviews.body: Love these! Finally got a chance to wear them. My feet are warm, cozy and dry! I'm tall and have slender to athletic legs and these fit perfectly. If you have calves on the larger side, you might want to go with another style. I'm 5'9" and the top of these come about 2 finger widths from my tibial tuberosity (the bump below the kneecap). I love that they are taller than most rain boots. The grey is a perfect shade and I'd love to have these in other colors as well. :)

reviews.title: Very snug shaft
reviews.body:
First I have to say, I am more than happy with the quality and appearance of these boots, in fact I would actually use the phrase "I love them" EXCEPT that the shaft (calf portion) is toooooooooo snug! I'm not a skinny girl but I am definitely not a large girl either. These fit very tight, to the point there is no way I could dream of tucking jeans in them or wear those cute boot cuffs that are so popular now. They are so tight they make a seal around my leg as well and I'm not sure if that will annoy me later on. I agree with other reviewers that these boots are also very difficult to remove, simply because they are tall and tight. Its managable though. As most fashion decisions go, style can sometimes over ride comfort and does for this purchase as well. They coordinate with a new coat I purchased and will make a cute and sassy outfit on stormy days!

Another note as to quality: when looking at them online I couldn't tell what the crest was made of or if the buckle at the top was functional or decorative. The crest is really nice! It is some kind of metal and is actually stitched on, not glue that will eventually pop off. The buckle is purely decorative though, but trust me, few would ever need to tighten these boots! Its a nice metal buckle with the Kamik name stamped on them. The construction around the foot is nicely made and the sole has a good amount of texture that they would probably not be slippery when wet. The heal height is nice, maybe 3/4" to 1" in height and comfortable. The boot is actually quite comfortable with the exception of the shaft. If it had been another inch in circumference larger these boots would be AMAZING. Which is why I gave them 4 stars rather than 5. I think the shoe portion is pretty true to size as well and I have enough room to fit an insole or orthodic inside if necessary. As it is they are darn cute boots!!

I ended up purchasing these boots last minute before heading out of town. When they arrived I was so excited! They felt comfortable, Snug, but not too snug. I Love them. reviews.title: These Run Small

Had to return the 9's and get a size 10 which fit perfect with socks.  They don't look big on my foot which I was worried about.  The calf size is perfect, not too big and not to small. reviews.title: Love these rain boots!
reviews.body: Very impressed w/ the quality of these rain boots for the price! They are very comfortable & cute, they also seem fairly durable.

reviews.title: How did I live without these before?!
reviews.body: I read the other reviews and was hesitant but could not get over how cool these looked.  I do have a narrow foot but I do not have small calves (maybe 15.5 inches?).  I went ahead and ordered my size, 6, and they are a perfect fit.  If I would wear really thick socks, I think my toes would reach the end of the boot but it's worth it to me to wear a thinner sock and have them fit perfectly everywhere else.  Yes, they are a tiny bit hard to get off but who cares when they look so stylish?  If boots are easy to kick off, they will be big a bulky and that is not what I was looking for.  I read that other people have problems with these rubbing their ankles.  I can wear them for 14+ hours a day with no pain at all.  The is a cushony insole and they are much lighter weight than I expect, yet very durable.  I love the emblem on the sides - adds a little more style to an already super cute boot.

I guess from taking them off with the help of my other foot? Not visible to others but I would imagine the rest of the boot could scuff fairly easily as well. As far as everyone complaining about the size, I disagree. I wear an 8.5, ordered a 9 and they fit great. However, I also measured my foot and checked it in the provided sizing chart first... May not be best for larger calved ladies, but I'm not positive. And as for the complaints about stuff rubber... They need to be broken in, as all quality boots do. I wore them around the house for an hour or so when I got them and they became increasingly more comfortable quickly. When I wore them out of the house, I had no problems and no leakage, and this was during the weekend of the epic South Carolina flooding. (That's obviously where I live)

reviews.title: A little big but kept my feet dry and warm!
reviews.body:
I have never owned a pair of weather-proof boots, as I live in very temperate climates. However, I would be traveling to Northern Europe and NYC during the winter. I wanted something comfortable enough to walk in, would keep my feet dry and warm, and would be relatively stylish.

I wore these suckers with some legging pants the time I spent traveling. I found that they are fine in rain and snow but can be slippery on things like hardwood. If you don't have extra cushion around the mouth of the boot, it may make a sound as the back of the boot hits your calf.

I wear a 7.5 and rounded a size up. I think it was a little roomy in the foot, but good for my skinnier calves. Also, these are like those jackets that don't breathe. While your foot doesn't get wet from the outside, it may let your feet...marinate... in sweat in warm climates. Sorry to be graphic!

Overall, it was a nice boot at a great price point. I like them and will keep them around for those special days. Meanwhile, the box they came in was beat up!

reviews.title: Love these boots!
reviews.body:
I bought these boots when I was working at an animal shelter. They needed to be 100% waterproof as I was dealing with some big messes and a power washer for half the day. The first few weeks they did hurt my ankles and calves (I wore scrub pants to work, they are very thin) but this went away as my feet got used to them. I did buy some taller socks, which I would recommend if you plan to wear these with thin pants or leggings. I used to power wash these to clean them at work, and I would also spray them with bleach and let them soak for a few hours if I ever had to take them home with me. Still look perfect!

Love these, even after I left the shelter, I still wear them daily to walk my dogs. Even after having these boots almost a year, I was able to walk into the river the other day (the easiest way to clean stuff off them, haha) and they didn't leak at all! And, you don't have to worry too much about what your are stepping into as you can clean these really easily.

The price has gone up since I bought them, but I still think they are totally worth it, especially after wearing uncomfortable boots for so long. I would buy these 10 more times!

reviews.title: Better than Hunter!

reviews.title: so far, awesome boots!
reviews.body:
I have been looking for a new pair of wellies since my old pair started leaking. I was about to bite the bullet and just order some hunters since they are supposed to be so great, but then I came across these. They looked decent and the other reviews seemed good, so I figured I'd give them a shot (the price helped a lot in that decision, as well). I am so glad I did! First, they are very comfortable. As a city dweller with no car, I walk a lot. These have an awesome cushy insole that makes walking long distances easy. Second, I am always worried about size when ordering online. I am usually between an 8 and a 9 but sometimes have to go up to a 9.5 depending on the brand. I ordered a 9 in these and they fit quite nicely. I believe i have enough room for my fleece liners as well (I haven't tried them yet). If this is any comparison, I fit a size 6 men's converse... for my fellow converse wearers out there that may need something relatable.
Overall, I have been quite pleased with these (I am wearing them as I type this), and would strongly recommend them to anyone. They are well made and seem like they will last me quite a few years.

reviews.title: I order my regular size in another Kamik rubber boot that is ankle length and they fit GREAT. I would suggest consistency in the
reviews.body: I ordered these rubber boots a size larger because of the height and knowing how hard rubber boots are to get in and out of after working outside in them for hours.  I was able to get my right foot into the right boot.  However, never managed to get my left foot into the left boot.  I order my regular size in another Kamik rubber boot that is ankle length and they fit GREAT.  I would suggest consistency in the size of the ankle curve and making the ankle curve a little less fitted for ease of entry and exit.  Loved the look of the boot and thickness of the rubber.  I wish these had worked for me.

reviews.title: Bought 5 Coconut coffees and I ranked this one the lowest flavor
reviews.body:
I purchased several Coconut flavored coffee brands and wanted to rank/describe them. I like my flavored coffee hot with International Delight Cold Stone sweet cream flavored creamer. I listed these in order I would prefer to drink them based on taste and then noted price comments per ounce of grounds.

Christopher Bean Coffee Toasted Island Coconut – Hot this coffee is good and has the taste of a more robust darker roast. The Coconut flavor is mild and had no tart aftertaste when it’s hot with the creamer and at just $0.66 per ounce it is a good coffee and a very reasonable price for those who want to taste coffee in their cup.

Dunkin' Donuts Coffee, Coconut Flavored – Hot with creamer it was a good Coconut flavor and tasted like a mild roast with no bitter aftertaste. It even made the kitchen smell wonderful while brewing. Cold and black had the tart aftertaste that was unpleasant. The real downside to this coffee is the price at $1.72 per ounce.

Joe Knows Coffee Ground Coconut Crazy Joe – Hot it is a good light roast taste with a slight Coconut flavor. If you want a very mild coffee this one may work well for you. I enjoyed it though I like a little more robust coffee roast flavor and at just $.77 per ounce it is also a good buy.

Royal Kona 10% Kona Coffee Blend, Toasted Coconut Flavor – This coffee seems to smell and taste more like it be be Kahlua flavored instead of Coconut and is OK tasting at best for a Coconut flavor. Mudslides are good, Kahlua Cheesecake isn’t and this is a taste in between. At $1.87 per ounce it is a bit underwhelming and there are better flavor and price options.

Kauai Ground Coffee, Coconut Caramel Crunch – To me this coffee is just gross. Tart fruit type aftertaste and no Coconut flavor to be found. Nasty hot or cold, black or with creamer. I had to throw this out in the trash after one brew. At $0.70 per ounce it is cheap to try so you may want to see for yourselves.

reviews.title: Time-tested classics that still hold up
reviews.body:
NOTE: The "black" version is the Massdrop release! It uses different parts than the classic "silver" design. This review is for the originals.
Great on-ears that are very responsive to EQ. Relatively easy to drive and can get uncomfortably loud without knocking. Classic design that has withstood the test of time. Comfortable and light, and the adjustable temples lets them fit every head size and stay there. If necessary, the metal headbands can be bent to allow for more esoteric fits. Easy to fold up and throw in a bag—however, will not easily fit in small/tight pockets since they fold in and don't rotate flat like other newer designs. Despite this, the Koss protective case (sold seperately with this version) ended up fitting well in my large jean pockets.
Works well when paired with smartphones and handheld HiFi players, or for on-the-go laptop use. Highs are a little messy and get worse with higher volume, but it is not noticeable in day-to-day casual listening. Their on-ear and semi-open-back design lets you hear what is going on around you at lower volumes, so they are good for walking and light exercise. Usable for critical listening though I wouldn't recommend it. If using for that, get the Yaxi pads to even out the sound signature, widen the soundstage, and make them a bit more comfortable. They are a worthwhile upgrade.
I find their out-of-box sound really complements the garbage sound chips on the smartphones I have tested them with, and smooths out the often poor highs and muddy mids you encounter in that particular arena. Of course, proper EQing and raw external DAC output is recommended if available.
While the build quality and design are solid almost all around, the cables are by far the weakest part, as the cables are fed loosely around plastic pegs on the back of the driver case before being soldered to pads. You can also get some light microphonics when the cable's rubber sleeve rubs againnst the plastic housing of the cups, though it is only noticeable while moving and if you're listening for it, in my experience. I recommend applying a bit of glue to hold the cables in place and help prevent damage; has an additional effect of removing the mentioned microphonics, eliminating most cable noise.
Overall I am very impressed that this design has lasted as long as it has. They still sound just as good as they did years ago. No reason to skip them if they are on sale. At full price there might be some better options available, especially if their features and design are not to your liking.

reviews.title: Koss PortaPro Headphones a Hit with Whole Family!
reviews.body:
I'm a Mom of teens ages 14 and 15 and I cringed every time I saw earbuds shoved in my kid's ears and could hear the sound from 6 feet away. I'd listened to a report on NPR, "Kids' Use of Earbuds Worries Hearing Experts" a few years ago and thought headphones might be safer than earbuds if used correctly*.

As usual for anything tec, I started my information search on CNET. The Koss PortaPro headphones were the only top-rated headphones under $100. Amazon was next and after scanning the reviews on Amazon, I ordered one for our son.

The [[ASIN:B00001P4ZH Koss PortaPro Headphones with Case]] are a HUGE hit! He loves the sound quality and has found a new preferred method to watch a movie - on his 17" screen laptop. I can sit next to him and not hear the sound "leaking" and he tells me that for the most part, ambient sounds in the room, even the TV (12 feet away) don't interfere with his listening, even though the headphones are not promoted as having a "noise cancellation" feature.

I've been doing spot-checks of the volume my son is listening at, and find that unlike his old earbuds, he isn't finding the need to crank up the volume with the Koss PortaPro headphones.

My son finds the headphones a snap to position, comfortable (have not pulled his hair) and loves the snap-together storage and bag for when he's heading out with his gear. He has no complaints and lots of compliments - best holiday gift he received this year according to him.

Mom -- well I love the sound too! I've always been partial to the bass being a little on the heavy side, so the sound is perfect for me. The sound is wonderful; I now prefer listening to music through the headphones over our room speakers (that I now know need replacing too)!

*Safe headphone use for kids, teens and adults: Just Google "The 101 on Ear Bud and Headphone Usage" for great advice from parentalguide.org

reviews.title: Koss dont ever stop making these headphones!!!
reviews.body:
Looking for a good pair of quality headphones nowadays is hard to do without breaking the bank, but I can assure you don't let the old school look fool you, when Koss came out with these in 1984 they got it right. Solid construction, adjustable temple pads, and free floating ear pieces, and a sound that for its price in my opinion cant be beat. Upon receiving the headphones I went right for my mp3 player anticipating what I would hear or not hear, and I can tell you the range, depth and just outright toughness these headphones bring to the music is unreal. I can honestly say I havent been able to crank them up to the point of distortion yet. You are only limited on quality of sound by the quality of your mp3 or recording, not the headphones. I have heard sounds in my music now that I didnt know existed, so check some of your songs you like and see what you "can" hear now that you couldnt hear before.

Pros:
1: Construction solid
2: Comfort is great, I have worn them for 5 hours straight with no discomfort
3: Sound is perfect, no distortion from the headphones, so if you hear distortion, check your mp3 download or recording itself and if you hear unwanted sound its the quality of what you are listening to and not the headphones
4: Value is key to me, for under $50 you cant beat it

Cons:

2: To me this isnt a con because I myself havent experienced it yet but some do complain of the metal bands catching their hair in it.
I have long hair and havent had an issue so, to each his or her own

Bottom line is Koss came out with a great product long ago and im so glad they continue to produce it. If the time comes I find out they discontinue this model, I will buy as many as I can so I will always have one to listen to and enjoy the sound and music to its fullest so everyone, try them and enjoy!!!

reviews.title: Maybe the best Bang for your Buck Headphones Ever.
reviews.body:
I am most certainly not an audiophile but these headphones came highly recommended not only from other sites but from other people I know. They are a classic design from the eighties which is now nouveau chic again.I am a heavy heavy tech user and like to use high quality items and I demand a lot from them.

With that said these are my new favorite headphones (the one's that travel with me everywhere).I was skeptical even after reading all the reviews, thinking "How could something so reasonably priced really be as good as all of these reviews suggest." Well they can be and are, consider my doubts banished as I was pleasantly surprised. The reviews are correct, this is Koss' masterpiece, homerun, the epitome of what Koss represents.

I have a pair of Bose Triport Headphones and Senneheiser PX200's both of which are excellent headphones....and these Porta Pros are commandingly better (the Triports are "warmer" and the Senneheisers crisper, but I like the sound of these best as they are the cleanest clearest balance of warmth & crispness).

They are light weight, foldable, exceptionally comfortable and of coarse the sound quality is excellent.

Actually, I cannot say enough about the sound quality, it is well balanced, full, hits the highs, lows and everything in between accurately. They produce clean scratch that pristine audio that is a pleasure to listen to. I find myself searching out music that can challenge or push these and they just keep on producing beautiful music to my ears.

Essentially they are awesome. (period) They sound and function better than headphones easily two or three times their price, look cool if you're into retro and they are dirt cheap.

CONCERNS:
The only concerns if any are that the part that connects the earpiece to the headphone part doesn't seem very robust and may break eventually(though I haven't had any issues). Some may find that the metal headband might catch on their hair (something else I haven't had an issue with, though I have short hair) and finally, the foam pads over the earphones sort of scream I'm cheap and I will wear out on you. In defense of them, it does keep with the whole retro thing, it's really comfortable, it's easily replaceable, and they are in fact inexpensive, essentially who cares. Many of these small things have been ever so slightly adjusted on the Anniversary Edition of these gorgeous nearly perfect headphones (but for twice the price I wouldn't bother). Oh and Koss has an included lifetime warranty for the life of the product, ridiculous!(amazing) For me this tosses basically all of the concerns out the window.

Conclusion:
-Beautiful design and function (form and function married beautifully, just one of those products that is right on, balanced, perfect in most ways) Clearly the designers got it and knew what they were doing when they made these.
-Koss' famous lifetime warranty.
-Worth every penny, I would feel good about paying twice the price and wouldn't bat an eye. Awesome part is you don't have to. I would buy them again, for myself or others.

reviews.title: PortaPro So-So
reviews.body:
I've had serious experience with the following:

Sennheiser PX-100s
B & O A8
Sennheiser HD 280 Pro

and now I've also experienced the Koss PortaPros.

I picked these up because my PX-100s were out of commission for a couple days. The plug wiring gave out and I had to solder on a new plug. No biggie. The other reason is that when I looked at the PX-100s, the $68.00 ++ price tag just made me so sad. These used to be $40 max back in the day!

The PortaPros are built alright. There's minimum fuss over the headband, which cuts down on the amount of things that can break, but the headband extension feature leaves a lot of be desired. It was irritating to have to reset the headphones on my head because every time I take them off, the headband snaps back to its default setting. The "firm-med-light" switch was pretty much useless to me. I played with it but after a couple fiddles, just gave it up. It snaps back to "firm" anyway if you knock the earphones' hinge with any amount of pressure. Pointless.

I put them on and cued up some Stereolab - Metronomic Underground. It's got a good drum track, a dedicated bass-line, layer vocals, guitar, squeaks and burbles, other synth effects. What shocked me was how much the PortaPros boosted the bass end. In fact, so much so that it made everything else seem extremely muffly at first. I do like the bass end of things, but I like it to be clear, punchy and immediate, not make me feel like it's melting over onto everything while being pushed through a cardboard tube full of toilet paper into a large anechoic chamber while I am standing at the other side in the doorway. For some reason, I always think the problem is because the speakers are just not on my ear, like I can never get the speakers to be on my ear CLOSE enough to the eardrum, if that makes sense.

But then here's the bizarre part, the mids feel close, like really close. So you have the muffle going on while someone is literally right inside your year. It's disorienting. It also makes the PortaPros actual sound sound a little cheap.

It took me a while to get used to and to be honest, I'm still not quite used to it. The boosted bass makes me cringe because it's too much while at the same time, not being immediate enough. But I've decided to keep these. My rating for them is in the wider relative range of things. If you're going to buy earphones and you have a budget, yes, buy these. These are better than the millions of crap earbuds out there on your stock iPhone/Pod/Touch purchase or Target offerings. I'm relegating these to everyday, beater use and saving my PX-100s for home use when I don't feel like bulking up with the 280 Pros.

But if you have the skrill and are competent with a soldering iron, get the PX-100s to use for years to come. Zey are still ze best.

reviews.title: Koss Porta Pro regular Black version vs Koss Porta Pro Limited Edition Black Gold version
reviews.body:
I bought Koss Porta Pro Black and Koss Porta Pro Black Gold Limited Edition at the same time 2 months ago after delaying for the longest time. I have other more expensive headphones such as Sennheiser HD58X, HD6XX, HD660S, Beyerdynamic DT990, Audio-Technica ATH-A2000X and ATH-AD2000X and had thought that these cheaper Koss Porta Pro headphones wouldn't amount to much in terms of sound quality. How wrong I was! Now having listened to them, I'm very impressed and tend to use them more often nowadays.

The Black Gold Limited Edition has a microphone, volume control and comes with the "Koss Porta Pro Official Hard Carry Case" while the regular Black version does not have a microphone, volume control and does not come with a hard carry case.

At the time of my purchase, the Black Gold Limited Edition cost 2X the price of the regular Black version.

I'm very surprised no one ever did an A-B sound quality comparison between these 2 versions. Perhaps everyone assumed that they sound the same and differ only in color scheme, availability of a microphone, volume control and a hard carry case while costing twice as much?

Who really wants to pay double for having an additional microphone, volume control and a hard carry case if the headphones sound the same? But I was really curious, so I bought these 2 versions at the same time to compare.

I'll tell you right off the bat that the Limited Edition sounds noticeably superior to the regular version. The regular version sounds good, but the Limited Edition sounds even better. I've done direct A-B comparisons between the two versions using the same songs and music tracks over and over and found that they sound clearer, are more lively, more dynamic and more 3-dimensional on the Limited Edition. Bass punches harder and there's more air, more sparkle in the treble of the Limited Edition compared to the regular version.

In contrast, the regular version sounded more laid-back, is less resolving and less dynamic. There's slightly less bass and treble extension in the regular version when compared to the Limited Edition.

I've wondered why there's a difference in sound quality between these two versions, as design, material used and the speaker drivers themselves are the same and have identical specs, until I examined their cables.

I now believe that the two versions sound different because they have completely different headphone cables. The regular version has a two-strand cable going into the headphone jack, while the Limited Edition has a single-strand cable. Complaints by other owners about the thinner cable used on the Limited Edition are justified, as the single strand of cable used has the same thickness as one of the two strands used on the regular version. And yet, the sound quality of the Limited Edition is noticeably superior to that of the regular version.

So it's a real trade-off: you get better sound quality, but thinner cable on the Limited Edition. And it cost 2X as much as the regular version too (although you do get a microphone, volume control and hard carry case with the Limited Edition)

Still, I'm of the opinion that the superior sound quality on the Limited Edition more than makes up for this cable shortcoming, just that you have to be more careful in handling the thinner single-strand cable.

In conclusion, if you are not so particular about having the best sound quality and worry more about breaking headphone cables, I'd recommend getting the regular Koss Porta Pro version.

But if you want the best-sounding Koss Porta Pro, it's the Limited Edition Porta Pro for you. And if you find the Limited Edition going for less than 2X the price of the regular version one day, it's really a no-brainer to get the Limited Edition immediately.

reviews.title: not durable enough -- my revised review changes star rating down to 3 stars
reviews.body:
follow-up comment, June 11, 2007
I ended up sending one of the broken headsets back to Koss, along with a $6 check. Turns out, these have a lifetime guarantee, and for $6, they will repair or replace them for you. I got the new pair in rapid order-- total turn-around was about 10 days. Caution--if you send these in for repair, do NOT include the pouch; they returned only the headphones, without the pouch. Anyway, it was really nice having the new headphones. BUT, this morning, I picked them up to put into the little carry pouch I use for my Nano and headphones, and found that the left earpiece was dangling again, broken at the swivel point.
I really like the comfort of these headphones and the fact that I don't have to crank up the volume to hear. But, I am now actively looking for a replacement to use, as these are obviously too frail for the constant folding and unfolding they get for my commutes to and from work. Sorry to have to do this, but I would change my 4 stars down to 3 (but Amazon is not letting that happen).
If you will not be stuffing these in a storage pouch but will be simply laying them on a desk or table, then these are great. If you plan to fold and open a lot, I now suggest you look for something more durable.
Sorry, KOSS!
------------
origianal review Jan 6, 2007:
Quality good enough to make me get a 3rd pair
I have gone through 1.5 pairs of these things, now (my current pair is nearly ready for replacement). The first pair finally broke apart while folded in the soft bag that comes with it (I had had those about 6 or 7 years) -- I took them out and the left earpiece had broken at the plastic attach point and was left hanging. My second pair is now only 2.5 years old (purchased April 2004), and the wire at the plug end is getting iffy. If the wire moves, sometimes the phones go into single ear mode, so I guess one of the wires inside the very thin cable is breaking at the joint. This plug has a right angle into the player, and it is right at the cord end of the right angle piece where the wire is weakening. I am going to try taping it here to keep it from moving, and see if that solves the problem temporarily.
I do side by side test with this headphone and others used by other individuals. I ask them to put the volume where it won't blow out my eardrums, then I listen using their phones and settings. I then plug in my portapros, and listen. So far, I have not found anyone's setup to beat the quality and clairty and volume delivered by these phones. Usually, I have to turn the player DOWN when I plug in my phones because they pick up so much more than others.
If you are prepared to buy a new pair of these every 5 years or so, then these are definitely a good deal.
I just wish Koss would send a hard case for storage since I do believe that the soft case does not protect them enough when they are stowed. Koss could also thicken the cable a little bit to make it more durable, or do a gradual thickening as the cable nears the plug. When I get a new pair, I will tape that end of the cable to try to postpone this problem -- less than 3 years is too soon for this to happen.
Becasue of these two design flaws, I rate these a 4 intead of the 5 that the quality of sound delivers.
I listen to jazz, smooth jazz, pop, rock, and audiobooks primarily.
Happy listening!

reviews.title: Are they really intended to sound like this?
reviews.body:
I am absolutely puzzled by the multitudes of glowing reviews. In my opinion,the sound quality of the PortaPros I received is actually inferior to that of the earbuds that came free with my Ipod Shuffle. At least the Ipod buds have a sharp,clear sound,as opposed to the absolutely muddled sound emitting from the PortaPros. I actually returned my first pair to Koss and got a replacement,assuming I had received a defective pair. Nope. Second one is identical to the first. Tried it from three different sources (Sony boombox,RCA personal player,HTC Flyer tablet) and all three produced the same results. The Ipod buds,while having a thin and not particularly impressive sound,always were clearer and much punchier. The PortaPros had no clarity. Where the PortaPros truly performed poorly was in playing anything with heavy electronic elements,such as industrial rock and trip hop. While the PortaPros sounded acceptable playing vocals against a more or less pop background,it all became fuzz when bass was involved. No punch,just muddled noise. A favorite album of mine became dull and lifeless when heard through the PortaPros.
I am not an audiophile,so I had a relative who is try them out,to get her opinion. Her immediate reaction: Muffled. She agreed the Ipod buds are clearer. She thinks that neither pair really sound any good,with no differentiation of tones(no highs,no lows,just mids) but she thought the buds were at least not muffled like the PortaPros,and so won marginally.
I do not expect 40 dollar headphones to sound as impressive as 200 dollar ones (although many of the reviewers here suggest they might) but I do expect them to sound better than earbuds that came free with a 40 dollar Shuffle.
The one pro I can think of regarding the PortaPros is comfort. I do find them easier to wear than other headphones(lightweight,not cumbersome,do not squeeze my head) and much more comfortable than the Ipod buds. Comfort is a moot point,however,when the listening experience is depressingly lackluster.
I still can't help but wonder...did I somehow get TWO bad pairs? This can't possibly be the same sound that endless customers are raving about. Still,it seems highly unlikely that a pair purchased through Amazon and one sent directly from Koss would both be defective,especially considering I am not seeing anyone else complaining of receiving faulty units with poor sound quality.

reviews.title: Upgraded from Apple Earphones to PortaPros
reviews.body: Listening to my iPod almost a year with Apple Earphones, I realized that the sound quality from them was not what I desired. After browsing many forums and searching for a reasonably priced pair of headphones, I discovered the Koss PortaPros. I'll start by reviewing what came in the package: The headphones itself, a bag-like carrying case, and the .25" adapter. The carrying case was not what I had expected, it seems very durable yet I am not quite sure of how to fold the headphones into the case for I've tried many different ways and it doesn't seem to fit. The adapter is very useful and I am glad Koss decided to include it as well. The headphones of course are amazing compared to the cheap earbuds I had before. Not only is the sound quality is great, but the overall design is  good as well. The comfortZone feature is an added design that provides extreme comfort to the headphones. Also, the length of the cord is not too short or too long. The over band is quite durable, and yes, it does snag your hair every now and then, but that is easy to ignore with such cans as these. Oh, and don't forget the Lifetime Warranty. These PortaPros are competitors against much higher priced headphones, so if you're looking for an upgrade in a mid level price range, I definitely recommend Koss PortaPros. I forgot to mention, I used the Super Saver Shipping and the order arrived 3 days prior to the estimated shipping date.

Although it is not a crisp, clear and punchy bass, it goes very well with dance, pop, techno, etc. Nonetheless, they don't sound good at all for rock n' roll. They are very easy to drive (high sensitivity). They are easy to carry as well (as you can fold them). For the price, I'd definitively recommend them. If you want a better build quality product, with crisp sound, punchy bass, nice noise isolation and easy to drive, you are going to spend much more. For that purpose, check the Sennheiser HD 25-1 ii (or the new model: amperior).

I have owned many high end headphones over the years, Sennheiser being my favorite, tube headphone amp and all. I know great sound and consider myself an audiophile. First off they are very comfortable. I have never found a set of in ear (ear bud style) headphones comfortable, and I've tried many different types, never felt comfortable wearing them regardless of the sound quality. These are comfortable. You can wear them for hours at a time. Never got my hair caught in them like other reviewers.
As far as the sound, they have good range and surprisingly good bass, for the design. Not the greatest detail in the mids and upper range, but overall they sound very good.
People rag on the aesthetics, but I really like it. I grew up in the 80's, and love the retro look.
For the money you can't beat them. Very satisfied with the purchase.

reviews.title: Not only great sound at this pricepoint, but a great warranty
reviews.body:
I've been using PortaPro's for two years. During this time I have gone through 3 or 4 pairs. These are great everyday headphones that I travel with all the time. In that travel I abuse and unfortunately break them abuse on the cords. The warranty on them is great. Simply mail the damaged pair with a $9.00 and you get a new pair in less than 2 weeks time.

Sound quality is perfectly good for a pair of headphones in this price range. They aren't noise canceling which I like, in NYC it's nice to be able to hear a honking horn to warn me if I'm about to get run over. But on the other hand I do need to be more courteous on the subway because noise will leak out. But overall I am very happy with the sound quality they provide for my everyday headphones.

The design hasn't changed, and I love the retro-look and very functional design. They collapse very well the springlike tension of the metal allows the clasps to keep the headphones in a nice little ball. Occasionally the clasps come undone in my bag, but overall it works.

There are a few annoyances though. Although, there are settings to adjust how much pressure is placed on your ears, I do notice that after 70 minutes or so of wear I do notice discomfort on where the bands grips my head. It's not terrible, but the pressure is noticeable, but only after very long uses. Also, I have had my hair get snagged while adjust the band during wear. I've learned to avoid that problem, but I expect most users will experience an unpleasant tug at times.

But despite this, you get a very reliable pair of headphones that provide good bang for your buck in terms of sound and quality. And should you every break them in the future, you can get a brand new pair for $9 with the lifetime warranty.

reviews.title: A lifetime warranty, yes, but problems after mild use?
reviews.body:
Should these headphones last longer than three years with very careful use? I bought them in 2012 for use with my desktop Mac and they never left the house, then suddenly one of the channels went out and I was left with one-ear-only phones. Koss famously says they have a lifetime guarantee, but I find it odd that I should need to invoke it after such a short time and with such mild use.
I've read reports here that a REPLACEMENT pair of phones went out on another customer after 6 months. I hope that doesn't happen with the replaced Koss models, which cost me $6 to send the old ones and a $9 check made out to Koss. Meanwhile my old, cheap pair of Sennheizers still work fine after 20 years.

This compares to: in-ear (terrible, but pocketable), over-ear (best noise cancellation, but hot to wear over time).

reviews.title: The hype seems very underserved or something is wrong.
reviews.body:
The description does say "Designed for deep bass performance" and yes... it delivers on that. And that seems to sort of be it? They're fairly uncomfortable, and sounds like it lacks clarity. The sound besides the bass is just ok. The bass is very strong. Do I regret the purchase? Not really. They are compact, and there might be scenarios where I want to use this form factor, and the price is low.

But the huge hype behind these is just baffling me at this moment. I'd seen these mentioned online, and a friend of mine was praising how good that are. (They introduced me to some very good JVC headphones so I had trust) and my disappointment is... pretty strong. I've certainly paid the same price or less for better experiences. I even see other reviews mentioning how BRIGHT these muddy things are? Are mine defective or counterfeit or something???? They're just meh.

I've seen mods online to make them more comfortable, but I feel inclined to not invest anything more into something so underwhelming.

reviews.title: I was hoping for more. I think they are just ok
reviews.body:
They are okay, considering the price. But I was really hoping for more. The bass is decent but the treble is a little painful. Surprisingly, the "comfort zone" adjustments really do make a difference between "light" to "firm". You might be able to get a nice balance with careful tweaking on your EQ, but these are NOT magical sound machines for a cheap price. If you have already been spoiled by nicer headphones, then these will not be that great. If you have never spent more than $50 for some headphones, then these will be great.

So far, my personal favorites are still the Klipsch Image ONE Earphones. They sound amazing and I am in love with the bass, but they get uncomfortable after an hour or two. My Sennheiser HD428 are my second fave - less bass, but better balance. And these come in third. I really wanted to like these more, but I honestly considered returning them. I think I'll keep them just as lightweight, inexpensive traveling headphones.
