reviews.title: Love these.
reviews.body:
This is my second pair of these headphones, but only because I totally destroyed the first pair through my own silly mistake, after 2 years of solid use.

Great sound, very lightweight, very portable. I start to get a little bit of a pinched feeling just above my ears after 5 or so hours of constant wear... which is really longer than headphones should be worn consecutively.

After about a year and a half, I wore out the cord joint near the plug, but I do that to just about every pair of headphones. Something about the way my iPod sits in my pocket. The cord frayed and I repaired it with Sugru. I don't feel like this is a fault of the construction; another friend has had a pair for 5 years and has no wear on his at all.

The new pair sounds just as good as the old pair, with no sense that the first pair had started to sound worse through use.

Like I said, great headphones. I hope they never stop making these, because the next time I do something ridiculous and destroy these, I'm going to want another pair just like it.

It was more bitter, but still lacked a good coffee taste I crave for a regular roasted coffee. I just can't get into it like what I would like.

reviews.title: Good audio quality but cheap construction in part
reviews.body:
Update: December 19, 2013

I would just like to follow up on the article I wrote previously for this product. I have been using this headset daily for nearly a year now and it has easily surpassed expectations. The volume control is still annoying, although to be honest I have so may other options available to mute the device or adjust volume that it is more-or-less a non-issue. The construction is also holding up well despite my abuse. There has been no staining of the ear pads and no dye rub-off on the skin. In fact, the headset itself still looks as good as new.

The only issue is where I accidentally walked away from my machine while wearing the headset and ended up yanking the USB plug which caused it to bend at a weird angle. It still works though and straightened out okay although the plug is now slightly loose - I cannot complain here.

This headset gets a solid recommendation.

--- Previous review - January 7, 2013 ---

I just purchased this item through a brick and mortar store. The overall sound quality is pretty decent, and after 4 hours of wear on first use I have experienced no issues at all with discomfort, which is surprising.

My primary issues are with the volume control not working consistently across different PC's and the overall build quality. On my laptop the volume control works fine while playing PlanetSide 2, however it does not work on my PC. This might just be an issue with the setup so I will have to investigate further and won't mark down the review due to this. The volume control is also setup slightly weird. The outer circular part of the control is for volume and the inner part is a mute button. I keep accidentally hitting the mute button due to my large fingers so for me this is a detractor.

I am a little worried about how well these headphones will stand up to use over time. Although the mic boom and ear-pads appear to be solidly constructed, there is a little too much play in the actual headband itself. I wouldn't be surprised if they break in less than a year as it feels slightly flimsy. For the price though you really can't argue too much.

All-in-all this is a reasonable product.

P.S. Packaging: To open this product you have to pull apart the packaging at the bottom. There is a kind of tear apart seam which requires two hands and a little strength. Look for the <[][] symbol on the bottom for where to pull apart.
There is also no real information about the product on the packaging or in the information packet apart from it being a USB connected device. It would have been nice to be able to see the frequency response before actually opening. I almost didn't buy this headset due to this information being missing.

reviews.title: I used the same headset for 7 years
reviews.body: I'm unsure if their product has since changed. This review is based off of my personal experience with this headset that I have used for 7+ years. This headset which I purchased followed me from the office to remote work at home and continued not only it's 40+ hour a week work abuse but also the occasional Netflix, Hulu or gaming binge. It also survived 2 major moves from 1 state and back. Never had any issues with sound quality,  the mute button was well used and no issues with that either. I used to get jealous of some of my co workers when I wished for an early out due to 'headset malfunction/ have to go buy a new one' because they seemed to have monthly issues with theirs and I also wanted an early out sometimes. Years and years later, with a lot of the same co workers I am the one laughing at how much everyone else has spent on their headsets. "Bertha" passed away at the age of 7. After I tripped over her from not paying attention. Had I been watching where I was stepping she would still be working today. I hope the quality of Logitech is still the same as I have just purchased another headset. Hope this experience helps anyone in the market for a good work headset.

reviews.title: Best of Four
reviews.body:
I've now purhased, all from Amazon, a total of 4 headsets, each of a different type, one of which was quite expensive [200$]: a blue tooth model, a folding usb model, a wireless usb model- and the Logitech model featured on this page.

I use a headset exclusively with a computer. Mostly Skype, but also occasional dictation, very occasional entertainment.

The BT: each time I restarted the computer, one needs locate the device again, then go to skype audio and re-assign the bluetooth feature. Not difficult, but an added chore when all one wants to do is make a quick skype phone call.

The folding model: good enough but delicate; of what use is portability if the thing breaks when carried?

The expensive model was wireless [USB]. Worked well enough, allowing one to walk quite a distance with the comfortable headset attached. This is quite liberating. However, the volume, even maxed out, was almost NEVER adequate: one must keep hand pressed to headset for the duration of the call [my hearing is not the same as a teenager's, but is still adequate].

Suffice to say that of all the headsets, and not inconsiderable expense- the Logitech on this page surpassed them all:
sturdy
immediate connection, true plug and play every time
great sound
reliable.

I use this for my base headset and portable model as well: just toss it in the brief. It's a solid build. Dictation: great sound quality. It has an 8' wire, so one can move about at least somewhat.

Soon I am traveling to a remote location, so I am now ordering a second one of these. Will carry two of these Logitech models [one for backup], rather than any of the other types. I rely on Skype for long distance phone calls, and with this USB model, at least I am sure I will have a headset that always works, and works well.

reviews.title: Headset I've used for years, and I love it.
reviews.body:
I purchase this headset every 3-5 months. It's a great headset. The sound quality is great, voice is amazing. It doesn't hurt my ears, and it's just comfortable. Maybe I'm used to it, and that's why I like it so much, I don't know.

There are a few issues, the cord after a month starts to get tangled. You can fix this by taking a hot cup of water and and wrapping the cord around the outside of the cup, and holding it there for about 30 minutes to an hour. However about 3 to 5 months in something breaks. Happens every time, and I've literally bought this headset for years. Seriously years. I don't take that great care of it though, and sleep with it sometimes. So it will probably last 6-8 months if you take better care of it and don't sleep with it on.

Overall, it's a good headset. I like it. It's comfortable. I recommend it, but keep in mind if you are rough with it, it's only going to last 3-5 months. Just purchased another one today since the one I have now, sort of broke on the right side, and the sound quality has gone down a bit.

reviews.title: Very good headset for teleconferencing
reviews.body:
This is a very good headset for teleconferencing on a computer. The earphones are of good quality (even good enough to listen to music!) and drown (but not cancel) most outside noises, and the microphone is excellent. The USB connection is more reliable and less noisy than standard earphone plugs. It just works, without any hassle, on Linux. You can control the audio volume - and silence the microphone - directly from buttons on the headphone's cable. The microphone can be folded out of the way when not speaking, e.g., listening to music.
The headset is not very small, but not huge either - so it doesn't look ridiculous on video calls.
The only downside for me is that wearing this headset for a few hours can become less comfortable on the ears (this may be related to the fact I have glasses).

reviews.title: Great sound, comfy not plush
reviews.body:
OK, I'd bought the Pro before this. Pro had a cord that seemed to wrap itself around my feet no matter where I tried to set it, until the last time I tripped on it, it almost destroyed my usb port. No quick-release to spare the usb port, instead the usb plug-in on the Pro fell apart, part of it remained lodged in my usb port until I stopped shaking and managed to gingerly remove it w/some effort.

Now these earphone cushions aren't as plush (ironic since it's the Comfort model, eh?), but the cord stays where I put it, instead of stalking me like a creepy snake! Sounds better than my computer Bose when listening to online music (Pandora Radio), clear as a bell on Skype, keeps all but the loudest ambient noise from reaching whoever I'm talking to. Mic is easy to get out of the way to just listen.

It looks cheaper than the Pro, so get the Pro if you can tame the stalker snake cord and care more about cushiness and looks than your ports and sound. The Comfort's sound seems to automatically adjust to whatever you're listening to, tho it doesn't have the Pro's fancy selector for gaming/phone/music. The Comfort vol control/mute should have a clip rather than hook-on, but I use the Mac remote anyway.

In sum, could've been more plush and fancier, it seems to fall apart easily if dropped (logo cover on one side fell off! clipped back on easily tho). I'd like to swap this cord w/the Pro, but the fiasco w/the Pro cord puts that model out of my setup for good! Obviously these imported (from China?) headsets aren't the greatest quality, but excellent for the price.

Oh, the packaging, an ecological nightmare. Find a plastics-artist to give the non-recyclable plastic packaging to, or it'll end up choking a sea lion or dolphin somewhere.

reviews.title: DO NOT USE ON RED DYED HAIR
reviews.body:
If you have dyed hair, DO NOT USE LOREAL PRODUCTS.

I used their Elvive Color Vibrancy set (shampoo, conditioner, and serum) this morning. My hair was box dyed two months ago, professionally dyed two weeks ago. I have pictures from YESTERDAY where my hair is the color it is supposed to be. Today, after using their products, my hair is almost back to its original color (from dark, dark auburn to ash blonde/brown). It didn't just NOT provide the 'anti-fade, high shine, & protect' it DID THE OPPOSITE. My hair is now dull brown, not a hint of red, and dry and frizzy. I have literally used dollar store products that worked better than this. I am furious and in tears. I saved for MONTHS to have my hair done right after I verified with the box dye (which was also l'oreal) that this was the color I wanted. I have hair past my hips, it is NOT cheap to dye. My time and money have been worse than wasted. What was I offered when I called the help line?

Coupons. Effing COUPONS.

I went to the FB page to post my story. I got the expected 'we're so sorry, please call us, here's a ref number, we're open until 7pm est.' So I called at 2:40pm pst...and got the 'our offices are currently closed' message. So so much for that.

My hair was one of those little things that made me happy through a particularly rough few months. So thank you, L'Oreal, for being an absolutely horrible company with zero accountability and ruining that.

reviews.title: Why you need to look out for sodium chloride in shampoos
reviews.body: I got this product at Walmart, and it's been great. Except for the fact that it has sodium chloride in it. I looked this up on google and this is what I found: Sodium Chloride is actually considered an irritant, and slightly hazardous. ... As one of the top ingredients in many shampoos, sodium chloride can affect the color of your hair and dehydrate the strands. Sulfates can potentially strip a layer of your hair, and the natural protective barrier of your hair will be damaged. I also found that it can potentially cause hair loss, which has somewhat been happening to me. But, the hair loss may just be shedding, I don't know. It all really could just be me, though.

reviews.title: If you want to smell like you live in a perfume factory
reviews.body: The smell of this shampoo and conditioner is SO potent! It didn't seem *that* bad while I was using it the shower, but when I got out it's all I could smell. I assumed the smell would fade, but after a few hours it continued to be so powerful that I could literally taste it, and when I had dinner it was interfering with my meal. I ended up taking another shower to wash the smell out of my hair with my old shampoo/conditioner, and it STILL smelled. I wasn't about to take a third shower in an evening, so I tried to deal. Went to bed, and when I woke up in the morning the whole bedroom smelled (again, this is AFTER washing my hair again with my former products). My scalp and neck/shoulders (where my hair touched) were then itchy from the overdose of perfume, and I had to take a 3rd shower in 12 hours. Guess what, it still smells like this stuff. And everything I touched after using this - my couch, bed, robe, etc., all reek of it. I feel like it could have been a decent product because my hair did feel softer after use, but the smell is something I can't get over. There are comparable products that don't leave a trail of smell behind you :/

reviews.title: Smells good//Wasted Product :(
reviews.body:
The smell is amazing and I cannot wait to try. The second I opened the box I was hit with such a very strong beautiful aroma. My only issue is that my shampoo must have opened during delivery because the bottle has no damage, but the lid was closed when I opened the box so it might have just leaked out of the bottle? I was super excited to try Maui products but opening my package to find a good bit of product had gone to waste was extremely underwhelming. I’m also confused on why only one bottle was wrapped, the bottle that was wrapped didn’t leak at all. I had seen a few other reviews saying the same thing about wasted product or even about damaged bottles so little helpful advice for future orders to save your customers and your company from wasting any more time and money, maybe you guys should wrap every product so that product doesn’t spill out or so the bottles don’t get damaged (:

Edit: I did receive a new bottle that was completely full, a day or so after writing this and I have been using Maui products ever since. My hair has never been healthier even though I am always dying it! I never knew how curly and voluptuous my hair actually was until using Maui products. All products I’ve used before would weigh my dense hair down so much making my hair flat and lifeless. Thank you Maui for bringing my hair back to life!

I've tried a couple of shampoo/conditioner pairs since and this brand is by far the worst of all.

I used it for a few consecutive washes just to make sure (I wash every other day), and this shampoo and conditioner somehow both weighed my hair down (it felt heavy?) but also dried out and tangled my hair worse than any other product in my life. My hair felt SO rough to the touch and I actually had a giant tangle the size of a ping pong ball that HURT to try to untangle, which has never happened before. I basically basted my hair in a different conditioner that was okay but I didn't love to gently untangle the mess this brand made. reviews.title: This stuff is alright
reviews.body:
I was recommended this shampoo from my demonologist for my scalp psoriasis. It may work for others, however the most this does for me is maybe not make me want to scratch my head with a razor blade the next day. (I will pair this product with another psoriasis product to help the effectiveness) I usually let it soak on my scalp for 10 minutes while scrubbing with a scalp scrubber before washing it out. It still itches and flares up without use of another product. However, my psoriasis is so bad that I do whatever I can to prevent it from giving me a lower quality of life- even if that means using this smelly, seemingly non-effective product.

The random sellers and fluctuating prices for this product on amazon are sketchy. I rarely have product that I would rather get in store than on Amazon, however, in Kroger I find it is usually cheaper. Last time I bought this product from Amazon it took almost a month to receive it. If this product works for you, buy it in store.

reviews.title: Cleansing and soothing
reviews.body:
I’ve been struggling with itchy scalp and dandruff for a while and have tried a few different products. This one is nice to use, and it can last a while even though it comes in a kind of small amount. I do half this and half shampoo for the first wash, then just this to leave on for a few minutes. It definitely cleanses my scalp and feels refreshing to use. I wouldn’t say it conditions though, as my hair feels a bit dry after, but not so much that it’s breaking off. The smell is ok, but it’s not as bad as some of the other tea tree oil ones.

Would recommend if other options haven’t worked, but consistency matters regardless of what product is being used since dandruff can only be treated and not cured.

reviews.title: Tasty Hot or Iced
reviews.body:
If you like hazelnut and flavored coffees, this one is very tasty. Our family buys this brand pretty exclusively.
We are especially fond of the hazelnut flavor. While other family members like to drink this coffee hot, I like to make an iced coffee drink out of it.

After cooling about a cup of the coffee, you add one and one-half cup almond milk (90 calories), one half cup of lowfat milk (about 50 calories), one T of dark cocoa (10 calories) and stevia--a natural sweetener from a South American herb-- for sweetener (no calories). Put it in the blender with ice and you have a delicious iced coffee mocha drink for 150 calories--the same named drink is about 400 calories at Starbucks. It is a tasty morning or mid-day treat or snack. The almond milk, decaf coffee and dark cocoa are actually good for you.

The hazelnut adds a layer of subtle flavor to the coffee and is a lovely addition.

Day 1 Selsun Blue, day 2 Neutrogena, day 3 Nizoral, and repeat). My dandruff was gone within a month and hasn't returned. reviews.title: Only 1% Ketoconazole; Impossible To Find 2% or 3% Anymore
reviews.body:
No longer 2%, let alone 3% Ketoconazole, as this brand used to be; I bought my last 4oz bottle of 2% Nizoral about five years ago; with short hair and only needing a tiny dab for a huge lather, 4oz of the old stuff twice a week (combined with quality non-active shampoo daily) was plenty and lasted forever (well, over five years, anyway).

Before that bottle, you could still get 3% "Extra Strength" Nizoral, and I had to use even less.

Walmart in Canada still sells the 2% Nizoral in the purple label, but it ain't cheap.

Apparently, Ketoconazole has been linked to liver damage when ingested; I have no idea how much your skin might absorb during a 2-3 minute shampoo, but I'm not drinking this stuff nor am I leaving it on like a cream or lotion of the same ingredient, so I'm not that worried.

I suspect I will have to use more than twice much at 1% strength, so that means the cost has effectively skyrocketed.

I have tried the other brands with different active ingredients; salicylate and coal-tar that is found in the rest simply doesn't work as well for me. I'm told there's a fourth active ingredient-shampoo that is worth trying, but I can't recall the name nor have I found any alternatives to the three common choices.

reviews.title: The Nizoral Rip-Offs Are OVER!
reviews.body:
* During the past five years, Nizoral has only been available via a "black market" of sorts.

* Sellers have been asking for mind-boggling amounts of money for bottles of the original, "gold-standard," Belgium-made-formula - taking advantage of buyers upset over the horrific red tape issues involving manufacturing standards associated with its makers, McNeil, Inc. in Fort Washington, Pennsylvania - and with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This created endless shortages and massive "hoarding behavior" throughout the United States.

* These issues have now been resolved!

* What does this mean to you?

* It means no more daily checking at eBay or at other sites to buy this product at a cost equal to dinner at a five-star Parisian restaurant. No more pain to your wallet, no more paying through your nose to get Nizoral.

* Just check Amazon and/or Drugstore online and watch prices drop to under $16 for a hefty 7-ounce bottle.

* The reasons Nizoral 1% ketoconazole - is still preferred EVEN over the always available (by prescription only) 2% generic ketoconazole - are legion. Its blue-silver-colored creamy 1% formula is silkier to the touch, lightly scented and soaks the scalp in ways the red-orange or other syrupy alternative formulas cannot match. For thousands of people, it's been the only thing that WORKS to treat scalp issues, which in turn created buyer desperation when it disappeared from store shelves, causing "after-market" prices to shoot to the moon.

* Hence breathe a sigh of relief and shop around! If you see a bottle of Nizoral at a retail store this week, don't worry about "stocking up" as if you were at a Costco or a Sam's Club preparing for the Armageddon.

reviews.title: For $15 I can usually get 2x more of regular shampoo but....
reviews.body:
This product works miraculously well. I’m a product junkie, have friends who are hair stylists who have given me scalp treatments and nothing has worked as well as this. I’ve had a huge issue with flakes for at least 10 years and this is the only product to have almost immediately fixed the problem. I wasn’t expecting this to work until like 4 washes in, but when it came to wash my hair the 2nd time, the flakes were gone. (If my hair isn’t styled, I usually wash 1 a week.) Normally, a couple of days after I wash, I can take my finger to my scalp and be able to see flakes under my fingernails after scratching. I can also go a lot longer without seeing flakes.

This product doesn’t have much of a scent to it, which is great because it doesn’t interfere with my other products. I usually wash my scalp first with this and scalp brush. I rinse and then shampoo with my regular shampoo. Initially, when I started out with the product I only washed with this and then conditioned with one of curly hair products. But then I decided to focus the Nizoral on my scalp, rinse then shampoo the rest of my hair with my normal shampoo. I have very curly hair (3b) and I find that flakes seem to be a common issue with curly hair. Additionally, there are tons of hair care regimes for curly hair and you’d think I’d mess up the effectiveness of the Nizoral by using some other shampoo afterward, but not at all!

My only issue with this is how much I spent and the quantity of the product. I’ve been looking around to see if I can get it either for less or same price but more ounces and I haven’t found it. For now, my rationale is that this is a medicated product and it actually works. I’d recommend this to anyone who has a problem with flakes and have completely excused the price 😂

reviews.title: The fragrance is WOW! You are sure to get compliments.
reviews.body:
Okay - so this shampoo has incorporated the latest IN things -
# Argan Oil - Check
# No parabens - Check
# No sulphates - Check

The shampoo is an eye pleasing golden color with a GORGEOUS fragrance. It does what it is supposed to do: clean your hair. It lathers decently and rinses equally well. It leaves no residue post shower. The fragrance in the hair linger on for a long time and is very soothing and refreshing.

On a serious note, this shampoo has basically replaced the evil ammonium lauryl sulphate and its stepbrother ammonium laureth sulphate with a reportedly lesser evil - Disodium Laureth Sulfosuccinate. These are the components that actually stick to dirt, oil and grease in the hair and pull them out when rinsed with water - similar to what a laundry detergent does. On a brighter note, it does leave the hair soft and shiny apart from just the cleaning which probably most of the shampoos in the market can. It has also Argan oil which is now a very famous treatment option for hair. This shampoo actually did control my hair fall to a good extent.

The bad - The price is higher on Amazon. Walmart sells it much cheaper, go get it from there till the sellers reduce the price on Amazon. You will have to drive to a local Walmart though for that - nothing beats the delivery experts at our beloved retailer Amazon ;)

In short, this is a great shampoo. Your hair will become softer, shinier and will carry a brilliantly pleasing fragrance all day. But the end of the day this is still a chemical based shampoo and in the long run might have unwanted effects. If you are worried about the use of chemicals, switch to something herbal or 100% natural and organic - they come at a price though. If you are OK with what you are getting RIGHT NOW, go for it.

reviews.title: This is for the Moroccan Argan Oil
reviews.body:
I love the Organix Moroccan Argan Oil shampoo. The Shampoo is non-stripping and sulfate free and lathers ok even with my hard water thanks to the Disodium Laureth Sulfosuccinate which is a great substitute for sulfates and it doesn't strip your hair's natural oils. "Squeaky clean" hair isn't good.

I love three things about this shampoo and dislike nothing so far.

First thing I love is this shampoo is fresh smelling rather than nutty or sweet. Several shampoos I have used which have Argan Oil or any other type of nut based oil always smell sweet or nutty and I get tired of smelling that over time. This shampoo smells clean and not too heavy in scent but it leaves a fresh scent behind, something my husband enjoys .... a lot. :)

The scent reminds me of soap scent , something like Ivory soap but with a slightly sweet undertone. Nothing over powering IMO but when effort is made to get a whiff of your hair you can smell it.

The second thing I love about this shampoo has Argan Oil in it but doesn't have so much in it that I start to feel it build up. I have used this shampoo for a month now without feeling like I need to switch to another shampoo to strip the extra oil out of it. There is another brand of shampoo which has Argan oil in it and even though I truly enjoy it, it's not a shampoo I feel I can use long term because I start to feel like my hair was becoming oily faster than normal. The Organix Moroccan Argan Oil Shampoo has NOT left me with that feeling yet it it doesn't strip my hair.

Last but not least is the fact that it's sulfate free and at a reasonable cost. There are not many shampoos available at your local grocery store which is sulfate free. The fact that it's sulfate free does mean it will not lather up as easily as shampoos with sulfates but please read up on sulfates and what they are. The only purpose they serve it create lather but these very things can also cause dandruff in some people. My scalp is extremely sensitive to sulfates. For years I had horrible dry and oily dandruff, break outs on my scalp and even bleeding until I found the culprit is the sulfates in our shampoos. Dandruff shampoos were not helping because they all contained sulfates. Once I switched to a sulfate free shampoo the very FIRST shampoo I noticed a huge difference. No dandruff. No tight scalp, no flakes and no overly oily scalp. The only purpose for sulfates in our shampoos is to allow the shampoo to lather, especially for those who have hard water. It's debatable whether lathering is actually needed in a cleaner. Some people feel it's not and we as consumers only have an association with lather as clean where others say the later helps to move dirt. I'm with those who feel it's not needed but with the Disodium Laureth Sulfosuccinate in this shampoo I feel I get the best of both worlds.

I wash my hair every other day but shower every day. Anyone who is prone to frizzy hair should be able to relate to this regime or should consider not washing their hair every day as it strips the oil from your hair.

My hair type in case anyone wants to compare is semi coarse , thick, with a natural wave and once prone to frizzing. It's black and I'm a Caucasian mix Asian heritage

Also, this may be a pro for you, but, usually after I shower and let my hair naturally dry I have beautiful waves. After using this shampoo, my hair is as close to naturally straight as I think it gets.

The coins for me are not really cons, just unexpected. Still, love this brand. I haven't tried it in humid weather yet, will update if it makes my hair too oily.

reviews.title: Fine Hair Beware!!!
reviews.body:
This absolutely destroys fine hair. I gave this product and matching conditioner two months time to truly see what it would do. I normally had very fine slightly wavy blond hair that was structurally strong, could brush it and barely get any strands out on the brush with using even generic drug store shampoos. My hair was never falling out in large chunks until I started using these products.

When washing my hair, I started to notice that my hair texture felt weirdly gummy, like it had this weird elasticity and was stretching and breaking as I very gently washed. If I tried to run my fingers through my hair, it would stretch and pull out in the most sickening way! I was losing more hair in the shower than I ever had. It was coming out in clumps between my fingers! Absolute stuff of nightmares.

But I thought, maybe there’s something wrong with me. So I kept trying it. Over time I noticed my hair was dryer than it ever had been on the ends. It started to frizz more. There was this weird residue feeling in my hair when it was dry, and I have not been using any styling products and have been mostly letting my hair air dry since we’ve all been in quarantine. It should have been healthy, but it has never been in worse shape.

I’m throwing this out now and going back to using the more expensive products that they use at the salon because even though they cost more, it’s a way better investment than chancing it with hair destroying products like this.

Be careful!

Edit: It has been a few weeks since I stopped using this shampoo and conditioner and all of the symptoms I had from using this shampoo are gone now. My hair is starting to bounce back in terms of thickness and volume (ironic, huh?) and I no longer have any residue feeling in my hair. I’m not losing hair in the shower like I did before and it feels strong again. And this is with me using regular herbal essence shampoo and conditioner until I can get products from the salon. Lesson learned.

reviews.title: this product stops my hair from SHEDDING!!
reviews.body:
I have thick, straight beautiful asian hair but had an excessive hair shedding problem. I have tried many of the natural products for hair but nothing works for me. I finally did some research about the components used in hair products and learned that one of the possible causes of hair shedding is the SLS (sodium lauryl sulfate). All of the OGX shampoo contain no SLS, so I immediately gave it a try when i found this product while still using a conditioner from other brands.

After a week of using it, the amount of my hair shedding was substantially less than before. It lathers very well, and my hair feels very clean. Now that it's been about a month, I definitely feel that my hair is thicker and fuller (I'm not sure whether it's because my hair doesn't shed as much or the biotin makes my hair grow quicker?!?) Overall, I'm very pleased with this product, so I decide to purchase the OGX conditioner as well (coconut milk one). The coconut milk one indeed has a much better smell than the biotin one. I would definitely try the OGX coconut milk shampoo next time.

reviews.title: Doesn't exactly THICKEN hair, but visible benefits
reviews.body:
My hair: thin, baby-fine, stick-straight.

Before puberty, my hair was so thick it would snap elastics apart, but when I developed PCOS I lost a good deal (and gained it in less desirable locations). Ever since then, I've been trying to find ways to restore the fullness and volume I once had. In a way, it's cruel and unfair - I'd much rather go my whole life without having the experience, but to have thick hair and then lose it...! It's a tease.

I purchased this shampoo on a whim after I discovered the yucca/baobab "thin hair" shampoo from Shea Moisture was reformulated and now "anti-breakage" instead. This isn't a miracle shampoo by a long shot - my hair does not feel magically thicker when I grab it. However, it IS the first shampoo I've ever purchased that actually had some kind of noticeable effect on my hair.

My hair is SO SOFT compared to before. It's almost unnerving. I always characterized my hair as soft anyways (it's baby-fine, what do you expect), but this shampoo kicked up a few more notches. When I was using Shea Moisture, I noticed other products would accumulate over time, making my hair feel kind of grimy and textured. I go 3-4 days between washing my hair (usually 4, sometimes 5), and the volumizing foam I was using + texturizing sea salt spray + heat protectant spray eventually left the texture of my hair grimy.

The OGX shampoo eliminates all that and leaves me with extremely soft and shiny hair. It has that lightness and bounce I get after I go to the salon (which I never thought I'd achieve with a shampoo). I don't start feeling that "I gotta wash" sensation until 4-5 days instead of 3-4, and even then I definitely could go another day or two and be passably okay.

I've also noticed my hair holds its style better (and for a longer duration) - I use a hot air brush on a low temperature setting combined with a heat protectant spray just to give my stick-straight hair a little bit of an inwards curl (which is always a feat... any body or shape would fall out pretty fast), but sometimes I can even go another day without using my hot air brush again because the style from the day before holds.

Unfortunately, I think the hair thickening claims are a bit dubious at best. How effective can something like biotin or collagen be if they're applied topically? Not much I'd imagine. I wasn't expecting miracles from this shampoo, and I've made my peace with the fact that a decent shampoo, nice quality hair brush and a good haircut are really all I can count on to actually give my hair the illusion of volume. What I didn't count on was actually getting softer, shinier, healthier looking hair out of the bargain. My coworkers have been complimenting my hair on a weekly basis... and that's never happened before, so it must be doing something right!

reviews.title: 4C FOR HARD WATER!
reviews.body:
Omg. My hair story is that I have baby-fine, naturally blonde hair that has quite a bit of damage from the sun. Where I live for my summer job, the tap water is incredible and humidity is almost never an issue. Every day is a good hair day while I’m there.

However, as soon as I moved back to my hometown this past August, my hair became AWFUL. All of a sudden, it looked 3 shades darker every day, was oily within 6 hours of washing it, and suffered through MORE damage than it had the whole summer while being abused by harsh UV’s. Finally, I was able to trace my hair issues to the hard water in my town. Thus began my mission to save my hair from this god forsaken water.

I tried clarifying shampoo after clarifying shampoo. High-end brands, and drugstore brands. I ordered stupid “swimmer’s shampoo” from Amazon, hoping that the chemicals used to remove chlorine from hair could help my hair. I was wrong. My hair slowly got more brittle, dryer, and UGLIER!

Three weeks ago, I was meandering through Ulta as I am known to do when I’m bored. On a whim, I decided to buy the Olaplex 4C because I LOVE No. 3, so I figured that maybe another one of their products would suit my hair. And oh my GOD it did.

After just one wash, my BLONDE hair was back. No more weird-looking, perpetually dirty roots. After washing, I follow up with either Olaplex 5 or Nexxus Humectress conditioner which is my favorite protein-rich line. Even though this goes against what Olaplex recommends, I use 4C as my normal shampoo. I wash my hair every other day and have just realized that considering how hard my water is and how often I exercise; clarifying my scalp with every wash is a must.

My hair is still far from perfect, but it’s blonde again from root to tip, which means my confidence and love for my natural hair is back.💘

Matter of fact, I don’t think there is any way my scalp has ever been this clean. The first time I used it there was so much stuff in my hair. It pulled stuff up from my scalp (dandruff, product build up, etc) that I didn’t even know was there! I couldn’t feel or see anything. After the first use, I started using it weekly for maintenance. My scalp is super clean and feels good. My hair is really clean and it gets all the oils out of my hair from leave in or styling products. My hair looks and feels more clean and stronger. I would 10/10 recommend. The only was this product isn’t for you is if you only want to see the drastic difference this company always shows in the pictures or if you’re using it for hair loss. The side mesh bottle holders are too roomy for my Camelbak Chute bottle but I can use the side straps to prevent the bottle from falling out. I can place my collapsible umbrella in the other mesh holder. The top handle does press against the back of my neck but I can fix that by lowering the height of the shoulder straps, although I do still feel some pressure against my neck. I really like the back space for a water bladder. It's big enough to fit my 1.5L bladder so I imagine it would fit a 2L bladder as well. reviews.title: Daylite Works Well for Carrying Gear to Road Races + Bag Check
reviews.body:
I had a very specific intent for this bag: I was looking for a way to transport my road racing gear (jacket, waterbottle, gels, bib, etc.) to bag check at road races. The bag had to be comfortable but also packable. I needed to be able to empty my stuff out of this bag and place it inside of the plastic bags they give you to store your stuff at marathon races and the like (so, 18" tall or less) and then stuff this bookbag inside of that plastic bag. In short, it needed to be quite compact. And I wanted to be able to run with the bag (if I was running late) for 1-2 miles to and from the start line. I considered the Daylite Plus and the Daylite, and ended up choosing the Daylite > the DL Plus, Nike Running backpack, and Deuter Speedlite 20.

First let me note the ways these 2 diff. Osprey models differ: The Daylite Plus is different from Daylite in the following ways:
--it has a little bit of rubber in the shoulder straps (nicer IMHO)
--bigger volume capacity (20L vs. 13L)
--it features a padded internal laptop sleeve, whereas the Daylite only has a thin little bit of nylon
--it has a front “grab” pouch that could be handy

--1 negative point of comparison: the water bottle holders are not effective/ too droopy on the Daylite Plus (This is not a problem with the Daylite, as the cinch strap is connected to the mesh and helps to tighten the mesh opening on the sides).

The Daylite was the second lightest and best-fitting of others that I tested. (By comparison, the Nike Running Backpack was better fitting but had no external pockets for carrying keys, wallet, etc, while the Deuter Speedlite 20 was too bulky in the shoulder straps). The shoulder and waist straps of the Daylite series fit perfectly on my runner's frame (5'11" / 155 lbs). I really wish Osprey featured one key design innovation used by Nike: loops in which to tuck away shoulder straps and waist straps (see pics). All bookbags should allow you to hide / secure the shoulder and waist straps so they do not flap in the wind as you hike / jog. The material felt relatively water resistant and the zippers were snappy and responsive.

As I said, i had a particular purpose for this bag that is not quite what it was designed for. I needed it to carry stuff to and from road races while traveling on subway and ferry--a bag that would allow for some organization but also enable me to comfortably run a short distance (1-2 miles) to the start line if I was running late. This was the best bag I have found to serve this specific purpose.

reviews.body:
Overall the bag was about the right size for a day pack during a recent vacation /cruise trip. As others have noted the bottom straps and lack of ability to store them when not using is annoying although can tie them up or zip tie them if never using. However, the strap webbing connection points could be improved since the chest strap (which I only used a few times) broke after about 7 days use. The sewing of the strap onto the plastic hook wasn't complete so the nylon separated and fell off. The side water bottle holders are also large with no easy way to cinch them up. So anything like the size of a soda/water bottle will fall out. A few more pockets on it would have been nice as well.

All in all would have kept the bag if the strap hadn't failed but at this price point the quality and design need improvements.

I still like it for hiking because it has room for a camel pack, so I can store water there, and I can store a few misc. items inside the backpack as well as a light jacket, but it's just not a very versatile backpack. I wore it around the city when traveling around Paris and London, and it was okay. I wish I could have stored a water bottle in the side mesh, and I wish I could more comfortably pack my items into the pack without feeling so lopsided. I am going to keep it, and keep using it for daytime travel as it is still a sturdy and well made pack. It's just not as convenient as most Osprey products are.

reviews.title: Comfortable, good size, well worth it
reviews.body: I really like this backpack. I’ve been using it on my daily walks to carry my water bottle, wallet, phone, and other miscellaneous items. Very comfortable, good size, and the chest strap relieves any excess pressure on my back or shoulders so even after 14 miles I feel fine.

reviews.title: Five Stars
reviews.body: Very comfortable and lightweight

reviews.title: OK as a hiking day pack, not so good for touring.
reviews.body: bought it to strap on to a Porter 46 bag.  Could really use some organization - even if just a pen holder.  I know it's geared more for a hiker, but if you're using it in conjunction with a Porter 46 and taking this one out on the streets with you, some more organization is a must.

reviews.title: Never thought a backpack could feel so good!
reviews.body: I needed a lightweight backpack for short hikes. My main concern was would a water bladder fit, I have a 2 litter bladder and it fit perfectly, though it didn't have a place for the mouth attachment up front, I resolved this issue with a velcro strap I already had. In addition to the water, I carried sunscreen, lip balm, snacks, rain poncho, lightweight jacket, sunglasses, and iPhone.  I still had room for anything else I might need.  I suffer shoulder issues from two previous surgeries and this pack didn't bother me a bit. I like that it has both chest and waist straps, so it is very secure as you move about. First Osprey purchase as I am new to hiking, and would consider an upgrade as my skill set improves.

reviews.title: Perfect small backpack
reviews.body: Its perfect, lightweight and all you need for a usual day or light hiking.

reviews.title: Multi-Use Day-Pack
reviews.body: Great little backpack. I mainly use it as my camera bag and it works great!! Looking forward to many years from my Osprey

reviews.title: Its like Marry Poppins magic bag!
reviews.body: I love my Osprey Daylite. I was really hesitant about the shoulder straps and water bottle pouches everybody was complaining about but it doesnt bother me at all and my water bottles have never fallen out. Its like the magical bag in Mary Poppins honestly. No matter what I pack in it never seems to be completely full.

reviews.title: Uncomfortable for short people
reviews.body: This is the second Osprey pack I've had this problem with, the handle on the back sits too high up, actually goes onto the back of my neck. It presses into my neck in such a way that I am unable to keep my head straight. Instead, I need to look slightly down. No matter how I adjust it, I can't get it to fit better. The same exact thing happened with the Osprey Poco child carrier, so I think Osprey is just not great for people my size. For reference, I'm only 5'1 and have a short torso. Anyone else who has this issue might want to try Kelty or Deuter, those two seem to fit me much better.

reviews.title: Perfect pack for day hike, base camp to summit or carry on.
reviews.body: Never thought such a small pack could do so much. I packed 4 days of tshirts shorts 1 jacket  basic hygiene items as my carry on bag and was set for the week. I bought a compression bag and was able to get more in the pack. It's my gym pack now also. I've climbed many mountains,  Shasta, Whitney, Split  Mountain. OSPREY is a top quality product. I 100% support OSPREY

reviews.title: Too small
reviews.body: Great design, premium material but is smaller than expected.

reviews.title: Great Day Hiker
reviews.body: Perfect for day hikes. Osprey quality at a reasonable price. Well constructed with several compartments. These are very comfortable and fully adjustable. Have had one for several years and it goes with us several times a week throw some pretty tough country. They are not indestructible but so far it has held up well. I just purchased another for my wife and she loves it. Only complaint is that it is not waterproof nor does it come with a rain sleeve. Definitely recommend.

reviews.title: It’s Navy Blue, Not Black!!!!
reviews.body: This pack is navy blue and grey, not black as described/pictured. If you are looking for a great fitting day pack in navy blue, then look no further.

reviews.title: Couldn't Hold Anything
reviews.body: The only reason I'm okay with giving this bag one star is because the bag/fabric seems to be durable. However, the bag was so small, I couldn't fit anything. I was debating if I should bring a backpack to Thailand or just my purse. I decided on this backpack. I could have fit the same amount in my purse. The inside of this bag has absolutely no room. I could barely zip it up when I put some clothes and toiletries in the bag for a quick overnight excursion. I would have been better off using a plastic grocery bag. Also, the water bottle holders on the sides are absolutely terrible. The water bottle would immediately fall out. I lost so many water bottles trying to put them on the side. The water bottle holder was one of the main reasons I chose the bag instead of the purse and that was more of a hassle than just carrying it. I wish I could return it and get a refund but unfortunately, I used it for two weeks in Thailand so I doubt I'll be able to get a refund.

reviews.title: AWESOME PACK
reviews.body: great storage but not too big - perfect day pack, plus it has the spot for camel back!

reviews.title: strong, lightweight and compact
reviews.body: Excellent day pack. Perfect size, light, and folds up very small when not in use.

reviews.title: Great every day commuter bag, or perfect day pack
reviews.body: Great commuter bag! Compact but still fits my 15” MacBook

reviews.title: Hiking Daypack
reviews.body: Awesome hiking backpack! Lightweight, but with tons of storage.

reviews.title: Great Backpack!!
reviews.body: Great backpack. Perfect for short hikes.

reviews.title: Five Stars
reviews.body: Very nice quality and functional for my day time needs.

reviews.title: too small
reviews.body: I am not a big guy.  This bag is very small.  Plus the pocket on top is perfect for my wallet then next thing you know my friend finds my wallet on the ground.  Slipped right out had no idea.

reviews.title: Five Stars
reviews.body: Small but good carry everything I need for camping day

reviews.title: Very well designed pack
reviews.body: I'm not one for reviews, but this pack is legit. I broke it in on a simple day hike. The pack fits to your body perfectly with Zero movement while walking. The water bottle holder is deep with clips to further restrain the bottle. Very well thought out. Get this pack.

reviews.title: Seems like an overall good day pack
reviews.body:
I like this bag a lot. I waffled for a while between the daylite plus and the original and ended up going w the original. For me this bag is for day hikes, a travel carry on, etc so I didn’t need the extra storage of the plus. I’m also somewhat petite and the plus seemed to look so much larger on women’s backs.

I added a pic of the stone gray color because it is a bit more blue than the stock photo lends.

I am 5’3”, 118lbs and don’t find the handle at my neck to be diggy. It definitely touches the base of my neck but wasn’t a big problem for the 3 mile hike I first wore this for. Regarding a water bottle falling out the side pocket.. I can definitely see this being an issue. But I just slid the strap through the cap holder of my Nalgene and it was fine. More cumbersome than just grabbing the bottle for a drink but isn’t a deal breaker.

reviews.title: Best pack!
reviews.body: Wish I bought it sooner. You pay for quality, and this is itS This backpack is perfect for day trips. It’s comfortable for long hikes as the design redistributes the weight. No pulling on my shoulders! It had the best zipper pulls of any pack I have had. I love that it has a chest strap if I ever do put a lot of weight in it.

reviews.title: Love this Backpack!
reviews.body: Perfect backpack - well made!  I gave each of my sons one to use for Boy Scouts and these are SO well made.  Great for day hikes.

reviews.title: Very good, with some flaws
reviews.body: It's hard to find a full-featured *small* backpack--even this one is a little big for what I wanted, but it's the best I've found so far. It has a lot of great features. The shoulder straps are shaped and padded, and the sternum strap is adjustable and comfortable. The padded back panel gives the bag structure and keeps items from poking you in the back. The main compartment has a stretch pocket against the back panel, which is good for a hydration bladder or anything thin-ish that you want to find easily. The small outer zip pocket is great, with mesh pockets and enough depth to carry small items like keys, cell phone, sunglasses, tissues, etc. The side mesh pocket are nice and deep, but are oddly shaped and a little too big to securely hold water bottles when you take the pack off, or bend over while wearing it. This is one of two main complaints I've read about this bag. I've solved this problem by using a safety pin to make one pocket smaller, and it has worked pretty well. As long as the bottom of the main compartment is packed with something squishy, the bottle is snug in the pocket. The other main complaint I've read is about the built-in grab handle rubbing the back of people's necks. This hasn't been a problem for me, though I think it's because I don't use the waist strap. It does seem to be an odd design choice, since it isn't standard on their other packs. My biggest complaint about the bag is that it doesn't sit upright on its own when you take it off. I realize this is a design feature of hiking packs to keep the load close to your body, but I'd love to have a full-featured bag that could sit upright when I take it off for day-to-day use. So overall it's a well-made pack with great features, but just a few tweaks would make it perfect.

reviews.title: Great
reviews.body: Luv it

reviews.title: Perfect for day hikes
reviews.body: Excellent pack! Lightweight, and sized to contain everything needed for day hikes. Side pockets easily hold my 26 oz. Kleen Kanteen water bottle. Pack is sturdy and designed to keep my back from getting sweaty on warm days. I thought I would remove the waist strap but fi d it and the chest strap very comfortable for me (5'5", 125 lbs). Well made. I would definitely  buy again.

reviews.title: Lightweight and the perfect size when you don't need a full on backpack.
reviews.body: This backpack is perfect for use when travelling and sight seeing.  The compartments allow for finding items with ease.  It is also great for an everyday commuting bag.

reviews.title: A great day pack, but my order never came.
reviews.body: Well,  the "black" color is actually more like dark blue, other than that I love the backpack!  My order never actually arrived...so I bought it from REI!  Thanks REI!

reviews.title: Great for long one day hikes
reviews.body:
Perfect for long hikes. Keeps your back dry and very comfortable. Straps are sturdy enough to attach your camera or other gear. I needed a backpack that was large enough for a 3-8 hour hike but light and comfortable.
Would not recommend this as a pack that you throw into your suitcase for travel. The cooling vent makes it a little bulky. I would go with the Osprey Dayhike pack that will fit flat in the suitcase.

reviews.title: Best everyday UNIVERSAL day pack I’ve ever owned!!!
reviews.body:
It is just right for an outdoor 1 day adventure such as a trip to the beach or hiking or exploring on vacation, with enough room for your lunch & two large liquid vessels of at least 1 L each, and extra jacket or a towel & flip-flops, sunscreen, hat, first aid kit, etc.

For commuting, you can carry a 13 inch laptop with chargers, a notebook, etc.., plus your lunch, snacks & liquids. Light stuff jacket.

It is perfect as your personal item when traveling by air, as it held my 11” MacBook Air, iPad mini 4, charging cords and mobile charger, magazine, a light jacket, travel pillow, several snacks and two liquid vessels for hot and cold drinks.. I also had a small clear bag for travel size toiletries. The small embossed 2nd pocket can hold wallet, passport, keys, lip balm, gum, mints, hand sanitizer, etc., easily.

Small enough to fit anywhere, simple design, rain cover deploys in 3-5 seconds, strong design with light internal frame. Backpacks this size without an internal frame, can only hold about half as much weight. Warning: I am 6 foot 1, 220 lb. fit build, 48” chest & 34-36” waist. If you are much bigger than that, this might not be the right bag for you to wear, unless you plan to hand carry, mostly. It just fits me.
Great bag I use everyday for everything!!!

reviews.title: Great ventilation on a useful sized day bag
reviews.body: The sprung back is the best ventilation system on rucksacks and it's unusual to find it on a smaller day bag. Highly recommended. Can easily accommodate a jacket, fleece, water bottles & snacks.

reviews.title: Amazing pack
reviews.body: Bought a cheaper pack on here at first and immediately returned after my first hike (the brand was Teton). This one fits amazingly well. It’s very lightweight. The straps fit and feel perfect. I love the updated feature on the back to help with airflow. I’m 5’3 135ish for reference. I saw this pack in store for $100 so it’s a good deal to order on here. It does not come with a hydration pack but for the price being cheaper on here, that was fine. I ordered the Teton hydration pack. My boyfriend bought a larger Osprey, the Stratos 24 and it’s awesome as well. I could carry it for a longer hike too because the straps adjust based on your height. Safe to say that I’m sticking with Osprey. 👍🏼

reviews.title: Highly recommend!
reviews.body: Great pack, good amount of storage, convenient pockets, and awesome durability

reviews.title: Lightweight
reviews.body: Just arrived this morning. I like the color, perfect for being visible outdoors. Very light and it comes with a bright green rain cover. Very excited to add this to my gear.

reviews.title: Perfect day hike size
reviews.body: Was given as a gift on their list.  I have the 20L and am very happy with it, so I know they will be happy for shorter hikes instead of using the 40L that was used for long day hikes.

reviews.title: Great pack
reviews.body: I love this pack. I wanted something that was off my back and this was perfect. Very roomy, I just wish it had more pockets. Note that this does have a frame, which I didn't realize before I bought it. I was hoping to be able to take this in my backpacking pack for day hikes, but it doesn't fit since it has the frame. But it is perfect for day hikes.

reviews.title: Like it
reviews.body: a small lightweight bag

reviews.title: Perfect
reviews.body: Haven’t used this back yet, but I can tell I will love it. Super well made and light backpack. Has just the right space for daily hikes!

reviews.title: H
reviews.body: Perfect for our trip out west. Used for all our hikes in the National parks

reviews.title: Perfect off trail/foraging pack
reviews.body:
I really like this pack. I went with the shiitake one.
Not a coincidence but I use it when I'm mushroom hunting.
It is comfortable and fits great. I also like that such a small pack has mesh webbing to keep it off of your back.
It holds just enough for a good day out in the woods.
I can pack a 2.5 bladder, an extra layer, a small hammock, some food/snacks, my ditty bags for foraging, an extra water bottle, a small toaks titanium stove in a 900 ml pot, and other small items.
I went with a previous reviewers idea and attached a zip organizer to the top. It really helps.

It is small enough to not get in the way when I am off trail which is most of the time.
It moves well with me when I'm ducking branches, dodging thorns, and hopping over small creeks, rocks, or logs.
If packed right it holds a deceptively large amount for an 18l backpack with a full hydration bladder.
I can tie my ditty bags to the backpack when full. A drawstring cheapo rucksack can also be worn and fits perfectly over the pack too.

Anyway,

It is light and comfortable.
It holds enough to get me through the day and back home.
It moves well with me and doesn't mess with my mobility.
The frame and mesh keep it from bouncing and hitting me. So much more comfortable than simple padding.
It distributes weight well and can almost be forgotten about.
Holds a deceptively large amount for 18l even with a full hydration bladder.
Great for when you need agility off trail.
It has a raincover.

Awesome mushroom hunting and foraging pack.

reviews.title: Good day pack
reviews.body: The internal frame is a unique feature for a day-hike size pack and really makes this pack easy to wear all day without being uncomfortable.

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.body: I have three Osprey backpacks now and they're all great.

reviews.title: Convenient to carry
reviews.body: The osprey bag is perfect for day trips, travelling on planes and to just carry around items that are needed for the day.  The added feature of pulling the pack away from the back is great for keeping my back dry.

reviews.title: These backpacks are incredible!!
reviews.body: From college students to serious outdoorsmen, these are the BEST!!  They hold up to all of the heavy wear and tear for years!!  One of my sons used his in high school for HEAVY books, backpacking on the weekends, and the same during his college years.  It finally developed a tear i the hem and he mailed it back to Osprey and they repaired it to be as new!  You can not beat it!!

reviews.title: Osprey quality never disappoints
reviews.body: Bought this for my daughter for a trip to the Ape Caves. I have Osprey mountain biking pack, hiking pack and running pack. The quality is amazing and I will always buy Osprey whenever I need a pack.

reviews.title: Five Stars
reviews.body: Works great and feels great.

reviews.title: Highly recommend for any day hikes
reviews.body:
Used this during a recent stay in Banff NP and couldn’t have been happier with my purchase.
The rain jacket covering on the bottom is a tremendous touch. I put it on the bag at the first drop of rain and it didn’t leak.
I wish the bag itself might have had one more outer compartment but I was still able to fit everything inside that I needed to.
The outside bottom pockets allow for either a Nalgene water bottle or 2 plastic water bottles for each slot.
The biggest savior of this bag compared to other hiking backpacks that I’ve tried is that it has a mesh back support so no matter what you pack weight wise inside, it always feels like your shoulders and back aren’t getting dragged on.

reviews.title: Good bag with a familiar problem
reviews.body:
This is a good bag, works well and is durable. Very comfortable. All the space you would need for an all day hike or day out with the kids.

I'm giving this 4 stars because, like almost every other backpack ever made, water bottles cannot be taken in and out of the side pockets unless you are a contortionist. It is astonishing that we could put people on the moon 50 years ago but still seem to be unable to make a backpack with accessible side pockets. With this bag the pockets have just enough angle to allow your bottles to fall out when you bend over but not enough for you to actually get to them.

reviews.title: Fits more than you'd think
reviews.body:
I fully expect to fit a 2L reservoir, food and extra clothes for two for a full day hike, no problem.
The straps are super comfortable for medium to smaller men's frame. The air mesh suspension is as good as advertised and better than any pack that doesn't have it.
If considering the 26: though it's just an inch longer and fits a ton more practical room, it's really not necessary for day hiking and effectively minimizes the weight, comfort.

reviews.title: Nice
reviews.body: Quality. Extremely light. Perfect for short day hike

reviews.title: Nice backpack. Color is lighter than pictured
reviews.body: The color is lighter than it shows on the picture but it's not a deal breaker. I still like the backpack. I have a used a couple times since purchase and it is good. I will probably buy the larger size for longer hikes. I recommend it!

reviews.title: Poorly made for Osprey
reviews.body: Waist straps are the old kind that does not stay put. If Osprey had used their newer waist straps that tighten by the hip I would have kept this pack. Sent it back because it did not live up to Osprey's standards.

reviews.title: Awesome pack
reviews.body: This is an awesome little pack.  It’s little but that is what I wanted.  It’s really comfortable and breathable.  It does have ridged supports in it so don’t expect to fold it up in a little ball.

reviews.title: Love it, but don’t wear with a favorite t-shirt
reviews.body: This pack it perfect, except for one problem-where the mesh back covers the frame at the bottom corners, it causes pilling on T-shirts. I tried sewing up some pieces to fit over the straps and cover the corners, it’s not super classy but gets the job done - it’s just a shame that that was necessary.

reviews.title: Great Day Pack
reviews.body: Osprey makes great packs that we often use for backpacking trips.  We were looking for a good daypack for carrying essentials while hiking with our dog.  This pack works great for my wife and she hardly notices that she is wearing it.  The included rain cover is a nice addition also.  She loves this pack so much that she won't let me use it.  Very light weight.

reviews.title: Perfect day hike pack
reviews.body:
I've done about a 100 miles of hiking with this pack so far, and I'm quite happy with my purchase. No issues, great quality, perfect size for day pack. accommodates a hydration bladder well if you use one. A+

Edit: Oct. 2019 - I think I love this pack even more than I did a year ago. I day hike 3-4 times a week for a total of about 22 miles a week. I reckon I've got at least 1500 miles with this pack and I haven't had a single issue. Talk about quality.

Edit: Dec. 2021 - Still going strong with over 4000 miles of rough, all season use. 😃👍

reviews.title: Great price, light weight and love the cavity fir water bladder
reviews.body: Light weight and great fit for 185 lb, 5’ 8” male

reviews.body: I was looking for a lightweight bag with ventilation, and this is it. One superficial qualm: I wish the colors were more muted. The Kumquat Orange looks like a gentle, almost burnt orange on my browser (which I prefer), but in reality it's even beyond kumquat level brightness. Hope the sun and dirt will tone it down within a couple of hikes.

reviews.title: Light enough for a day hike
reviews.body: Just enough pockets to carry my important stuff

reviews.title: Used it for half dome!
reviews.body: I love this pack! Use it on my day hikes and even used it hiking to half dome. I chose this one because of the back style which is very comfortable and cooling and also because it was the only small affordable osprey I could find with trekking pole loops. Would definitely recommend!

reviews.title: Great Daypack
reviews.body: This backpack is not hot on my back, holds a lot of water and is perfect for a day trip. Best day pack I’ve had.

reviews.title: Carries what I need
reviews.body: I was looking for a day pack to bring a few things on hikes, especially my Nalgene bottle. I’m impressed with the size of this bag because it looks smaller but can hold more than what I need. The best part is that I can keep my 32oz Nalgene in the side pocket for quick access and for a longer hike, there’s another pocket on the other side so I could take 2 if needed! I also liked how it didn’t make my shirt ride up my back like plain old back packs have.

reviews.title: The PERFECT daypack!!
reviews.body: I purchased this backpack for a full day hike and it was absolutely perfect. It held all of my items with ease and I barely ever felt it was there. The special features like the built in rain cover, the soft lined pocket for your phone, the clasp for your keys, and the wide side pockets that hold my 40 oz water bottle perfectly all make this an amazing backpack. Do not hesitate, buy this backpack now. It’s comfort, durability, and versatility are unmatched!!

reviews.title: Comfort
reviews.body: Love this backpack! Been hiking lately and it is very light and easy to adjust on my back! Love the two pockets on the sides so i can put coffee in one and water bottle in the other. Might have to get another color as well.

reviews.title: Great product
reviews.body: Meets all my expectations

reviews.title: Raincoat!
reviews.body: Comfortable and light. And the attached raincoat kept everything safe and dry during our inaugural hike with the pack.

reviews.title: Very comfortable but lacks organization
reviews.body:
The backpack is very comfortable and the mesh back panel is nice.
However the side mesh pockets are loose and water bottles will slip out. The top zipper pocket is also poorly placed. When the backpack was not full the contents in the top zipper pocket would bounce around causing a vibration on your back since there was no support.

reviews.title: not good for me........
reviews.body: this pack is great but with a hard frame not good for me.  i only do day hikes so i do need lots of storage.  i have moved on to a frameless pack.  but time will tell.

reviews.title: Light and comfortable
reviews.body: This is a great lightweight day pack. Very comfortable to wear on a medium female frame, 5'8" 150.

reviews.title: Works alright - but shoulder strap padding is too thin, and your shirts will pill badly
reviews.body: Works alright for day hikes, for sure, but the shoulder strap padding is too thin (first time using, at the end of a strenuous five-hour hike at altitude carrying a full pack (mostly water and snacks, and extra layers), my shoulders hurt and the skin over my collar bones were bruised - never in my life have I experienced that with a backpack before) and the pack itself makes your shirts pill badly around the lower back.  I ruined a bunch of t-shirts on a recent trip.  I'm actually worried about carrying this pack while wearing a more expensive jacket or rain shell.  It might damage those items too.  Seems there's no way around that.

reviews.title: Traveled to Australia this past year and the black Lullumon ...
reviews.body: Traveled to Australia this past year and the black Lullumon backpack was a sweaty mess. This arrival is welcomed, compact and organized and a mesh set up to keep the pack from being saturated with sweat in high temps. Hiking Tallulah Gorge with this puppy

reviews.title: Will buy one of each color !!
reviews.body: Great all day pack , for all terrains and ocassions

reviews.title: Best one yet
reviews.body: Perfect weight, one day or overnight pack. Super durable w a rain cover and mesh back preventing from a sweaty back. As a female the front strap fit perfect over my chest, not on the chest /breast or under which has been an issue for me charcoal color great, yellow will allow for easy identifying amongst other dark backpacks when traveling. Happy hiking.

reviews.title: Nice small pack
reviews.body: Nice for everyday use. Like that it has a removable waist strap. I removed mine as it's not really needed on this small pack. Much tidier without it.

reviews.title: Versatile hiking pack
reviews.body: Comfortable on my shoulders, will hold enough for my kids and I for a day hike on vacation, but not so big that I can’t take it on a short hike locally too.

reviews.title: Used as a overnight/day pack
reviews.body: LOVED this bag!  I'm a mom with 4 kids and I used it while we traveled Paris and Rome.  It was lightweight and comfortable for the ALL day walking we did.  I was able to pack one outfit, swimsuit, ipad, chargers, water bottle in the main compartment with room to spare and the small zippered pouch at the top of the pack fit my wallet, passport, chapstick, hand sanitizer, and phone.  The straps never cut into my shoulders and when it started feeling heavy I utilized the clips around the shoulders and waist to distribute the weight and I could go for another few hours.

reviews.title: LOVE THIS!
reviews.body: Love this pack!! Used it for the first time for half dome. It was perfect, held enough snacks, and water. And yes it is compatible with a a camel bak bladder! And the breathable back of the pack was a life saver!!!

reviews.title: Nice basic pack, not likely for rugged camping/hiking
reviews.body:
LOVE the back frame and how it lets air through when hiking. Less sweat on my back. 🙌🏻
What I dont like is the lack of compartments. Its really just one big area. I prefer to sort things, especially when using as a carry-on. The larger version of this pack has an outside stuff compartment, so I ordered both. After seeing them side by side, the minimal amount that could fit in the outside area was not worth the price difference, imo.
Osprey makes quality products. I bought this primarily for light summer hiking and it is good for that, but not great. When using water bottles instead of the bladder, they do fall out of the side pockets when I bend over. Super annoying. Still trying to figure that out. The side pockets are large for ‘stuff’, but not meant for a water bottle. It could use a drawstring to cinch them closed tighter based on what is in the pocket. I lost a pair of sunglasess in RMNP when I bent over as well.
It is good looking though and comes in some beautiful colors- the blue and green especially. No hip belts. Keep that in mind-might be a deal breaker for some. Its a casual pack, not an off the grid pack.

reviews.title: Great for hiking
reviews.body:
Tough good quality hiking backpack.
This is not athletic gear that I would consider appropriate for casual use. I would not use this as a school backpack, for example. This is for actual hikers.
If that is you, this is great. Five stars.

reviews.title: Great pack good cost
reviews.body: Great pack as advertised

reviews.title: Comfortable and fits well
reviews.body: The backpack only has 2 pockets plus a little rain fly pocket. Would have been nice to add pockets on the waist belt and maybe extra front pocket too.

reviews.title: Tiny, overpriced, with too few pockets
reviews.body: Tiny, overpriced, with too few pockets

reviews.title: Most comfortable personal item sized backpack I have ever used but needs better organization
reviews.body:
So let me first start off by saying that the reason this bag only gets 4 stars is because of the organization. They only give you 3 zippered compartments. The main, the small on on the top maybe large enough for a phone or eye glass case then the one on the bottom for the rain guard if you should even count that. I understand that this is a hiking bag but why not give us a large ziped compartment on the front where we can put some small things or atleast some internal zip pouch that can be used for things like passports.

The bag is easily the most comfortable personal item sized backpack I have ever used. Its light weight and the frame helps a ton for support and adds almost no weight. The waist straps are removable and leave a clean look when removed can be used for attaching some gear or hanging bottle.

I was also looking at the day light, daylight plus, day light travel, one because they attach to the larger packs and the daylight travel is larger then this bag and has the organization I crave. But there all missing this awesome frame this is why in the end I went with the hike lite.

To add some organization to the bag I purchased the Osprey UltraLight Zip Organizer and attached it to the top of the bag with some clips (See my photos). This gave me an great use of the top part of this bag and taking everything out of the front pouch that caused it to sag and not really look nice when the bag was empty. I will mostly be using this for travel and very light hiking I can fit 2 or 3 light jackets/hoddies or one heavy jacket with this set up. I hope this is helpfull to some others.

reviews.title: A great, lightweight pack that is everything you would expect from Osprey
reviews.body:
This is a great, high-quality, lightweight backpack.
I have the Shiitake Grey color, which is beautiful - a cool bluish-grey, which is not the color of any shiitakes I've ever seen, with soft lime yellow (not quite lime, not quite yellow) accents. I love the colors which are a nice change from the usual, either boring or ugly colors that serious backpacks usually come in.
This pack offers just about everything I want out of a day hike pack. The included, integrated rain cover is great - my old pack did not have that...and it's a feature that would have been welcome on any number of occasions. (It rain cover is bright green.)
The inside sleeve for a water reservoir/hydration pack also gets a big thumbs-up.
The suspension mesh panel on the back is to prevent sweating and is therefore a most welcome feature, but in the current winter weather, I've not had a chance to see how well that works but it certainly looks like it will allow air to circulate in that area.
Lots of hooks for carabiners and walking sticks.
Chest and (removable) hip straps.
The product description says it weighs 1.49 pounds, but it really feels much lighter than that to me.

Bottom line: I love this backpack.

reviews.title: The suspension alone makes this pack worth checking out!
reviews.body: The trampoline suspension works incredibly well keeping my back dry on hikes. The material is lightweight but incredibly thin to where on the orange pack, if its packed full you can see what's pressing up against it. The rain cover is a nice touch to have since if this got wet, it would be soaked instantly. I have the Daylite pack too and the problem with that one is the side pockets design is horrible to where everything falls out. The side pockets on this pack is deep and holds things in place. Overall, very good pack!

reviews.title: Short hikes
reviews.body: Tired of carrying water bottles in hand and a cross body bag. First pack I’ve bought and went on a 3.5 mile hike. Bought an Osprey 2L hydration bladder to go with this. I’m 5’8, 200lbs and had no issues. Need to get more usage out of it but I feel like it’s still going to be a good pack. Love the hydration pack also.

reviews.title: zipper jammed after 5 months of light use, holding my house keys hostage :(
reviews.body:
After 5 months of minimal use, the zipper to the front pocket jammed shut with only 1 cm opening to try to get things out. I discovered my house keys were now being held hostage in this pocket after working a 16 hour shift in the ER. I was exhausted and just wanted to go inside my house and sleep. But nope, couldn't open the stupid backpack's pocket to get the keys. Ended up driving to a gas station nearby to borrow scissors and cut open the pocket as 15 minutes of trying to unjam the zipper proved futile.

Yes Osprey brags a lifetime warrantee on their products, but I now get to ship the pack back to them AT MY EXPENSE, and then wait 4-6 WEEKS for them to either fix the broken zipper & subsequent damage inflicted SOLELY because the zipper was stuck, or to replace the pack. That's not such a great customer service experience. Just saying.
