reviews.body: I use it everyday for work and hiking on the weekend. It's a great small pack and a welcome addition to my Osprey Atmos 65. Just wish there was a more effective way to rein in the clip straps when not in use, then tend to get in the way.

reviews.title: Great day pack
reviews.body: It’s perfect for my day hikes. Holds a 3L water bladder. Very comfortable. Place to keep your trekking sticks also.

reviews.title: Backpack for vacation!
reviews.body: Daughter used this in Europe and loved it! Easy to carry and water repellent

reviews.title: Very light, superb ventilation, fairly comfortable, major shirt pilling
reviews.body: I really wanted to love this pack. It's lightweight, fairly comfortable and I absolutely love the airspeed ventilation system on the back, which lived up to the hype. After a 12 mile hike in mild conditions, my shoulders/back felt completely dry.  However, I had mixed feelings about the frame. It seemed a little much for such a small pack, but perhaps necessary for the awesome ventilation system. The bottom corners curve out a bit, so I tightened the straps to make it sit higher on my back to prevent the corners from rubbing against my hip bones. I'm a pretty lanky individual (5'11" ~160 lbs), but the frame felt a bit narrow and seems like it would be ideal for a smaller individual. There's a seam where thicker material connects to the mesh on the lower back. That in combination with the bottom corners where the frame sticks out caused major shirt pilling. Despite being fairly lightly packed, after just a single hike, the brand new shirt I was wearing showed substantial wear on the two spots on the back where the pack frame sticks out. This issue (pilling shirts) was one of the main reasons I've been looking from my old pack which was made from cheaper materials. Unfortunately, it appears this pack may be worse than my last one in that regard.

reviews.title: No sweat.
reviews.body: I like the mesh suspension that keeps it off of my back.  No sweat and nothing poking me.  I prefer frame full-sized backpacks for this reason, too.  I've used this pack in desert cold and heat. 46 C..  but I like it back home for the same reason.  Water, in the 3rd world, even in cities, comes in plastic bottles (from plastic trees?) so it's really handy that the water bottle holders on this pack are right sized (not low rimmed like some packs)..

reviews.body:
I didn't know what to expect from this bag. This is my first hiking backpack and I love it! It's very slim but it fits a lot of stuff. I use this as my daily commuter bag. The side pockets expand nicely for my water bottle. The smaller pocket in the front i use for my keys and earbuds. Anything that I need quick, easy access to. The bigger pocket fits whatever I want. I eventually want to see if I can add a pair of shoes. Since I take public transpo to work, I walk a lot and want to wear my sneakers and put my work shoes in the bag. I don't think I could fit a pair of boots. I love the rain protector that's included but haven't had to use it yet.

I do plan on using it for hiking. Whenever I decided to finally try hiking. ;)

reviews.title: Pretty Durable, Very Versatile.
reviews.body:
I don't really consider myself to be very gentle with a lot of my outdoor equipment. That being said I've owned this pack for over 2 years and I've haphazardly thrown scissors and other hard pointy tools into the pockets and haven't had a hole yet. I've thrown a full jug of water in there and ran around some hillsides and never had the straps wear out. I've used it as a camelbak, day pack for hiking, and most recently as a fishing backpack (Although the lures and hooks were in containers and not just sitting in the bag). I think the most I had in the bag at one time was my hammock, 2 twenty foot ratchet straps, my rain fly, an E-tool, an extra fleece jacket, a 36oz water bottle in the side pocket, a poncho, and still had room for plenty of snacks and small misc gear.

For a fisherman's reference I can fit three 2x20x10in Plano lure organizers and still have room for a 2.5x3x5 inch trout and crappie box and my 2x3x5 inch fly box on top of that.

My favorite feature is the clips on either side of the backpack. You can use it to secure long items in the exterior side pockets or to simply compress the pack for a lower profile (this helps keep weight from shifting and somewhat helps keep the pack from getting caught on brush when hiking). I think I've used these little clips about 70-80% of the times I've taken the pack out. I've secured large fishing nets, large water bottles, small camping chairs, and fishing rods in the side pockets and used the clips to hold them down with no issue.

As long as it continues to be durable this pack is worth the money. It's not too bulky or too tiny and can be used however you want to use it.

reviews.title: Great pack for any occasion
reviews.body: So far I've gotten on two flights with this pack.  Super comfortable to stable.  Hitting the slopes with it next.

reviews.title: Fat people can hike with this.
reviews.body: I'm 6'1", weigh 280 lbs., and have struggled to find hiking gear that doesn't remind me that I don't "fit in" with the hiking crowd.  This bag does just that - it's light, offers good support, doesn't run up against my back, and is just the right size for my foray into hiking.  The straps are adjustable so they offer the proper support to take weight off your lower back and provide enough space so you don't feel crunched up or unnecessarily restricted.  My only complaint was the waist strap, which was not long enough (i.e. my gut not small enough) to fit around my waist.  However, the waist strap can be removed until you're in a position to fit into it.  Otherwise, this bag is perfect for day walking trips.

reviews.title: Great comfortable, quality daypack for petite stature
reviews.body: I had an Osprey daypack for several years before it got stolen. I liked it so much, I decided to replace it with the same thing. Although it is slightly different (the old one had a camel which I never used anyway), I like this new one even better. The best feature is the mesh back which creates an air pocket to reduce sweating; it also has a built-in rainfly. Every other pack I have ever owned or tried on was simply too big for me as I am under 5' tall. This one is perfect and very comfortable.

reviews.title: Lightweight, sturdy frame, keeps sweat away from back
reviews.body:
I am a regular day hiker doing 8-14miles. I bought this backpack for its design that allows very good ventilation on the back. No more sticky-sweaty backpack :) Easily carry a gallon of water, still has just enough space for a jacket and lunchbox. The metal frame keeps it well balanced. It features all the adjustments that one can desire, chest, shoulder and hip straps. All very well built. Chest strap has a built in whistle. It comes with a rain cover that stealthily goes into a zip pocket at the base, which also doubles up as a cushion.

Note: due to the sturdy frame, this backpack is not collapsible. You cannot fold it. This allows the bag to retain its shape and keeps weight balanced.

reviews.title: Good Day Pack
reviews.body:
This is an excellent pack. It is VERY lightweight. It does have an 18” tall frame inside, so it is a hard pack. There is a rain cover that stores in the bottom of the pack that covers the entire pack during rain. That cover does take up some space in this small pack, but it is removable if you need the space more than the rain cover.
The straps are ventilated padding. Very light, but also breathable. The frame holds the pack away from your back, so there is also ventilation behind your back and it keeps the pack a little off of you. There is a thin waist strap and chest strap. Both are on the thin side, but this pack isn’t going to be heavy enough to need to to be thicker.
This is not a long trip pack unless you happen to be an exceptionally light packer. And I mean exceptionally light. This is more of a day hike kind of pack. It is sized to be considered a “personal item” on an airplane. So, smaller than a carry on.

reviews.title: Lightweight nice pack
reviews.body: I used this on a slot canyon and it did really well. Has some wear from the sandstone but that's expected in that environment.  Great little pack!

reviews.title: Very comfortable pack with nice features.
reviews.body: Would have given this five stars if it weren't for the price. But the quality materials, construction, and lifetime warranty comes at a price. This pack is really comfortable. I've worn it on all day hikes and bike rides around Colorado Springs and nearby towns this past summer (in moderate heat) and the frame and mesh venting kept my back dry like no other pack I've ever used. The pack itself weighs next to nothing. The integrated rain cover (neatly stowed in the bottom zip compartment and easy to deploy when a sudden shower comes along) means the pack itself need never get wet, nor do its contents. I also have Osprey Momentum 32 day pack. (This 18L Hikelite is meant for my wife.) But unless I have a larger load to carry, I much prefer the Hikelite 18 pack to the Momentum 32.

It presses on my mid back and the bottom edge is curved in a concave way that is designed to spoon your back but the corners aren't wider than my back so they just press into it. I'll return this one for sure and maybe try the skarab hydration pack instead with no frame. It's a bummer because the ventilation on this would work well in Texas.

reviews.title: We use this as a diaper bag!
reviews.body:
We use this as a diaper bag because we are always on the go-go-go with the kids and needed something lightweight that could carry all our stuff! We usually carry two water bottles, one for each kid, a change of clothes for each kid, some diapers, some wipes, and some snacks and this pack can easily manage all that PLUS room for more all while being extraordinarily lightweight and comfortable to wear around. One of the best things is the side pouches for the water bottles. When you bend over to pick up ...I don't know whatever one of a million things your kid has dropped that you need to pick up...the water bottles stay secure in their pockets but they are accessible enough for a *quick* grab when you need it.

I can't say enough good things about this pack. It's slick looking, designed incredibly well, comfortable to wear, and functional....what more could you want?

Most backpacks that I've had have three zippered compartments going from small to large.  This has only two. I miss that small front one where I usually put my keys and phone.  It's not a big item and I should have examined the picture more carefully.  That said, the backpack is great.  The straps, zippers, and material are first rate.  This is the second Osprey I've owned.  My son claimed the first and after about five years he is still using it frequently.

reviews.title: Osprey Farpoint 40 Travel Backpack
reviews.body: This is the most comfortable and easy to use backpack I have ever owned.  It holds enough clothes/gear for me to go out traveling for 10 days!  It is easy to open and get to my gear as it is loaded from the side, instead of the top like most backpacking packs.  The shoulder straps are comfortable and fold away in a zippered pocket for easy carrying on planes or trains.  My husband and I both have these packs and have traveled with them extensively.  We are very happy with the quality, design, capacity and durability of the farpoint 40.  Thank you!

It was also difficult to use the front pocket when the rest of the backpack was full. So the shape of the backpack was kind of weird and a little difficult to work with. I still give 5 stars for the quality and fit. The waist support and the shoulder straps fit me very well. And this does fit in the overhead compartment on an airplane.

reviews.title: Awesome backpack for traveling!! Great carry on!
reviews.body: I bought this backpack before I took my first trip to the Philippines. I did a ridiculous amount of research and ended up going with the Osprey 40 and I'm very happy that I did. Fully packed, it won't slide under the seat in front of you if that's what you're shooting for but it does fit perfectly in the overhead compartment and I've never had a problem with it for carry on size in the United States or Asia. With this and a regular size backpack that will slide under an airplane seat, you can easily travel with everything you need for a long time with room for some small souvenirs along the way. It holds a 15" laptop and has padding for it also. I recommend purchasing some packing cubes to help save space. The compression straps both inside and outside the bag ensure that you can get the bag's profile as small as possible. You can also buy some extra straps to get the bag even more compressed if taking up as little space as possible is what you're going for. I have them and they do help compress the bag as much as physically possible. The bag has plenty of compartments and the main opening folds open like a regular suitcase which is really nice for packing and especially unpacking compared to a regular backpack. The super padded shoulder straps and waist support fold into the pack easily and quickly which is so useful, helpful, and downright ingenious. Handles located on the top and side gives you options when carrying the bag when it's not in backpack mode. This pack is really comfortable and the straps have a lot of padding. The extra support straps along the chest and waist make this thing a joy to carry, even fully loaded. My research paid off big time here because I am very happy with this purchase and feel that it's worth every penny spent on it. Two thumbs up and many kudos to the designers behind the Osprey packs. They obviously had the traveler in mind when designing this backpack. Couldn't be happier and will buy another one if my traveling needs change.

I'm 5'4", 120 lbs, and this just looks ridiculously large on my back (extends almost to the top of my head).  I'm a light packer and only traveling for weeks at a time (not months nor perpetually), so I don't need that much space, and I don't want to have to maneuver something this size through airports, etc.  I'll stick with my Swiss Gear Weekend Getaway (Hybrid) bag: it's small and sleek, and though it doesn't have a hip strap, it's  comfortable enough for the trips I take.

reviews.title: I was not disappointed. So glad I went with the 40 over ...
reviews.body: Purchased this bag after A LOT of research! I was not disappointed.  So glad I went with the 40 over the other larger sizes.  I'm a petite female & this bag fit me GREAT.  (I purchased the S/M).  To top it off, I used it for a 9 day trip to Panama.  I had plenty of room to SPARE & my finance was jealous of the innovative construction and the way the main compartment unzips in a suitcase fashion.  (I'm sure I'll be buying him one soon) :).  I know there were some negatives about the water bottle slots being not useful.  I used a carabiner/reusable bottle clipped to my bag when I wanted.  And I used the mesh pockets for a light sweater & my raincoat - for easy access.  After 6 flights, several cab & water taxi trips - this bag looks brand new.  I suspect it will continue to perform on our next trips. I utilized the zipper compartment to hide the straps/waist belt when I was forced to check my bag on the teeny planes.  That feature drew attention from strangers.  So nice not to worry about your straps being slung & tugged on in transit. Thanks Osprey & Amazon - wonderful product.

reviews.title: Looking forward to using it more!
reviews.body:
The fit was as expected: I'm a woman about 5'7 and dress size 2-4, and I got a small/medium. If you're much smaller than me you may have some trouble, but I think it will sit in the right places for most women.

I've so far only tested this on a domestic trip to Park City for skiing, but I bought it for a month-long European backpacking trip in the spring. I've read reviews on blogs and it seems that this backpack is one of the best, if not the best rated for short backpacking trips.

I will say that it was a huge mistake to put my ski boots in the bottom of the bag. It just isn't padded enough for something so hard against my back the whole time. I don't think that any shoulder straps could have reduced the pain from how heavy it was after everything else that I fit in it, too. I did manage to pack almost everything except for my skis and ski clothes in the backpack, including makeup bags, hats, two sweaters, my laptop, chargers, iPad, curling iron, socks, and underwear.

After I took the ski boots out I was very encouraged by how much volume I could fit into the bag and then compress with the straps on the outside. I'll update this review when I'm packed for Europe!

Also the main compartment is huge, but it would be improved slightly if there were loops inside for attaching carabiners. It would be nice if straps had retaining loops so there wasn't so many straps hanging.

Pros
Multi functional, can be used for urban tourism and for hikes.
Great support
Great cost to quality
Capacity
Meets most carryon requirements

Cons
Laptop pouch is in the front pocket
Backpack must be taken off partially to access water bottle pouch
Strap management is lacking

Summary
There are better hiking bags, and there are better dedicated carry ons, however, this bag surpassed being just a 'jack of all trades' and is closer to being a master of all trades.

reviews.title: but it was definitely a great trial run
reviews.body:
I did a lot of research on travel backpacks since I am going on a 20-day backpacking trip through Europe this summer. The Osprey Farpoint 40 was one of the top-rated packs I could find, so I decided to give it a try. I am 5'2" and 140 lbs, and this pack it me perfectly. Just trying it on, I knew that the support would be there. I just got back from a 7-day trip to the Philippines and took this pack with me. Obviously it was much easier packing for a 7-day trip than it will be for 20, but it was definitely a great trial run.

The pack opens up completely like a suitcase, which was a HUGE pro. I couldn't imagine getting my things from a top-loading bag. It would've been terrible and inconvenient. There are many convenient pockets to organize your things: passport, wallet, etc. I always knew where to look. This is also a big pro for me, because it is really easy for me to just throw things into a big bag with no organization. This pack made it easy to organize.

I packed a LOT of stuff in here. Way more than needed for a 7-day trip, but I was attending a wedding, so I fit makeup, three gowns, a curling iron, and heels in there in addition to my regular clothing. Definitely not bad considering I had everything I needed on my back! I have no doubts that this backpack will be perfect for my Europe trip. I'll be packing much simpler clothing, no makeup, and of course no curling iron (who has time to curl your hair at a hostel?), so I know that I'll make it for 20 days no problem.

Overall, I recommend this! Get the S/M if you're short like me. The weight was so beautifully distributed throughout my back/hips that it was never uncomfortable (this does require some packing planning on your part!). And the look of the bag as whole is not too flashy.

Love it!

I didn’t realize there’s a 7KG/15LBS limit for carry-ons. Mine overexceeded the limit by 5 pounds so I had to check it in. It’s super cool that the straps have a piece of material that goes over them so they don’t get ruined.

The black/dark grey color is really nice! My friend has the same pack and says the same.

The only thing I wish is that I could put my computer in a neoprene case before putting it in the designated spot. The way it’s made now, there isn’t enough room. I have a 15”.

Even though I shoved 20 lbs of stuff into my backpack and carried it around, it was comfortable.

Oh, one tip is: buy the rectangle eBag packing cubes. They fit perfectly in here. I wrote a review for them so you can easily find them if you click my name.

reviews.body: I ordered this because I was going to Iceland and wanted to avoid checking any bags. When this arrived, it was much bigger than I expected. While it looked like it had similar proportions to regular backpacks, it was very long. It reminded me of one of those hiking backpacks. But maybe I'm just bad at visualizing dimensions. I am a small person, so I felt that it would be too uncomfortable, was more space than I needed, and I was concerned that it wouldn't fit in the overhead compartment. The other issue I had was that when I got it, the shoulder straps were zipped inside. When I pulled them out, it appeared that the only way I could use them was to roll up the outer layer. There was a place to velcro the outer layer in at the bottom, but that meant that the side facing my back would have half a zipper along the border, which I found strange. It also took me about 20 minutes to figure out how it worked. I returned it and ended up going to Target, where I found a simple, traditional backpack for $25, which fit all of my stuff easily.

reviews.title: The perfect backpack for me
reviews.body:
I did a bunch of research on backpacks for petite female travelers who like to travel light. The 40 liter offsprey is by far the best option out there, in my opinion. I'm 5'3''/ 90 lbs and most travel backpacks are awkward for me to carry, as my body dimensions aren't "average". I saw a few other women (and men!) carrying this same model during my 3 months in south America, and everyone raved about how much they loved it. It's a high quality, durable product, it's got a simple/great design, the waist strap was always comfortable, and even when you pack it to capacity, it never feels too heavy. I like the zipper pulls because you can loop a lock cable through, and also it is a perfect carry-on size, it always fit in the overhead compartments (even in those ultra-low cost little airplanes). You have the option of hiding the back straps and using a provided shoulder strap to carry as a duffel.
Get yourself a couple of packing cubes, learn to travel with the basics and avoid carrying a 75 liter monstrosity thats just going to hurt your back. I can tell this b-pack will last me many more years, and when its time for an upgrade, I will be purchasing another one from this brand. Highly reccomend!

reviews.title: Seems like the best carry on pack out there!
reviews.body:
I haven't taken it on a trip with it yet so I will update after with a lengthy posting. I plan on doing 3-4 months in Southeast Asia and bought this bag to fit as a carry on in budget airlines. It was between this bag and the Osprey Porter 46 (or 45?), anyway... I chose this bag over the Porter for a couple reasons although it was very close.

I liked the Porter because it cradled my back a bit better whereas the farpoint has a plastic frame making it more sturdy but stiff, although it was not tested for extended time, again, I will update. Also, the Porter seemed to easier to pack a large amount of things, it's huge for a carry on.

I ended up going with the farpoint because I felt it would force me to pack smarter. You can fit everything you need in it but it make me not take that extra sweater and pair of shoes that I would inevitably take with the Porter. I like the internal cinch straps in the farpoint. The porter lacks these so if you have loose items in there they can shake around if not fully packed and cinched from the outside. The farpoint meets just about EVERY carry on dimensions whereas some airlines (I think Latam is one) the Porter is too big. The farpoint seemed to be made of a better material and looks more like a backpack instead of a carry on luggage with shoulder straps. Last, the farpoint has a mesh waterbottle holder on the outside.

In the end, if I bought the Porter I felt that I would need another smaller pack for short weekend trips. With the farpoint, I can use this backpack for every trip. Will update after my next trip but after testing both I really like the Farpoint.

reviews.title: I will stop wearing these when I am dead.
reviews.body:
These are my headphones. They don't break easily, they block out just enough of the outside world, the sound is good, and they're cheap enough to own several pairs so I'm not always searching for my headphones. Once I was on the bus and someone was being loud so I reached into my pocket to grab headphones and realized I was carrying 3 pairs of these with me. I love them.

I never thought I would actually write a review for them, though, until last night. I put several pairs of jeans through our old, hot, not-at-all-gentle washer and drier, and when I took my pants out of the drier I realized a pair of these headphones had been left in the pocket. I almost threw them out then and there, expecting they would be totally wrecked, but I decided to see if they still worked first. They did. Just as well as before. And now they're very, very clean, too. These things are like tiny warriors. I'm a convert for life.

reviews.title: DON"T BUY!! They TEST ON ANIMALS.
reviews.body:
Please boycott and look for products that do not tprture poor animals. It should be illegal.
-Over 100 million animals are burned, crippled, poisoned, and abused in US labs every year.
-92% of experimental drugs that are safe and effective in animals fail in human clinical trials because they are too dangerous or don’t work.
-Labs that use mice, rats, birds, reptiles and amphibians are exempted from the minimal protections under the Animal Welfare Act (AWA).
-Up to 90% of animals used in U.S. labs are not counted in the official statistics of animals tested. Take a stand by kidnapping your friends’ products that were tested on animals (seriously!).
-Europe, the world’s largest cosmetic market, Israel and India have already banned animal testing for cosmetics, and the sale or import of newly animal-tested beauty products.

Anyway, the coffee is good. It does have some subtle hints of Ethiopian coffee, but it's not quite as good. But that's fine as the Ethiopian coffee I've used in the past is about three times as expensive as this Peet's coffee, and it's still pretty darn close. I'm a big fan of medium or light roasts as I believe dark roast coffee A) tastes like burnt ash; and B) burns out some of the caffeine, which is not a good thing. This coffee doesn't have either of those issues. It's a nice, smooth flavor with a rich smell. It will wake you up.

Overall, this is a good little bag of coffee and I'd have no issues buying it again. Five stars.

reviews.title: Not packaged the same as we get from local grocers, and weaker
reviews.body:
Over the past several months, I've ordered four bags of the Big Bang medium roast. The price here on Amazon is a bit more than the sale price at local grocers, but less than the regular price, so I end up ordering online between the grocers' sales.

Based on the bags recently ordered, however, I'm having some doubt whether the product on order is the same as what's sold at the grocery. The bags are slightly but noticeably different. Bags from the grocery are neatly creased, and securely glued. The bags ordered online have have been assembled somewhat sloppily, all of them have leaked grounds into the shipping envelope, and one of them had a 1-1/2" tear. On the bags from the grocery, the "freshest by" and "roasted" dates are clearly printed in gold Roman-type font on the black background. On the bags from Amazon, those dates are dark gray on black, appear to be in a sans-serif font, and are readable only from an angle in strong light. The code numbers on the right side of the bag are distinct and completely readable on the bags from the grocery. The codes were about 50% worn off the online bags. The UPC is printed directly as part of the bag from the grocery, but it's a big sticker pasted onto the bottom of the online bags. Finally, it takes roughly 20% more grounds from the online bags to produce the same strength of brew I get from what we buy locally. The flavor seems to be the same, but definitely weaker.

reviews.title: Fresh, Flavorful, Distinct, Excellent Coffee!
reviews.body:
This review is for Peet’s Big Bang medium roast ground coffee, 18oz. I wasn’t sure what to expect. I typically do dark roast because I like a strong and bold flavor, but I was curious, and my experience of Peet’s coffee has always been great.

They describe this as a medium roast with a “vibrant blast of tropical fruit.” Sounds strange, but I was interested. Honestly, it would be weird to taste even a hint of fruit in coffee, but I honestly can never really detect any specific tasting notes in coffee anyway.

I never drink coffee black. It just isn’t my preference. I always use creamer. I did try a spoonful of this black and it was very good and flavorful. I’m satisfied with the strength for a medium coffee. This makes a very enjoyable cup with an interesting taste. I loved it with my dark chocolate almond creamer. The flavor is strong enough that I can still really taste it even after adding my creamer. I’m terrible at trying to describe coffee, but I haven’t had a cup of Peet’s coffee that I didn’t enjoy. Their coffee is never boring to me- always distinct and memorable.
The coffee was well packaged. It says it was roasted 10/15/20 and is freshest by 01/13/21. The coffee smells wonderful in the bag. I have absolutely no complaints. If you love medium roasted coffee, then definitely try this. I would still recommend it to try even if you usually prefer light or dark roast. If you somehow don’t like this kind or just want to try something else, I’m sure you’ll find something by Peet’s that you will love.
I hope my review was helpful in some way, and if so, I would love to know-thanks!

reviews.title: Deep dark and rich taste all day long.
reviews.body:
Peet’s makes the best dark roast coffee in both regular grind and K-Cups. Believe me I have tried many different coffee brands from medium, to dark to Italian/French and decaf dark roasts and nothing compares to this coffee. There is no bitter taste like most other dark roasts on the market. You get a smooth and deep coffee taste with every sip you take.
Major Dickson also made a decaf that had a terrific taste and no flavor was lost because of the decaf process. Now it’s just dark roast decaf and still terrific. Having had military coffee most of my life I got use to drinking coffee just black and sometimes the GI coffee had a lot to ge desired.
A true test of a good coffee is to make a pit in the morning and let the pot get cold or simmer all day. If the coffee is still good after it’s rested then it’s a great coffee. Peet’s certainly meet the coffee challenge head on and passes with flying colors.

reviews.title: A Great Tasting Signature Blend Of Coffee That’s Roasted To Perfection!
reviews.body:
# My Review
This review is for Peet's Coffee Decaf House Blend, Dark Roast, Ground Coffee, 18 Oz. First of all, it should be noted that I’m not a coffee connoisseur! I do like good coffee, drink coffee daily and have tried many different ground coffee brands such as Starbucks, Dunkin Donuts, McDonalds, etc. that I’ve purchased from the grocery store. That said, I use a French press to create my brew, so my results may be different to that of a coffee pot. From a brand perspective, I’ve known of this brand and its stores on the west coast that rival Starbucks, so can confirm that it’s legit and been around for years.

As for packaging, this comes in the usual fresh coffee packaging with the identifiable Peet’s logo, labeling and design with details about the coffee. It’s a nice reassurance that you’re getting a good quality product.

Taste-wise, Pete’s has developed a well-rounded dark roasted blend of coffee. Whichever way you brew it, the end result is a nice, bold and aromatic flavor that’s full of richness. I like the smell as it develops with that recognizable aroma to tease your senses. The decaf version isn’t as strong, yet it’s a mild variant that still gives you the smooth coffee satisfaction without the caffeine.

Overall, this is a nice dark ground coffee variety from a well-known brand. I received mine fresh with an adequate roasted / freshest by date, so I had a good experience on delivery. I liked the blend, brew, flavor and taste! I recommend.

reviews.title: Perfect backpack for daily use and travel!
reviews.body:
I am loving this backpack so much that I ordered the brown one as well - having one black and one brown will pretty much match any outfit!

Pros:
-padded laptop section is plenty big enough for both 13inch MacBook with room to spare for charging cable
-main section is large enough to store daily essentials with plenty of pockets if you need them to stay organized
-large main section zips all the way around so that it opens up nice and wide to fit and/or find things towards the bottom
-separate large front section also has lots of pockets and opens up wide
-small front zipper area can be used for quick access to smaller items if needed.
-when zipped up, the backpack has a slender, in bulky look.
-large sections have two zippers so that you can easily access things on one side with one hand without having to take the backpack off your back and unzip it all the way around
-genuine looking leather

Cons:
-the mesh material on the straps are a little
bit itchy when wearing tank with thin straps
-probably due to all the added padding, the backpack itself is a bit on the heavy side before you even put your belongings inside
-backpack was a little on the pricey side

reviews.title: Very slim but lots of pockets and it’s sturdy!
reviews.body:
I wanted this product because I needed a back pack that I could use to look professional (teaching undergrads). I wanted a back pack, not a handbag or work tote, because I bike to campus.
If you want to put a lot of things in this bag, it’s not for you. I mean smaller things like hand cream and lip balms etc. is fine! But I find that the main pocket fills my water bottle (700ml), my wallet, my chargers, my laptop, and that’s pretty much it. There’s some more space I could fill in the top but in terms of width, that’s it — and you don’t want to over stuff because that could mess with the structure of the bag!
I don’t know if I would use it for traveling because I’m the type of person who wants to travel with lots of snacks and lots of water especially for long flights. But, this is great for what I use it for — going to school and teaching.
I find that it’s very sturdy and I’ve been using it for a month but no rips or tears yet! And I don’t think there will be.

I bought it because I’m familiar with the Samsonite bag and other leather bags I was looking at had flimsy thin straps but these are thick, have mesh lining like a regular back pack, and are sturdy.

One final note is that this is a slim and small back pack. I was a little worried when I first got it that it might look like I was an adult wearing a kids back pack. I think it works for me (and I might have just been used to wearing big back packs), but I would suggest taking the measurements into consideration for aesthetics.

reviews.title: Fits under the aisle seat, even with THE BOX
reviews.body:
Got this because my airline regulatory standard duffel no longer fits under the already narrow aisle seat due to the box that's screwed to the floor in a lot of planes these days - an IFE [in-flight entertainment] box I'm told they're called. It fits into that smaller space because it's, well, small. I travel with a lot of junk that I should learn to do without: the usual Can't Live Without e-waste, snacks, usually a book and a magazine or two, pens, pencils, paper, a travel diary, planing calendar, reading glasses, passport, and my wallet and phone; by the time it's all in there - with the pockets expanded to accommodate all the junk, it's a tight fit in the main compartment, 1 of 3; the other two, one for your laptop, will accommodate your hand by that point and that's about it - so if something falls to the bottom, you can't dig around in any compartment without taking some of the stuff out. Still, it served its compact purpose and has stylish & neat squared edges that keep their shapes, padding in the right places, comfortable enough - it will keep you from slouching. Color choices are limited to two drab dirt hiding colors - either that or so insecure men will not be perceived as carrying a woman's back pack - gosh, not that! But in this day and age, navy or black, really?

UPDATE. Now that I've taken this on multiple trips, it's too small. when you put too much stuff in the pack like I do, the compartments get too tight and you have to take stuff out if something works it's way to the bottom. reviews.title: Full of (Good) Surprises
reviews.body: This is a surprisingly well-designed and constructed backpack at a great price.  Better than packs from more prestigious manufacturers that cost twice as much or more.  Examples: the interior is a light, burnt-orange color (like Briggs & Riley); the light color makes it far easier to find small items that have fallen to the bottom.  The key fob leash is long enough to pull out and unlock a door without unclipping the key - nice touch.  There are lots of slightly-padded dividers for a laptop plus a tablet (or two) plus a Kindle.  There are also a number of zippered compartments, some with "see-through" netting - enough that you'll be able to find a place for everything.  While it's lightweight, the construction is stiff enough that it will actually stand up on its own, not collapse and slump over like most backpacks.  The zippers are of excellent quality, and there are a couple of spots of leather in high-wear locations.  It's just tremendously well thought out, not something I've ever have expected from a venerable name in luggage.  Well done, Samsonite.  Can't wait to see what your design team comes up with next.

reviews.title: Most functional backpack I've ever used. Well priced. Spectacularly accessible main compartment
reviews.body: I'm  1.5million miler on American, and still racking up miles on many airlines. This sturdy bag fits under a coach seat in front of you, has lots of usable space, stands up on its own, has a fuctional front-top go-to section for quick needs, a roll-aboard strap, and comfy grab handle, and more. Wonderfully, the well thought-out main compartment offers flexibly movable compartment dividers that can be moved to accommodate seriously large items when needed. And the main compartment zipper opening opens this bag WIDE, so a large item or two can be easily accessed. I've used Tumi bags (great but too heavy and small pockets too tight) and lots of others. This one tells you the designer thought things through. Thank you Samsonite. Also though I love Tumi items, compared to Tumi, this one is the bargain of the century. Also, it looks very good - not too extreme-upscale, but upscale enough, and definitely not a high-school kid's look, nor an REI camping backpack. You may just be mistaken for a grown-up who used his backpack for a briefcase. For the reviewer complaining about no lock. Really? Who is kept out of a cordura backpack by a small lock? And if you want a lock, by the small one of your choice. I would rather not charge for and force a lock on the vast majority of users who don't need one.

First, if you want more of the surrounding sounds even in noise canceling mode then these might be better such as if you are where you still need to have some level of attention.
On the other hand if you are looking for noise canceling in a plan, a bus, a car, a noisy place then it will sound like you are either cutting down the higher or lower frequencies so I'm not sure in noisy places if the anr is actually on or off.
The most annoying part of these is when you pause and it decides you really wanted to double tap and fast forward your audible instead of pausing it (P.S. audible can you set an option of on lock screen to have only pause/play as even in lockscreen phones like to think you wanted to do something so it moves forward or back a chapter or two or fwd or rwd a random amount so I had to disable the lock screen mode)
Next most annoying, Samsung, why? Why do we need to give these the precise location to adjust settings, there is zero reason to need a location to change what the presses do (are you required to attach a high precise GPS to a computer or laptop to setup, nobody has been able to explain why location is needed for Bluetooth or why it's tied together and it doesn't help find them if I lose one of them.) Sometimes I just want a a good set of wireless earbuds without them having to know where I am and who I'm with. If anyone is wondering what I'm talking about, Bluetooth doesn't use GPS for functionality to function and after you've had your phone hacked then realize here you have middle of the road ear buds they want you to provide your precise location to use all the features.
If they'd both stop the location service alert and stop interpreting single taps as double taps then these would ne halfway decent. I need to see if I can find my old ones.

reviews.title: Sexy looking earbuds with above average audio
reviews.body:
Full disclosure: I bought these on Samsung.com but they don't have a review section (go figure) so I am reviewing them here.

I bought these the Buds Live almost solely so I can lay down in bed and watch a movie/youtube without having my ears impaled, and they don't, as the earbuds lie flush against the inner ear and I can barely feel them: it's wonderful and very dangerous to my sleep schedule.

That said one thing I have learned in the few days I have had them, is that if your face mask goes around your ear and if it's too tight around your ears it WILL hurt if you wear the Galaxy Buds Live. Luckily I can adjust mine which has solved the problem. The pain is not constant but it is quite sharp when you press on the buds. I suspect if you have larger ears this shouldn't be a problem.

The sound quality is surprisingly great, I suspect they're not as good as my Lypertek Tevi's but it's very hard to tell. I spent last night listening to music, going from the Live's to the Tevi's and the difference is nearly indiscernible, the Tevi's slight edge is almost entirely due to their in-ear design and that they use Apt-X: clarity and better details. In either case, they both sound is enjoyable. I am listening to Xanny by Billie Eilish right now on the Live's and the track sounds great.

The ANC is a no-show, well it's there but it doesn't really do anything except block some low frequencies, including in your own music, which makes some music sound muddy. It's just a battery drain, DON'T USE IT. Don't know what Samsung was thinking.

Battery life is solid, especially with ANC off, a good 7 hours.

If Samsung makes a Galaxy Buds Live 2 with the same ergonomic design but with in-ear tips, it would be a game changer.

reviews.title: Broke after 1 year (was: Fit well, good price, sound is pretty good)
reviews.body:
UPDATE July 2021: I took off 2 stars because, just over one year old, the left earbud has stopped working and/or charging. No sound, no control, no battery level. Very disappointing.
ORIGINAL REVIEW: The Apple-style buds did not stay in my ears, so I wanted something that would, with good sound, and reasonably discreet. The Samsung Galaxy Buds+ met all those criteria. They stay in, even while exercising, sound clear, shut out the outside noises really well, and look pretty good -- it's actually nice to have something different that the "cigarette-in-the-ear" look of the Apple devices. Complaints: The bass is very underwhelming, even with "bass boost" mode turned on (bass boost is really more of a "treble suppress" mode). Also, there's a mode that lets in ambient sounds (to allow easier talking to others, for example); however, that mode amplifies and distorts the outside sounds too much, and is very annoying -- I tried it a couple times, and haven't used it since.
Overall, great purchase. (And they only cost a little over half the price of the Apple buds!)

reviews.title: Very good but not quite perfect.
reviews.body:
I'm a bit obsessive when it comes to buying things like this. I looked at the Sony WF-1000, the Airpods Pro, and this one. I read and watched as many reviews as I could find. I ultimately chose the Galaxy Buds Plus over all the rest because of the reviews. I was like a kid waiting for Santa Claus as I watched the Amazon tracking showing it get closer and closer to my house. It finally arrived and I dropped everything and ran to the door, opened the box, and started getting everything set up.

The setup was pretty much flawless. No issues here. The sound quality was as decent as could be expected from earbuds. It doesn't compare to full size, over the ear headphones but I expected this. For earbuds, they sound great.

The good:

Sound quality. Like I mentioned, it's not as good as regular headphones but it's decent for earbuds. In the Samsung app the Dynamic EQ setting is by far the best. If anything, they could use a little more bass. If I use them with my phone I can compensate for that with the phone's EQ.

Ease of setup. I opened the app, took the buds out of the case, and the app paired them to the phone without any problems. Although there are some issues with syncing the bud's volume to the phone's volume. It's not as simple as it should be and sometimes it syncs, other times it doesn't. What this means is that when it's not synced you have two volume controls - one for the buds, one for the phone. When it does sync, the bud's volume control is synced to the phone's volume control. I haven't spent enough time messing with it to figure out how to easily enable and disable the media volume sync. I have a Galaxy S10 and under the bluetooth settings it used to have an option to sync the two volumes but in their infinite wisdom Samsung decided to remove that feature in a recent software update. I suppose this isn't an issue with the buds so much as it is with Samsung having removed that feature from the phone itself.

Ambient noise setting. This is actually very useful when out walking the dogs or when on a phone call.

The bad:

First thing I noticed is that after wearing them for 15 minutes, they started to hurt my ears. Using the medium wingtips, it's almost as if the ridge of the wing is digging into the inside of my upper ear. This is the smallest size wingtip that actually has a ridge to help it stay in your ear. If I put on the smallest size "wingtip" that comes with it, it's just a piece of rubber with no ridge so it doesn't do anything to help the bud stay in place.

I wish they had a wingtip that was sized between the medium one that comes attached out of the box and the small ones that don't have any kind of ridge or tip to help hold the bud in place.

The silicone tips that go in the ear canal are pretty much standard for earbuds but nowhere near as comfortable as some foam tips I've had in the past. It needs more comfortable tips and wingtips.

Almost 15 years ago I had a $20 set of regular wired buds with some foam tips that were the most comfortable I've ever had. I could leave them on all day and forget I had them on. For the cost of the Samsungs, you'd think they would include more comfortable ear canal tips and wingtips.

The feature that lets you double tap the edge of the bud to raise or lower the volume is very touchy. It's hard to figure out where exactly to tap it. The only thing I've found that works consistently is literally hitting the back of my ear twice, pretty hard. This is obviously pretty uncomfortable and annoying but I suppose if it works like this, I can deal with it. It's a cool feature to have but it needs a little work.

TLDR -- Overall they are very decent earbuds at a good price point compared to its main competitors. They sound good for earbuds although nowhere near as good as normal full sized headphones. They could also be a little more comfortable, at least for my ears.

::update:: I put on the small wingtips that have no ridge and wore them for a few hours to see if they would be any more comfortable. Unfortunately, they still hurt my ears. I think the main body of the buds are just too big for my ears and end up digging into certain areas of my ear.

::second update:: I've had to downgrade my rating from 4 stars to 3 stars because of how uncomfortable they are. I've tried different size eartips and the small wingtips and they are still uncomfortable. I've also found that during calls, the person I'm talking to is able to hear too much of the ambient noise around me. One other issue is that they do lack bass. Listening to music that has deep bass, I find that it's missing when I listen through these.

I wouldn't buy these again.

reviews.title: Almost fantastic
reviews.body:
Sound Quality:
These tws iems provide a very relatively neutral sound for a consumer-focused product. Everything sounds present, Subbass-bass-mids-highs. Nothing really overpowers each other. If you are someone who listens to many genres or likes to explore music, these are a solid choice. With the EQ presets you can 'slightly' adjust the sound to better suit the genre - I wish they just implemented custom eq, they already have it in sound assist...

I would say where these can fall short is when there is a bad connection between these and their transceiver. If the connection is stable, but 'bad' the highs start to artifact really badly. For my Samsung Note 9, this usually only happens for the first minute of pairing, but eventually ramp up to A+ quality and low latency - most likely because of the Samsung Scalable Codec. My computer, however, if I get a bad connection it stay there until I try repairing it a couple of times - I don't like installing drivers as much as the next person, but I mean why hamper the experience + they sell laptops too.

Other Features:
Hear-through: My jaw dropped the first time I put them in, its really just crazy to know you are listening to iems, but can still hear the world around you. It almost feels/sounds like you aren't wearing anything, but somehow still getting music pumped into your head. It also helps with the cabin air pressure feeling I get from just wearing closed headphones/iems.

It falls short in busier sounding environments though. If there is 'loud' chatter going on in the background, I can't really hear the person in front of me too well. That said I only ever kept them on the middle setting, never bothered with the super-hearing mode.

Fit and Comfort: With 3 sets of wings and tips, I was able to find a good fit for both my ears. Where with other iems I would have to learn to seat each monitor differently to fit my ear, the guides really aid in positioning the monitor very easily into your ear.

Touch controls: Didn't always work as intended. Sometimes I would want to turn on hear-through but it would just register as a single click or if I was adjusting the monitor it my ear it would also register as a click. The corner double-tap rarely worked for me. Maybe 1/10 attempts it would work. Some people said that kinda flapping the back of their ears with would press the button more accurately for them, but unfortunately my ears are too small and my fingers too sausage-y to get it.

reviews.title: Superior European-style Coffee
reviews.body: I have worked high-end restaurants and have had the privilege of tasting the finest coffees from Michelin star restaurants in Chicago, Atlanta, Memphis, and NY all the way to Spain, France and Italy and I can tell you after tasting most everything on the shelf here to recapture those experiences in my home, Post Alley Blend is the closest I can find. I must educate other readers to remember that a perfectly well dark roasted Arabica bean will smell literally skunky in the bag. The skunkier, the better. Invest in the grinder and buy the beans. Patiently experientvwith the amount of grounds per cup to match your unique taste. You will delight in the naturally foamy top and well balanced full flavor. I have been buying this for 2 decades since discovering it during a visit to Washington, and every time I attempt to try something new and trendy, I'm disappointed with stale superficial flavor too high in acidity and no lingering foot notes. Seattle's PA blend even makes a perfect ice coffee. I really regret that I can't find it most places anymore here on the east coast  since Starbucks purchased the company in a predatorial act to subdue a competitor. I pray that it is not discontinued in the remainder of my lifetime.

reviews.title: Really helps me with my Tinea Versicolor!
reviews.body:
I have breakouts of Tinea Versicolor (TV) when the weather starts to change in the spring/summer. Starting at my neck and going down my back.

I’ve been using creams prescribed by my doctor for the past couple years that I’m supposed to apply daily. But it’s difficult to apply such a thick cream on your back when you live alone and plus then it annoyingly makes my T-shirt’s cling to me. And I’m not sure they were even that effective.

I tried this based on the reviews, and it helped my TV a lot! I followed other people’s advice – the first time I applied it and left it on for 10 mins before washing off. It’s a thinner consistency, so much easier to apply and spread on your back than a dense cream. Now I just use it as a special body wash every time I shower as maintenance. My TV has definitely stayed under control and if it’s there, I don’t notice it at all!

Of course the smell is intense and the coloring is very blue. But 100% worth it if you have TV and want an easy way to treat and prevent it. :)

I discontinued this as it is way to strong for my fine hair, and resorted to using my own combination of a mint, tea tree oil mixed with himalayian pink salt ( exfoliant ), mixture as a pre-poo leaving in after massaging onto my scalp for 20 mins, then following up with regular shampoo and conditioner.

reviews.title: This shampoo really fights the dandruff!

Inspired by reviews of this shampoo, I bought it, and have to say, it really helps! used it only 3 times so far, and almost all my dandruff is gone, no flakes, only couple of very small particles remain! I'm very pleased to find a shampoo that really helps. And also it has pleasant (as my wife says, I'd say - neutral) aroma, unlike these tar shampoos, which make you smell like burnt log.

NOTE: This is very etchy shampoo, so when applying to your scalp, try to rinse it after in such way, that no residue hits your face or other parts of body, because if you don't, than you going to feel like little stingers hitting your body all the day.

reviews.title: Made dandruff worse
reviews.body:
This shampoo is awful for dandruff. It made mine so much worse it was embarrassing. Instead of minor flakes, I had huge scales (some approximately .25 inches in diameter) that caused me concern. And my condition would get better when I used regular shampoo.

Recently, I looked at the ingredients (aside from the active ingredients) the top 3 (meaning most concentration/quantity of) were all sulfates - Ammonium Lauryl Sulfate, TEA Lauryl Sulfate, Ammonium Laureth Sulfate - which are cleansing agents.

Meaning it creates that lather and removes dirt and oils. Great! However, for sensitive scalps and especially those that are experiencing inflammation or other conditions, sulfates exacerbate the symptoms because it is harsh, irritating, and drying. Not something you want if you have dandruff.

Pro: It smells better than H&S.

reviews.title: Wonderful headphones for mid-budget gaming
reviews.body:
So I've been trying to stream more and while I had a mic, I didn't have a quality set of headphones, and after one week where my ears were aching from the earbuds set I've been using for years for work and working out, I finally decided it was time to get an actual headset for gaming. I should also point out the reason I didn't get an all in one set is because those tend to not be as good as individual parts and I already got a decent standalone mic.

Originally my budget was lower and while I was given solid suggestions in that range, the two had drawbacks: one was great for shooter games as you could detect when an enemy was walking up behind you but the bass sucked for music and cutscenes, while the other was ok with cutscenes but wasn't that great for very heavy bass and hearing enemies sneak up on you in games. As I listen to a lot of music with heavy bass and find cutscenes pretty important, I couldn't really compromise on this and so this one got pointed out to me instead and I decided it was worth the higher amount to try.

Overall, I'm very happy with this choice. The sound is amazing, regardless if it's music or games, and the pads are large and very comfortable on my ears, especially with my various ear piercings. The only slightly down side is the cord (as my tower is on the bottom right but the cord is out the left ear piece) but I'm trying to avoid using batteries so I refrain from wireless and it's not too noticeable as long as I don't do a 180 in my chair.

reviews.title: Better than my ears
reviews.body:
I bought these to replace the beat up old closed back Sennheisers I use for practice with my Chapman Stick. The sound quality turned out to be better, even the bass, than the old headphones. In addition, it turns out I love the sense of the music playing in the space I occupy instead of transporting me to an isolated sound space. I don't mind background noises, the sounds of people nearby, my dog shaking out his fur, the Yamahas and Harleys a quarter mile away; it's all music to me. But what I gain are the almost delicate direct, unamplified sounds of my hands on the neck and strings, sounds I didn't know I was missing until I started using these 'phones for a time.
To the point, these 'phones have the best dynamic range I have heard in those costing several times as much, the frequency balance is excellent except for the growliest bass, and any sense that the sound is not being produced in the space I occupy by my speakers is absent. In addition, I can carry on a conversation without impairment and I hear my voice naturally, unamplified, when I try to sing.
In addition, the light weight, well chosen materials, and fit make it possible to wear the headphones furlong periods without noticing their presence.
All in all, I think this was an excellent investment, more than doubling my enjoyment of the instrument I love.

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.body:
I got these for less than a hundred dollars when Amazon ran a special. For anywhere near that price, these are phenomenal headphones. I am sure there are much more expensive headphones that sound a fraction better, but if you appreciate awesome quality at a modest price, these are winners!!

These are traditional headphones - no noise cancellation, no batteries, no recharging, etc.. They are wired headphones that you need to plug into your music device or stereo system's headphone jack.

Mine came with 2 wires: 1) a headphone cable with a 3.5mm plug on both ends (ie, the size of plug that fits into the headphone jack on portable devices like an iPod Touch, and 2) a longer 10 foot headphone cable with a 3.5mm plug on one end and the larger plug on the other end that would go into an component stereo receiver or preamp.

Mine did not come with a case or a bag, so that is my only small gripe. Otherwise, these headphones are awesome.

Say goodbye to your hearing.

reviews.title: I have listened to higher end headphones like the HD 600
reviews.body: I have spent many many hours listening to both the HD 518 and the HD 558 and i also use the ATH-m50x in public while on the go. I have listened to higher end headphones like the HD 600 , dt-880 and HiFiman 400i but i haven't spent much time with them. Having said that I really love the HD 599. The sound signature is definitely new and different compared to the 8 series before it as others have mentioned. It is definitely more forward sounding and i was concerned about having a lack of soundstage but I have actually found them to be more immersive. The imaging is great. You know where everything is, it just sounds closer. But these phones pack some great bass that provides more of and umph for pop and more contemporary music in general. I actually like the bass on HD 599 alot better than the ATH-m50x which I wasn't expecting. I have also found them great for gaming and haven't noticed any loss in soundstage compared to the 558 and event the 518. I think they'r a great value for the money under $200.

reviews.title: The expanded bass and lack of sound separation caused loud bassy noises like explosions to drown out the opposite ear cups audio
reviews.body:
I returned these due to a distortion problem with certain points of bass. The strange part is overall these provide a very clean audio experience with a more prominent bass than the 598. The 70$ difference is not worth it over them IMO as after receiving my new 120$ pair of headphones from Audio-Technica... the a550z while paired with an audio interface... these are destroyed. Please note I used both with the Scarlett Solo. The sound separation is lacking, this is an issue with the Sennheiser line of products as I've tested all the way up to HD650's and directional audio for FPS games, while solid in comparison to "gaming headsets" are lacking. The expanded bass and lack of sound separation caused loud bassy noises like explosions to drown out the opposite ear cups audio.

Sound separation is a new thing that I didn't fully understand until the last couple pairs of headphones I tested. I'm not sure if there is some high end headphone amp/dac that would have altered my experience with Sennheiser products by after the Game Zero's PC37X, 599's and 650's I'm getting a much different experience from Audio-Technica ADG1X and now the A550z. There is a distinct difference in audio separation. You hear more sounds at different depths.

Tools used. MSI Godlike audio jack 3.5 & 5.3, Fiio E10K, Scarlett Solo.

These are adequately comfortable but beat by the HD650's, ADG1X a gaming headset from Audio-Technica and the a550z which is a near model semi-closed back headphones from Audio-Technica. Honestly while these are functional headphones there is no reason to get these over the 598's or spend more and get the 650's... or even the 6XX from Massdrop for the same price. This item is the epitome out of place merchandise that should maybe cost 10$ more than the 598's

reviews.title: Great headphones
reviews.body:
Let me start out by saying that it's been quite a while since I've used over-ear headphones. Usually I buy in-ear headphones to go with my mobile device, but my use for these is for use with my desktop computer to replace a set of Logitech gaming headphones.

Setup: Windows 10 Pro, ([[ASIN:B009ISU33E Sound Blaster Z PCIe Gaming Sound Card with High Performance Headphone Amp and Beam Forming Microphone]]) to which the headphones are plugged directly into (via back of computer), male, early 50's, mostly rock music (Rush, Garbage, etc.)

When listening to these with no equalization, they sound pretty good, especially the bass. It's right in the sweet spot where I would expect it to be. I find the treble okay, but I prefer a little more myself; but I attribute this to part of the aging process. Enabling a little equalization at the 8k and 16k levels wake up the treble (Geddy Lee!) to the point where I like it.

These are pretty light and fit well on my head. The pads don't make my head feel hot and are more comfortable than I thought they would be with the cloth ear pads, as my previous experience has been either foam or a vinyl type of pad. I like the fact that the ear pads are replaceable, but haven't had them long enough for that.

This is my first experience with open back headphones and one of my concerns was sound leakage. If I were in a room where I wanted to listen privately and wanted to avoid noise from others, that these would probably not work as intended; in which case I would use my in-ear headphones. In my case, the environment is within my home office and it is nice to be able to hear other things without removing them (doorbell, dog, wife, kids, etc.).

Overall, I'm very pleased with these and if some of the reviews I've seen elsewhere are true, they will improve with use.

Buildwise, 4/10. The build isn't as great at the M50X. Kinda flimsy plastic. You gotta be careful not to break these. Not to mention that you can't fold these.

Sound wise, 10/10. I previously used the M50x which were good but after hearing these it's just ok. With these, I could actually differentiate the bassist from drums from guitarists. This thing manages to make Black Metal sound well produced, and thats saying alot. The open back lets me hear if someone is trying to talk to me without me having to take them off. I wouldn't reccomend wearing this on public transportation, as it does leak sound. It doesn't leak very loud, but people will know what you're listening too. You can't hide your p0rn with these.

reviews.title: Amazing starter
reviews.body:
So this is my first open back headphone.
And I gotta say, I am pretty impressed with the quality. But the thing is, you do not notice how good it sounds until you get used to it. Let me explain.

So I was already using a good budget wireless earphone, Jaybird X2. It was amazing to what I was used to. I mean, after apple's earphones, I was like damn son..
A year later I upgraded to Jaybird X3's. It was even better. I used it 16-months before buying HD 599's and still using them outside my home. They are still superior to me. But when my HD 599's came in; the first go sounded pretty bad to me since I wasn't used to a sound like this (Gamers with 7.1 headphones will say that too). It was pretty 'boomy', I don't know how to put it to words.
After two weeks or so of constantly using HD 599's at home environment, I've started to enjoy it more every time I put it on my head. Really loving them.
Now, I still love the characteristic sound of X3's. But if I'm at home, there is no way I'm using them over HD 599's (sometimes while I'm laying down, I use them.).

The only thing I don't like is: When you push the volume to almost max, sometimes songs sound bland. Like there is something behind the actual sound. A snake doing ssss, or a low frequency sound echoing.. I can't really put it to words. And I am not sure if this happens because of my MacBook Pro 13 inch Touch Bar 2017's original DAC or maybe my library's quality (I buy them from iTunes).

reviews.title: Amazing Quality for a Good Price
reviews.body:
I bought a pair of Audio Technica ATH-M50Xs for Christmas last year and the sound quality is amazing, but they're extremely uncomfortable after about an hour. Thus, I decided to do a bit of research for longer wear and stumbled across Sennheiser's HD 599s.

After a couple days' use, I've come to a few conclusions about the HD 599s that might help you make a decision:
- The sound quality is great for these headphones. They're not quite on par with ATHs, but that's largely due to them being open-back, meaning they don't isolate noise as well. The upside to this, though, is that you can maintain a conversation or listen for something in the background if you're not comfortable with total noise isolation (which is great for multi-person households).
- Audio is crisp, clear, and more than adequate for an average listener. For the more discerning ear, there are great soundmapping equalizers with settings specifically for HD 599s that you can find with just a bit of research.
- They're the most comfortable headphones I've owned in years. I've already worn them for an eight-hour session and didn't feel any form of fatigue or discomfort.
- They're sleek and stylish. They conform to the head much more smoothly than most headphones that I've owned, including the ATHs.
- The cable variety is useful for multi-purpose listening. Shorter cable is useful for close device listening, but the longer cable is great for sitting on the couch and hooking up to an entertainment system for those late-night watching sessions.
- They're not as portable as the ATH M50Xs (they don't fold, for example), but if your goal is to keep them on your head rather than stuffing them in a bag or a case, then they're just as good for on-the-go listening as anything else would be.

I'm a huge fan.

Normally these will say things like "now with ten times extra moisture" and won't smell particularly good. It's hairest! Where are the products that will help me step out of the shower feeling like a queen?

Well, SheaMoisture understands my hair. This shampoo looks and smells incredible and washes out of my hair in a way that makes it feel amazing. Like I'm in my own hair commercial, tossing my head and letting my locks spill attractively over my body. Literally the only product line I will use anymore... I also enjoy Shea's moisturizing conditioner. I am thrilled to discover a company that is thick-haired forward and doesn't make it a hassle to find delicious bathing products.

reviews.title: Pretty good stuff
reviews.body:
This lathered on my hair magnificently, and felt very good, very rich and moisturizing and that's its main selling point, right? So high points for that. After my hair dried it felt fuller and softer. I also liked that. But I did not expect nor care for the cloying vanilla-ish scent. It's heavy and I am not used to using scented shampoo. Maybe the strong scent is necessary to mask the unvarnished smell of castor oil - in which case, it can't be helped, but I did take one star off because the scent seemed so overpowering to me.

This personal preference of mine may be due to my own sensitivities - - I dislike the common perception that <i>everything</i> needs to be scented from laundry soap to shampoo so that by the time you get dressed you have countless different scents competing: toothpaste, deodorant, soap, shampoo, sunscreen, moisturizer, hand lotion, face cream, laundry soap, mousse, hair gel, cosmetics, god help you if you use perfume too. I wouldn't mind if these corporate conglomerates would be good enough to synchronize with each other so everything came along the same line of scent - wouldn't that be great ? But they don't, . . so I look for unscented things whenever I can

reviews.title: Faulty Product?
reviews.body:
While I love this product, the version of this I get from Amazon is, for some reason, consistently worse in quality than the version of this product I purchase at the local grocery store. For whatever reason, the Amazon version has been clumpier for at least several months--think large brown clumps residing within a strangely watery liquid, whereas the store-bought version is even throughout. Sadly, the clumpy version is noticeably less effective at cleaning my hair of its abundant, and I mean truly ABUNDANT, oil.

For reference, I have thin-ish blonde hair and a lot of it. It is both fantastically greasy at the root and shrieking-for-death dry at the tips in a way that evokes awe at nature's inspiring capabilities. With that in mind, it's very impressive that an affordable line of hair products can help this British disaster. Shea Moisture Castor Oil shampoo and conditioner + the castor oil leave-in conditioner (*chef's kiss*) have been brilliant, keeping my hair looking somehow healthy, clean, managed, and moisturized, which is no small feat. This brand is wonderful in quality and affordable in price, and I appreciate all the work they do. I'm not sure why the Amazon version of this product specifically seems to be faulty.

reviews.title: My favorite headphones of all time easily. Best Bass and best looking.
reviews.body:
These were my first serious headphone purchase ever. Before these headphones, I bought the $20 Bluetooth earbuds that hurt my ears or $5 earbuds from the target. It has been a year since I bought these and I can say firmly that these are the best headphones that I have ever tried. I was considering the Bose QuietComfort 35 [[ASIN:B0756CYWWD Bose QuietComfort 35 (Series II) Wireless Headphones, Noise Cancelling - Black]] or the Senhieser PXC 550 [[ASIN:B01E3XLNA0 Sennheiser PXC 550 Wireless - NoiseGard Adaptive Noise Cancelling, Bluetooth Headphone with Touch Sensitive Control and 30-Hour Battery Life]] I tested both of these headphones in stores and watched reviews and I thought that they were the way to go until I found out about these. I am a bass head for sure. I listen to a lot of rock and rap so bass is very important to me and I love the adjustable bass controller on the back. You can literally feel the bass which is possibly my favorite thing about these headphones. These were my one and only pair of headphones for my first year of college. I wore them on my 2 hour commute to school and the 2 hour commute back not to mention the hours in the library. I ABUSED these headphones and they are still kicking with full force. Their sound is very bass heavy so you do lose some quality at the higher end but you won't really notice it unless you are listening to a lot of that kind of music. Another thing I love is that they also go above the volume set from your device using the controls on the headpiece. I can play my music at full volume and not feel any pain at all which is nice and I do like that they are loud. The wireless connection is very impressive. I can walk anywhere in my house with very little connection dropping. Additionally, the headphones are very heavy and sturdy and I love that about them. I really felt the quality of these headphones. The ear cups are very comfortable and the head strap is this very soft silicon which really balances out the weight. I have literally worn these headphones for 12 hours straight during finals and I did not feel any discomfort during that whole time. The are made of a hard plastic and comes in a matte black or white (I opted for the black). They are very stylish and don't stick out like other bass heavy headphones like the Sony XB. The branding is almost invisible and sit pretty tight on the head so they won't make you look weird.

I have 2 problems with these headphones. First, they don't have noise canceling which isn't really a problem since they are pretty loud but I would like that option. Also a related issue is that there is a good amount of sound bleed. The people sitting next to you can hear what you're listening to which is a non-issue but if you care about you're privacy it is something to keep in mind.

3 year update:

I've been using these headphones as my daily driver for 3 years. Multiple vacations, commuting 2 hours to school every day, summer internship and so much more and it is still fighting strong. I haven't seen any diminished sound. All that I've seen so far is the hinge for the earpiece started to fall apart, unfortunately. It hasn't affected the usability much but it is annoying as it feels like it will fall apart soon. That being said, I don't trust another pair of headphones to produce the sound and feel that I got from these headphones. My next pair of headphones will most likely be another pair of crushers wireless.

reviews.title: Great to work and play!
reviews.body:
Before this, I used LG Tones, somewhere in the 700 series. I really liked the LG Tones design because it was wearable and with the right collar it was concealable. However, when those died (after a good three or four years of daily use) I decided that I wanted to move to the over-the-ear design. The in-ears are convenient, and low-profile, but I wanted to up my game on quality of sound and battery, and I knew that in-ears like LG Tones weren't going to get me there.
My Tones died in November '17 and I bought these in March '18. I scoured the internet for a reliable set of headphones, and I'm glad that I got these. They have great range, they are comfortable, the sound quality is great for music and for video editing, the back-up cable is perfect for those moments when you forgot to charge in the last week, and it just works consistently.
I noted some of the reviews saying that they have a tight fit, which is true - they are tension headphones, so if you're prone to any sort of tension headaches or muscular discomfort in your neck/jaw, be wary about how much you wear these and what you do to stretch.
I'd recommend these for the price any day.

reviews.title: These are not the headphones you are looking for
reviews.body: There are better options for less money or about the same. I have tested many headphones, including the Bose noise cancelling headphones. I ended up with a pair that fit my budget and quality needs. Before I talk about why I didn't like the Skullcandy headphones, I'll save you the time and tell you first where I think you should look. If you haven't checked out the Avantree wireless aptx headphones, give those a try. I think most people would be very pleased with them. They are just as comfortable as the Bose, have a much longer battery life, and support aptx audio (which iPhone doesn't currently support, but some android phones do), you can also hook them up to a hub for low latency high quality audio for watching movies, etc. I did not like the base on these Skullcandy headphones, it sounded very fake and honestly hurt my ears. They also had a pinging noise whenever anything would tap on them or anything bumped against them even lightly that really annoyed me. I would have given them 1 star, but they aren't completely hopeless and have some redeeming qualities like the battery life. I would just recommend you look elsewhere as there are better options.
