reviews.title: Audiophile Review
reviews.body: These headphones are as close as you can get to having a subwoofer in your headphones. The bass feedback is not perfect by any means, but pretty darn good. I'd say the bass cuts out around 35-40hz. Definitely is good on midbass but don't expect it to continue to play down low at the 20's to low 30hz range. There is no delay in the bass response as I saw some other review mention. The bass just cuts out when it doesn't sense that bass needs to be amplified or if it senses that the frequency of the bass is too low for the headphones to reproduce. I will mention that if the bass slider is up too much, it might sound muddy depending on the song. Luckily it's easy to adjust. Good pair of wireless headphones even without the bass feedback feature, though definitely glad it's there. Pretty comfy, looks good. I've always been a fan of skull candy. And I sure like my eardrums being pressured by the bass

reviews.title: Really nice bass headphones - Great for modern music
reviews.body:
These things really surprised me with the way the bass feels. I was skeptical reading how they worked, but they are awesome. You can really feel the bass. It's a great sensation.

I mainly got these for hip-hop listening. Newer songs sound great and it's brings life to older trackers from 90s/early 2000s. You can really tell songs are mastered different nowadays. Some older songs have the bass in a different range and things just generally sound a bit different.

Does this thing have the best quality mids? Not really. Listening to punk or rock, some things sound dull to me, and obviously they do not benefit from the bass that much (depends on the song though).

No headphones are perfect, but these full a need in a great way, when I want to listen to some hip-hop and feel i want that "bass" experience. I am other headphones reproduce instrument sounds better, but these are great for what they are.

reviews.title: Unique Audio Experience
reviews.body:
I recently purchased the Sony WH-1000XM4 headphones, and I must say, from the moment I put them on, I was transported into a world of exceptional audio bliss.

Let’s start with the sound quality. The WH-1000XM4 boasts outstanding clarity, delivering rich and well-balanced audio across all frequencies. Whether I’m listening to my favorite tunes or watching movies, the headphones consistently reproduce a detailed and immersive soundstage. The bass response is deep and punchy, while the mids and highs are crystal clear, ensuring that no musical nuance goes unnoticed. Sony’s proprietary noise-canceling technology elevates the listening experience by blocking out external distractions, allowing me to truly appreciate the music.

Comfort is another area where the WH-1000XM4 shines. Sony has designed these headphones with plush, soft earcups and an adjustable headband that fits perfectly. I can wear them for hours without any discomfort, making them ideal for long flights or extended listening sessions. The earcups also create an effective seal, enhancing the noise-canceling capabilities and further immersing me in my audio world.

Lastly, the build quality of these headphones is simply amazing. The materials used feel premium and durable, instilling confidence in their longevity. Sony has thoughtfully included a sleek carrying case, making it easy to protect and transport the headphones wherever I go.

The other con for me is that when I place a call from my work computer when it routes to my phone I have to pick the headphones, it does not automatically go there. Had many people hang up because they thought no one was there since I did not realize this. Sorry Sony and all the tech YouTubers out there who made me love this, I have to disagree. reviews.title: perfect headphones
reviews.body:
I bought these after spending a lot of time going back and forth between these and the AirPods Max. I finally decided to save myself $200 and get these. I'll have to admit, I was afraid they would feel cheap compared to the AirPods which have a mostly metal composition.

I've been using them for about a week now and I can safely say that they don't feel cheap at all. They're built with a very premium feeling soft-touch plastic and faux leather. They're extremely comfortable for long listening sessions.

Though I may be slightly biased because this is my first pair of "real" headphones, I think they sound amazing. It's like I'm hearing all my favorite artists over again for the very first time. Noise cancellation is a killer feature, especially if you're sensitive to noise like I am. I'm able to put these on and just focus on whatever it is I want to do.

reviews.title: Nice but could be better
reviews.body:
The sound is good but I wanted even better. While the noise cancelation is pretty cool it bothers my ears and I don't see myself using it in the future very often. It also always defaults to that setting which is annoying. A lot of the controls are just ... bad. Side Note I got this at a discounted $278 price.

Sound Quality:
Good sound quality but really fatigues my ears with and without noise cancelation. A problem I never had before. This is the main reason I will be returning them. And why no AptX Codec? I've read some technical reviews saying most phones don't use the top bandwidth LDAC codec and that the at lower bandwith this Codec is worse. While I likely couldn't tell this still annoys me they give me the option of AptX.

Daily Use:
Annoying. But I do like the case it comes with. Give me buttons!! I've been wearing these on my walks in the winter and I can't change the song or skip without taking off my gloves AND jacket hood. If I have a hood it ignores my touches likely due to the fact the old versions would pause very easily with light touches. Pause to speak sounds like a cool idea unless you actually use it. And the headphones auto-pause feature often doesn't work when taking the headphones off and putting them on my head. If I pause the music with a tap on the side control and then take the headphones off later the music actually starts when I take them off my head... and obviously turn off when I put them back on again. Very annoying.

Overall I feel like I expect more from a premium product from a usability standpoint at the very least. The sound is more of a personal thing which some people may not mind. I would not get these unless you NEED good noise cancelation.

reviews.title: Great sound, but several issues make it a no-go for me. Sticking with my Bose QC 35 Series I
reviews.body:
I have owned the Bose QC 35 series I (the originals) for four years now, and just recently replaced the ear pads since they finally deteriorated. I figured after four years there has to be some serious improvements in noise cancelling technology, and since the WH-1000XM3 model got so many good reviews I figured these would be awesome. So I pre-ordered them.

I pulled them out of the box and followed the very quick connect process of downloading the app and using it to pair to my phone. It downloaded a firmware update automatically while I fiddled around with some settings briefly and listened to some music. Super easy, awesome.

The sound is very impressive. Punchy kick drum (I listen mostly to rock/metal) and nice bright sound. I quickly settled on a slightly customized version of the included Bright preset.

But things quickly went downhill from there.

After using the headphones for a bit, the touch controls became frankly annoying and easily susceptible to mistakes (I triggered track skips multiple times just by removing and putting the headphones back on). The volume adjustment is especially tedious...if you want to raise or lower the volume significantly you have to swipe it up or down a large number of times because the volume adjustment is done in small increments. With the Bose QC 35 and its dedicated buttons, you just quickly push the buttons. Simple.

I spent about 20 minutes trying to figure out how to pair the headphones with my laptop, reading the guide in the app and doing some web searching, thinking it must be provided by one of the two dedicated buttons like on the Bose QE 35s. Nope. It must be done with the app. In fact, everything has to be done with the app except whatever you have the custom button configured to do, and the power. On the Bose I just have to slide the power button, and it goes into pairing mode. Simple.

The above are honestly smaller issues that you could probably put up with since the sound these produce is so good. However, the deal breaker for me was when I connected them with the included wire to the controller on my Roku Ultra to enjoy some TV time after a long day. I always watch movies and TV with headphones. To my horror they produced a clearly audible hissing sound that is incredibly distracting. I turned them off and on again, disconnected and reconnected the cable. No change, still the hissing sound. My Bose don't produce this sound. Ugh.

After listening to them for a couple hours I had a slight headache and felt fatigued, almost nauseous. I know some people are affected differently by the noise cancelling technology, but I don't get this from my Bose, even after listening to them all day.

Additionally, speaking of noise cancelling, I compared my Bose QC 35s to these, and I couldn't tell the difference between the noise cancelling. They sound the same to me. :shrug: I'm sure you could tell the difference with laboratory equipment though.

All-in-all the sound these produce is really good, and the noise cancelling is great (although I can't tell the difference from my Bose QC 35 Series I). But they have 1) lots of annoyances in the touch controls instead of dedicated buttons, 2) the fact that the app is required to do everything (including pairing) except turning them off and activating the custom button, 3) the hissing on the wired connection to my Roku Ultra, and 4) the fatiguing after listening to them.

I'll be returning them.

reviews.title: Excellent sound quality, excellent noise reduction
reviews.body:
Headset is fairly lightweight, ear cups aren’t as deep as some headphones but deep enough for my average sized ears. Cups are soft and the overall comfort level is high, even after extended play time.

The touch controls on the ear cup are very slick and help reduce the number of physical buttons. However, taking the headphones off (or putting them on), I’ve accidentally turned music on as it mistook the contact as a command. Not a deal breaker but a quirk to be aware of. The auto-pause when you remove the headphones is a nice touch too.

Noise cancelling is truly excellent. I was working in my office, window open, tower fan blasting. Silence. Took my headphones off and there was a police helicopter flying circles over our house (nothing to do with me!!). The only downside is that it’s SO good that I literally cannot hear my wife talking to me and this has earned me some angry glares. In the app settings, you can adjust the level of background ambience that the headphones filter out but I cannot find a balance where the noise cancelling is on but still allowing my wife’s voice to be heard. Unfortunate but some may consider that a benefit!

The headphones are paired to my desktop computer (a 2011 Mac Mini with Bluetooth 4.0) and to my phone (an iPhone 11 Pro with Bluetooth 5.0). Between the two, it seems to connect faster and more reliably to the desktop. I’ve had a couple of instances where I struggled to get it to connect to my phone after it successfully connected to my desktop. Full disclosure: I’m running the iOS 14 beta on my phone and it’s not exactly super reliable. I feel like the Bluetooth got better between Beta 6 and Beta 7, so take this observation with a pinch of salt.

The optional “Speak to Chat” feature (if you start to talk, it lowers audio playback) is clever and works well but there IS a slight lag before it kicks in. It also caught me off guard today when I was in a WebEx meeting because it essentially shut off the WebEx audio and I then couldn’t hear responses to my comment. Had to disable that feature for the remainder of the meeting.

The 360 audio feature is kinda hard to comment on.. in the demo within the app, you can clearly hear a pleasant difference (it’s more immersive). In practice, after signing up for a free trial with a supported app (TIDAL), I don’t really hear it. On a side note, the TIDAL Master track streams sound amazing on these headphones. Like.. truly amazing. Not sure I want to spend $26/month but it’s got me thinking about seeking out other lossless / higher quality sources for my audio streaming.

Regarding the setup process for testing the 360 audio.. photographing my ears would not work using the automatic capture system and was very frustrating. Manual capture worked better. But ultimately.. I don’t think that the effort was worthwhile, given that I don’t hear a difference in supported 360 apps.

Speaking of audio quality.. these are great headphones. The default EQ out the box feels a little muddy / bass heavy (or at least not to my taste) BUT the app lets you tweak this, has some nice presets and custom curves for you to set up. What’s great is that the EQ you set up from the phone app also works when streaming from other sources (e.g. your computer). It’s global, which is exactly what I was looking for.

I’ve listened to a lot of tracks I’m familiar with, some less so, and heard little nuances that previously I’d missed. There’s a lot of detail here. With DSEE on or off, I’m not worried about wireless compression negatively impacting the signal. It sounds great.

Overall, these are a fantastic set of noise cancelling headphones. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Decent with some unfortunate caveats
reviews.body:
These are overall one of the best models available right now, I’ve tried all of the Sony models, several Bose models, and the Airpods Max and while these Sonys are good they’re not my first pick for a few reasons.

1. Reliability - these started malfunctioning just outside of warranty and I had to get a new pair when I was expecting many years of functionality.

2. Noise canceling - noise canceling isn’t just the raw amount of noise that is canceled. The problem with these is there is a lot of crackling and noise from the headphones and they can often create an uncomfortable pressure effect on your ears. The quality of noise canceling beat the Airpods Max that I tried and the Sonys cut out the most high frequency noise of any pair I tried but I had to give it to the Bose QC45 for overall best quality.

3. Call quality - I practically can’t use these for calls because no one can ever understands what I’m saying. I have to hook up a separate microphone or just use my phone normally.

4. Sound quality - I have been an audio engineer for 15 years and these have a very interesting sound that I haven’t quite heard before anywhere else. I would say they’re the most listenable headphones I’ve ever used because the sound is so inoffensive. The downside is they have no punch, they sound boring. You can’t fix it with EQ, the bass always sounds flat no matter what. Overall, I do like them but for ultimate engaging audio quality I found the QC45s to be best once you add the bass back in and cut the treble a bit in the app. (Bass +2, mids +1, treble -1) Neither of them will compare to a DT770 pro without noise canceling in a quiet environment but once there is noise the Bose easily win because the noise canceling leads to overall better audio quality since you can actually hear it.

4. Transparency mode - The Sony has a very scratchy sound to this mode, rather unnatural sounding, so i rarely use it.

Strengths. I can’t leave a review without talking about strengths, now can I? These definitely have some redeeming qualities I can’t ignore.

Comfort. The top headphones all have their strengths in terms of comfort but I found the Sonys to be the best here because they distribute the pressure on your ears very evenly and I can easily forget I have them on whereas the Bose QC45 seems to be a little more uneven so you feel more pressure overall. Airpods Max I didn’t try for several hours so I don’t know but for a few minutes they were very good.

Microphonics. If you brush up against anything with the earcups the sound is not annoying unlike other headphones I’ve tried like the QC45. I think this is the microtexture of the plastic. I am extremely impressed with the quality of plastic used in these headphones, it doesn’t seem to scratch, they look brand new after a year.

Touch control. Easiest touch control I’ve used, you can fast forward, go back, skip, pause play, change volume, and several other settings just by swiping, tapping or holding the right earcup.

Battery life. Just a few minutes of charging can get hours of playback. I’m very impressed by this and haven’t ever had a problem.

Overall these are quite good, although the weaknesses I’ve outlined above do exist. The only reason I’m wary of these is the questionable longevity and customer service. I like them.

reviews.title: Truly a Worthy Successor to the WH1000xm3!
reviews.body:
Honestly, there was a part of me that was worried that these headphones would not be the best pair to own after the issues that I experienced with the prior generation of them: the WH1000xm3. The main issue that I had? The build quality: the plastic around the headband snapped due to a flimsy connection, resulting in me having to tape both headbands together so that the headphones don't fall apart on me. I tried several alternate brands to see if they would work, but they never came close to giving me the same level of satisfaction while wearing them as the WH1000xm3 did, even with the taped headband taken into account. So I decided that the best replacement for a Sony headphone was another Sony headphone, and I invested in the M4, which succeeded the M3 last year (as of this writing).
My initial thoughts were as follows: the headphones were a definite improvement upon the originals, retaining what I liked most about the original headphones (largely the overall comfort) while also improving the headphones in other small ways (especially in regards to the special features-the M4 are way more feature-packed than the M3 were, incorporating many elements that are being found on most other headphones these days). My favorite thing that was fixed, however, was the sound quality. You see, the original sounded amazing, and honestly sounded better overall than the likes of Bose and Sennheiser, which I have tested as potential replacements for the Sony headphones. And that is despite the fact that the headphones have a relatively small 40mm driver inside, instead of a more traditional 50mm driver. However, the one minor issue I had with the M3 was that the low frequencies were heightened a bit more than I would have liked, making songs sound a bit bass-heavy even when the EQ was turned off (the only way I was able to fix this was by setting the EQ to 'bright', which isn't ideal since the EQ does degrade the battery life). With the M4, Sony improves this by tuning down the low ends, resulting in the headphones having a very flat frequency response, which in turn results in every song having a much wider sound stage than the M3 did (and almost making them sound as good as the various open-back headphones I have tried, including the Sennheiser 650, which is my personal favorite open-back headphone).
In terms of the special features, I think they were implemented quite well in these headphones. The noise cancelling is exceptional, much like it was on the M3, and the transparency mode is somehow even better than it was on the prior generation headphone, sounding a lot more natural and less tinny overall. The auto activation of transparency mode during conversations is fantastic, and enables me to talk to people naturally without ever having to remove the headphones from my ear. This also means that I don't have to awkwardly tap my hand on the earcup with the M4, either. The DSEE Extreme audio enhancer really helps to make music sound a lot more full, even when using devices that don't support the LDAC wireless standard. It isn't as good as listening to lossless files wired, mind you, but it is still an amazing feature that helps to take advantage of the flat sound stage and frequency response of the headphone drivers.
Now, this isn't to say that these headphones don't have issues, mind you. The auto-pause when removing the headphones from your ears is very much a gimmick, and doesn't always pause the song (and may even resume the music before you have a chance to place the headphones back on your ear). Since the headphones use a light sensor to tell if you are wearing your headphones or not, it means even a simple shadow can cause the headphones to think that they are back on your ears and restart music playback. It is quite obnoxious, and it is best left out. Another, more minor issue is the touch controls. While I personally have no issue with them, I know that there are many people that don't like them whatsoever. So I will just make a note that they are still here, and they work in much the same way as they did on the M3. Finally, I should mention that the flat soundstage, while amazing for my listening experience, may not be for everyone. Bassheads in particular would likely prefer extra pronunciation on the lower ranges. And while they will never be quite as bass-heavy as the Skullcandy or Beats line, the EQ can still bring the bass levels up quite a bit, using a 'clear bass' slider that reminds me of the slider on the Skullcandy Skullcrushers: raising the bass without causing distortion.
Overall, the headphones turned out to be quite an exceptional pair, especially when it comes to listening to music during commutes. The great noise cancelling, beautiful audio, and fantastic transparency mode definitely make these headphones a winner in my book. And the app only helps to improve the flexibility of the headphones, allowing for many different features to be unlocked. And while these headphones certainly have some issues (no pair of headphones are perfect, after all), I think the benefits more than outweigh the issues for me, and put these at the top of my list of best closed-back headphones that I have worn. Hopefully Sony will continue to make amazing headphones like these in the ears to come.

reviews.title: Best option for the price-point imo
reviews.body:
I'll start by saying I don't exclusively care about name brand, but I prefer to have a recognized brand for the things that people will notice. This is the best looking product at this price by far.

Pros: very sleek and they don't protrude from the side of my head like a lot of headphones do. I think the bulky ones are ugly and look cheap. This factored heavily in my decision. The sound quality is what you would expect. I obviously wanted to buy the nice headphones that are $300 but these will mostly live in my golf bag and be used while being active. They stay on my head nicely without giving headaches from pinching too hard.

Cons: for the price, there aren't really any cons. Compared to nicer headphones I have owned they are not as bass heavy as I would typically prefer, especially at the lower volumes. Some songs do have a slight "playing in an echo-y room" sound. I listen to a lot of rap, so it's typically loud enough to not notice these things but when I listen quietly it doesn't seem to have the range needed to portray a genuinely quality sound. If you're looking for those ranges, you will likely need to spend $100+. Listening to more indie pop artists like Jon Bellion where all of the pitches and sounds genuinely matter they actually seem to produce a really nice quality sound.

I've only had them a week so I cannot speak to durability but if I haven't followed up on this review it means they're meeting my expectations!

Edit: following up with another "Pro"
The battery life on these is baffling to me. I received them April 3, it is now April 24. I've used them quite a bit and they still have 70% battery. They came fully charged and haven't touched a charger yet. My guess would be 6-8 hours at 60-100% volume for the large majority of it.

reviews.title: Lovely headphones with great sound!
reviews.body: This over the ear headphone is lovely and produces a surprisingly great sound! I’m not a millennial and have never been comfortable with Bluetooth earbuds. I prefer old fashioned headphones if I want to listen to music or audio books and not be bothered by outside noise and distractions. These are terrific. They feel great wearing, no pinching or tight squeeze on my head and ears and are so adjustable and comfortable.  They are so lightweight I don’t even really feel them while on and walking around the house. I really like how easy the controls are to operate. The power button is easy to find by touch because it’s slightly raised and easy to pause music or take an incoming call. The call quality through the built in mic in the headphones is perfect and has no distortion. It was so easy to pair the headphones with my Samsung S22  Ultra and the Sony headphone connect app is very easy to follow and use for setting up the sound settings and fit. While they may not be as immersive a sound field for a very particular audiophile, for the price they have wonderful full sound that is crisp and clear. I’m a fan of jazz, swing and big band sounds and they sound fabulous!

reviews.title: Great bang for your buck. Good gym headphones.
reviews.body:
I bought this pair of headphone because I wanted a pair of over-the-ear headphones for the gym. My requirements were that they were cheap enough that I could toss them around, tight fitting so the wouldn't fall off at the gym, and noise cancelling enough that I could listen to an audiobook or music at the gym and still be able to understand the words.
I am pleasantly surprised by how great these headphones are. I have a very nice pair of over-the-ear Sonys that I use when I'm not getting all sweaty, but these measure up to those suprisingly well. They stay on well at the gym without crushing my ears (and without bothering my cartilage piercings). I can do RDLs, rows, and bench without them falling off.
The most amazing part is the battery life. I have charged them once since I got them, and they're still at 75% battery. I literally don't understand how that is possible. It's like they're solar powered or something. I swear the battery life goes up instead of down.
Overall, these are a great purchase for an easy and convenient pair of headphone for the gym or around town. I wouldn't recommend them for hours of listening, as they do squish your ears over time, but they're great for an hour or two of gym time. My only other complaint is that they don't fold up or come with a case, but they're cheap enough and sturdy enough that they can be banged around a little in your bag.

reviews.title: Great headphones for the price
reviews.body:
My Bose SoundSports recently stopped working, so I was in the market for a new pair of buds with a wire between the two. I mainly use these at bedtime, listening to an audiobook as I fall asleep. One feature of the Bose I really liked was the auto-shutoff after xx minutes. I was worried that with these new Sony buds, I'd have to re-charge it every day since I regularly fall asleep with the audio still running.

So I got these and I am very happy to discover that I've had no problems with the battery draining if I fall asleep with them on. I set my audiobook to stop playback after 90 minutes, and it would appear the headphones go into some low power state when that happens. The following night when I put them in, the headphones are still on but have as much power left as when I went to bed the previous night.

So despite having no auto shut off, they still preserve battery. For $30 this can't be beat. The sound quality is just fine for my use (audiobooks), I will say that the extra tips they provide are VERY flimsy as I ripped one trying to remove it from the holder.

The wire that runs between the two pieces is VERY long. Almost too long, but that's a very minor complaint.

If you want a pair of cheap earbuds, these are a great buy. They don't have all the bells and whistles of the more pricier ones, but there's very little not to like here.

reviews.title: Good bass response - sturdy for the long haul
reviews.body:
I purchased a Pixel phone in 2016 and the lack of an earphone jack got me into blue tooth headsets. I've tried earbuds, but most of them do not fit very well. When they fall out on a plane, you'll find me crawling under the seat in coach, looking for my flying earbud. (The exception seems to be Anker's LibertyAir. The worst? Those Jabra Elite 65t - way overpriced for mediocre sound qualty and buds that just don't fit me!)

These Sonys are not earbuds - they're tethered and therefore lose-proof! I have some other tethered headphones - Anker makes a nice set - but these sound better - more bass without cutting out the highs. The cord on the Sonys also seem more substantial and less likely to break easily. There is an extra 'dongle' on these Sonys that adds a bit of balance to the 'phones - so when they're not in your ears, they are less likely to go sliding off to one side.

Charging is simple - the charge port takes a USB-C cable. I asked on Amazon if you could use any USB-C charge cable rather than the short little cord that Sony puts in the box. Sony replied that they only want you to use their dinky little cord, but I charged them with my other USB-C cords and everything seems fine.

These are now my favorite way of taking calls without my phone firmly planted on my cheek. They turn on quickly, have a nice sound and look like they'll hold up for months.

reviews.title: Good Deal for The Money.
reviews.body:
I am a former live sound engineer. To me sound quality is the number one concern. My last two sets of buds were actually sold as in ear monitors for professional musicians. One set were wired Sony's and the other Advanced AD3 wireless with a wire between the buds. Both had excellent sound quality. Since I have not had individual buds before and was afraid of losing one, I decided not to break the bank with my first pair. High end buds go for north of $200. I bought the P3s after doing quite a bit of research.

When they arrived they were pretty easy to set up. The app you use with them is pretty simple. It includes a customizable EQ so you can tailor the sound to your liking. I use a "dog eared" setting boosting the bass and treble while leaving the midrange flat. The sound is really quite good.

I would call the noise cancelling decent but not great. Of course in my opinion the only way you get great cancelling is with full headphones. You have a choice of different NC settings. I find the "indoor" setting works the best at the gym to somewhat drown out the music they are playing. I have not tried them on an airplane yet. As I mentioned I was afraid of losing a bud....so much that I leave them in until I get home and dump them in the charging case. When I leave the gym I just switch to the "Ambient" sound mode and I can hear the world around me pretty well. The buds work very well for phone calls. My wife says my voice sounds perfect when she calls.

The controls on the buds for changing volume or tracks work ok, but are not perfect. At time I find myself just reaching for my phone to change track or adjust volume. That may be more about my gnarly fingers than the buds.

I am still trying to get the pairing routine worked out. I have them paired with my phone, tablet and Peloton. I know they are supposed to pair automatically to the primary device, but I find I need to put them into pairing mode most of the time. Once paired they are rock solid....solid as in I left my phone on a machine at the gym, went to the other side of the building and they still worked.

The buds fit well in my ears. I don't run, but a sweaty in the saddle, out of the saddle Peloton HIIT ride does not pop them out.

The battery life seems good, but honestly I do not wear them more than a couple of hours and the rest of the time they live in their charging case.

I would recommend these buds for people who want a pair of bud with good sound and don't want to break the bank to get it. They also look pretty cool.

reviews.title: Great sound quality, fit and comfort. So-so ANC, finicky touch controls, features missing.
reviews.body:
Bought the Anker Life P3 on a sale for $68 and these are my initial impressions after having it for a bit over a month.

Pros -
Excellent sound quality and sound stage (this is also a con because these are bass heavy for me at the default setting, but you can fine tune it in the app to your liking)
Well made case and earbuds, good materials and quality.
Comfortable fit. Again, this is very personal, but since the drivers themselves are large (11mm) I used the small tips and they work fine. These are fairly light also so I didn't find fatigue wearing them for long times.
Wireless charging case (I like this over USB-C)

Cons -
ANC is average. I think the sound quality is better with ANC off but it might be personal preference.
Very finicky touch controls, although you can change 1 click, 2 click and hold to various functions in the app I do not like it and its very fussy. Has a mind of its own.
No in-ear sensor. I have cheaper earbuds that stop playing music when you take it out of the ear canals, but these ones don't. (e.g. Airfun Air True)
Stem is a bit longer than competitor earbuds.
Call quality is okay.
Battery life is mediocre.

Overall I think they are good for the price I paid, but at the full retail you have plenty of options.
4.5 star for sound quality, but everything else is a compromise so I can only give 3 stars at the full retail price.

reviews.title: Great sound and overall great value for the price
reviews.body:
I’ve had these earbuds over a month and I love them. Couldn’t give a 5 star ratings because in my opinion there are a couple of minor things that could be fixed. But overall, high-quality affordable earbuds!

Good things:
- sound quality! Music has a full sound, bass sounds great with these,
- comfortable fit, sleek look. I don’t like the look of AirPods/white earbuds and I got these in black
- app is easy to use, I love the ability to switch EQ settings depending on what genre I’m listening to
- maintains a good connection. I can leave my phone in the garage while I go upstairs and my music doesn’t stop playing

Things that could be improved:
-noise cancellation is okay. In busier environments it doesn’t completely cut out noise. I was on a plane recently and used outdoor noise cancelling setting; it greatly reduced the engine noise but didn’t completely cut it out.
- touch controls on the earbuds are not always as sensitive as they should be, so it can take a couple of times to make adjustments

Overall, these are great affordable earbuds and the good qualities outweigh the minor drawbacks IMO. Get a pair!

reviews.title: Amazing bass and great ANC
reviews.body:
It’s amazing how much quality and great features you’re getting at this price point. I honestly didn’t know what to expect, since I’m used to buying much more expensive gear, so I wasn’t expecting much. I gotta say, I was pleasantly surprised! They sound GREAT, extra, full range, deep bass, but the rest of the frequency range sounds good. Definitely not muddy or overbearing, I listened to rock as well as bass heavy electronic tracks and all sounded great.

Comfort:
Comfort for me is the #1 thing when it comes to earbuds or headphones. It doesn’t matter how good they sound or how good the ANC or features are if they’re not comfortable! These fit the bill nicely. I had never worn stem style earbuds before, but it doesn’t really make a noticeable difference to your comfort anyway, you can’t feel the stem. These are light and don’t apply pressure to any area on my ear that would otherwise lead to discomfort (like most of the other earbuds in the market that are unnecessarily large, like the new Sony WF-1000XM4). I can wear these for hours with no discomfort whatsoever, so we got a winner here.

ANC: The ANC on these is a bit different than what I’m used to, as I’ve never owned earbuds with ANC, just cans like my beloved Bose QC35’s and my JBL Tour One, of which the Bose obviously is the king. Well, when compared to my Bose, these Life P3’s do a pretty good job of muffling the heavy, industrial fan I have in my room, and in some cases blocking out different frequencies better than the Bose. The fan just sounds different. Maybe it's not as quiet as with the Bose but the pitch it gets on these is very subdued. (I have a VERY loud fan in my room on purpose so as to have a very loud white noise that I can sleep to while drowning out the rest of the outside noises that wake me otherwise). The thing about the ANC on these earbuds is that it has 3 modes, transit, indoor and outdoor. I found indoor to be the best for me personally around the house, it brought a very impressive level of attenuation. I could still clearly hear my dogs barking but all the other, more constant noises went VERY silent. In some cases it feels more silent than the Bose cans do, and those are among the best ANC performers on the market. Don’t get me wrong, the Bose are still kings in that regard, but it does by no means put these buds to shame, they stand up surprisingly well. I wish there was an option for selecting “maximum” ANC where it would mix the 3 options, because while standing next to my fan, I went through all 3 and they each blocked a different frequency range from the fan and changed its pitch and perceived loudness. I’m sure they’re capable of consolidating all 3 and bringing even more impressive ANC but I suspect they don’t do this in order to not hurt their flagship. Just my guess but regardless, the ANC performance in these buds is nothing to scoff at and I am actually very happy with and impressed by them in that regard. Transparency mode on these is also very good, you don’t have to take your buds out in order to have a conversation or be aware of your surroundings. I have mine set to long press to switch between ANC on and Ambient aware on. Which brings me to the next plus, the touch controls on these earbuds is actually decent, unlike my JBL Tour One where adjusting my headset often times results in activating the touch controls unintentionally. That doesn’t happen with these buds.

Find my buds:
This has a feature where it makes your buds make a loud noise so you can find them. Pretty neat if you ask me, I’m thinking of getting a pair of these for my mother, since she’s constantly losing everything.

In conclusion:
I’m very happy with my purchase, I have included many pictures so you can see what you get when you buy these and what it all looks like. I would definitely recommend these to anyone, for the money, they can’t be beat and even if they were more expensive, I’m sure most would be happy with them.

reviews.title: Great overall. Bad default eq.
reviews.body:
I've been using these daily for a couple months now both at work in an automotive shop and at home and I really like them. They are much lighter and more comfortable than my Sony WF1000 XM3s and sound almost just as good. I also prefer the companion app with these over the Sonys.

Out of the box, the default EQ setting is terrible with the bass massively overdriven and other tones very underdriven. Fortunately it is fully adjustable and I was able to get a natural sound profile out of it. Calls are clear and I haven't had any problems with people not being able to hear me talking.

The active noise cancellation and transparency modes are excellent. I have worn them to the shooting range with and used them in full isolation mode and been very comfortable. At work I use them in full transparency mode and I can have conversations with coworkers all the way across the shop and hear them perfectly and also use loud power tools without hurting my ears.

Battery life has been excellent, with full transparency mode turned on and listening to music at relatively high volume I get about 6 to 7 hours on a charge and the case is good for another 2 charges of the earbuds. If I put them in the case on my lunch break I can get a full work day of music and then some without interruption.

I would happily recommend these to anybody.

reviews.title: Perfect all-rounder & the only pair you need. These are on par with $100+ earbuds.
reviews.body:
Rating for Anker - 5 stars! I previously bought the Soundcore LIFE P2i as it was within my budget of $30. I was looking for earbuds to use mainly for work (Zoom meetings and phone calls) with the occasional casual music listening and game playing on the iPhone. The P2! did not meet my requirement (see review.) so I returned them. Surprisingly, Anker customer support reached out with sympathy and offered to send me this pair of LIFE P3. Kudos to Anker for caring about their customers and the quality of their products. They are up and coming and will do well if they keep this customer-centric focus up! Review as follows:

1. Fit / Finish / materials - 4 stars. Well made appears high quality. Nice mix of glossy and matte surfaces. Glossy on the insides of the bud for easy cleaning and matte of the outside for an up-scale look that fights off fingerprints. Took off 1 star because the hinge of the case is a little loose and appears to be a potential weak point prone to failure in the long run. A full range of silicone ear tips is included to ensure a good fit - XS-XL.

2. Sound Quality - 5 stars. While the P2i totally lacks bass, the P3 is very well-balanced. Bass isn’t pounding but is very present and doesn’t overwhelm the other frequencies. Overall, the P3 is a very balanced sound across the low, mid, and high frequencies. Kick drums have an impact and are not muted, snares are clear, cymbals are not clipped. For $80, the quality is spot-on for the price - it is a very viable alternative to the more expensive buds (beyond $100)! Additionally, the connected app lets you save your own EQ presets.

3. Audio / Video lag - 5 stars. No lag at all. In-game mode, audio syncs. Same results in non-game mode watching movies. Well done.

4. Bluetooth - 5 stars. No indication of which version, but I’m guessing 5.0 and above as the connection is stable, clean, and without lag.

5. App Support - 5 stars. This is where Anker distinguishes itself from the competition. They are one of the few that provides a companion app and it makes a world of difference, especially when it is well implemented as is the case here. The Soundcore app allows customization to the earbuds for EQ, taps/touch, etc.It goes a step further by offering customizable ’Sleep’ sounds! These all work very well. and most importantly, it updates the firmware the first time you use it. The potential for continued updates (I hope Anker supports this model for a long time) is amazing! There is even a function where you can test to make sure you get a perfect seal from choosing the best fitting ear tips and how you position the buds in your ear. This simple implementation via the app is something every (high-end) earbud should provide.

6. Calls - 5 Stars. Very clear when tested in a normal home environment. Both reception of the caller and my voice were clear and without break-ups or static. The reception of the phones was between 2 to 3 bars during the tests.

7. Noise-cancelling - 4 stars. Not the best, but on par for the price and design (not over-the-ear). The proper size ear tips provide good isolation and the ANC does the rest. There are 3 modes to choose from to determine how much (and what kinds of noise) is blocked out. Good implementation overall.

8. Battery - 5 stars. I have yet to run out of juice within a working day using it off and on. 7 hrs per charge as advertised.

9. Design - 5 stars. Looks high-end and well-made. Light and stays in my ears. The buds don’t stick out far from my ears and the stem is not too long. The case is compact and feels good in the hands.

The LIFE P3 is highly recommended if you are looking for a pair of earbuds that can be used daily and for the widest range of use. This will not disappoint, and other manufacturers should learn a thing or two (or more) from the P3 as this checks all the right boxes for a pair of quality earbuds. $80 isn’t chump-change (at least for most) but if you’re already looking to pay beyond $100, forget that. Get these instead.

reviews.title: Nice sound, but problematic
reviews.body:
Update- after a couple of weeks using these, I’m returning them. Bluetooth has disconnected several times and the headphones have simply turned off while I was on a call. Battery life was sufficient (medium), so there’s no reason it should have happened. Also, I’ve been hearing a light windy sound in the right earpiece that is really unbearable. I’ve tried different equalizer settings, but it doesn’t go away. Unfortunately, it’s something I’m not willing to deal with. I hope this was just a faulty pair, but I will never know since I’m not at all interested in trying another set.

Pros:
-Long battery life
-Convenient case
-Nice color choices
-Transparency mode when you need to hear your surroundings.
-Most importantly, great sound quality right out of the box.
-Several equalizer presets in the app, making podcasts clearer and music sound better. Ability to customize your own too!

Cons:
-I’m fairly certain that the ear pads cannot be replaced. It’ll be a bummer for these to be junk when the pads inevitably start breaking down.
-I had higher hopes for the noise cancellation, but it’s decent. It does well with those constant, low sounds, so I think they’ll be nice on an airplane or bus. I can still hear conversations on lower volumes though, but the NC makes it easier to ignore.
-All the buttons are simple rectangles. Different shapes (volume up and play/pause) would make it easier to quickly feel what you’re pressing.
-There’s an unpleasant hollow scratching sound when anything touches the headphones, and I’ve heard occasional popping that’s quite disruptive if your volume is up.
-I’ve been using them for only a few days and already the headphones dropped a call so I had to quickly grab my phone to continue the conversation, and I’m sometimes noticing poor connectivity during video streaming especially. I think it’s the Bluetooth but I’m not yet certain.

reviews.title: Great product with some flaws
reviews.body:
These are definitely the best headphones that Soundcore makes. The sound quality is great and the Soundcore app makes them so much more flexible. I personally use the "Acoustic" setting as my default and I have no complaints at all in this regard. The Q30's have phenomenal battery life, you'll only have to charge these every few days and they tell you how much battery is left after powering on. The noise cancelation is very very good. Noise is noticeably muted or completely blocked out, and the transparency setting is very accurate to what's going on around you, letting you have a whole conversation while still wearing the headphones. Other headphones do have a better implementation of noise canceling, but they are also around 3x the price so imo these are an amazing value. The build quality is also fantastic, these are built solid and are incredibly comfortable. I often have troubles with other headphones that clamp very hard on my head, these do not have that problem at all. The foam on the headband is much better than the Q10's, those had a memory foam band that would compress and get very hard and uncomfortable after a while but the Q30's don't have that problem at all. The included travel case is a nice addition as well to protect these while on the go. I definitively recommend the Q30's for anyone looking for a good headset.

A few things I would like to see improved:

1. The biggest issue I have is the voice that plays whenever you change modes. I owned a set of Q10's some months ago that also have this voice but on that headset it is stupidly loud which made me return them, on this Q30 it is much better but I still would like the option to not hear it at all. The voice is robotic, jarring, and makes the Q30's feel more like a cheap aliexpress product. The voice stops playback of any audio you're listening to, which if you're watching a video will make you have to skip back a few seconds to hear what you missed because even though the audio stopped, the video kept going. It's honestly baffling since the Q30's actually do switch to using beeps instead of the voice while you're in a call so the function is already there, it's just limited to only calls. I understand they have it this way so users know which setting they are switching to if they don't have the Soundcore app, but it would be nice to have an option in the app to always use the beeps to get rid of that robotic voice once and for all.

2. The L and R inside the ear cups are a very good addition but the lines are thin and therefore are hard to see in a low light situation. If these letters were filled in instead of being an outline they would be much easier to see. Bonus points if a reflective material could be used as the paint to really distinguish them from other headsets that take this approach.

3. The last thing I'd like to see changed is how long you have to hold the power button for the headset to turn off. I haven't counted but it feels a lot longer than it should, I often find myself waiting for them to turn off. Perhaps a power button could be added to the app widget to make powering off easier.

reviews.title: Good Price Vs Value
reviews.body:
First of all you have to be aware that this are budget headphones so you can't expect Sony or Bose features or build. Also, I own the Sony XM4 so i was able to compare them side by side in sound quality and fit (not an expert audiophile), build, case, apps. My main use for this headphones is streaming (mainly movies) on ipad

SOUND AND FIT
PROs: In general I like the sound of the SoundCore as they more inclined to bass so movies/anime/series sound great in normal mode (ANC OFF). When turning ANC ON you loose some of the highs of what you're hearing. ANC is good ( i tested them with the Vacuum Cleaner ON) but not nearly as good as the Sony. In general they fit nicely on the head putting enough pressure for the headphones to do a nice seal.
CONs: Transparency mode gives a weird vibe to it, it doesn't feel natural, but its usable. When changing between normal, ANC, transparency mode the headphones have a strange behavior, they seen to be turning off the and goin back on again as there's a brief pause on the sound (not sure if its a behavior only on mine). Lastly , even thought fit is good you can get some wetness and ear fatigue if you use them for a long period of time.

BUILD AND CASE
PRO: they included a a nice carrying case which is way better than a carrying pouch or nothing.at all
CONs: The case internal division leave a lot to be desired (compared to the case from Sony). Also, headphones have to be aligned in a particular way to fit correctly.

APP
PROs: they try to mimic the Sony app by letting you select the diferente modes and features. A nice adition is that the SounCore app has some music playlist that you can listen to and test your headphones (instead of just going to youtube)
CONs: I didnt fin any, being honest it s nice app.

CONCLUSION: As i already mentioned, this are no Sony or Bose, but based on the price i would highly recommend them to anyone who will use them for everyday activities live movies, light commuting and music. ANC is good, they are confortable, battery last a lot, they can link to 2 devices, and sound is great for the average person and they are 1/3 of the price of the big brands (at the moment of this review)

If you're a heavy plane traveler or hard commuter you might be better with something like the Sony.

reviews.title: I was initially hesitant to buy another Anker headset
reviews.body:
I was initially hesitant to purchase these headphones. I've long coveted the industry standard Bose, but just couldn't bring myself to spend THAT much for headphones.

My first pair of noise cancelling headphones were the Anker Soundcore Space NCs that I bought two years ago, while the noise cancelling was okay, there were several things about them, that were extremely disappointing. One, is that I couldn't use them while traveling with JUST the noise cancelling on indefinitely (it would shut itself off after like 30 minutes, unless I were actually playing something through them) and they broke apart of less than 2 years of light usage. Granted I do have a large head and have to extend the ear cups to their maximum in order for these to fit comfortably, but that shouldn't mean that that makes headphones more prone to breakage.

So here I am. After reading the reviews (mostly all positive and absolutely fawning over these new headphones), I decided to give Anker another shot. Boy was I glad I did!

In short, these are amazing! I haven't been able to test them while traveling yet, BECAUSE COVID, but they've managed to improve just about everything from the Space NCs. The noise cancelling is superior, the transparent mode is really nice, the build quality seems better, and I don't have to max extend the ear cups to accommodate my large head. reviews.body:
01/24/21 update:
Got in contact with Anker support, and they were very reasonable trying to help. They proposed some basic troubleshooting steps, which didn’t solve the problem. Then I could either get a replacement unit or a partial refund. I opted for the refund. Support personnel were always very polite and nice, and I had no issues with the process itself.
I hope they release an improved version of their nc technology, so I can finally enjoy my backyard without that annoying tollway noise.
—————————
I live 2 blocks from a tollway. I bought these headphones hoping that they would cancel that noise and I would enjoy my backyard more.
I turns out that regardless of the noise-cancelling modes (Transport, Indoor or Outdoor), the highway noise keeps coming through, loud and clear. The NC actually blocks other noises (the pool waterfall, for example), so it is working.
Sound quality wise, it is ok. However, I didn't buy it because of the sound quality. I bought it because of the noise-cancelling feature.
I was able to pair it with my phone and mac laptop easily. No issues here.
I haven't spent a long time using them, so I can't tell if they're comfortable enough for long sessions, but for the time I used (a few minutes each time), they are comfortable.
Microphones: Doing a mic test using Zoom, I didn't like what I heard. It seems to have captured a lot of the ambient noise, and the voice sounded far. I compared with the HyperX Cloud Alpha that I have at home, and the HyperX mic sounded way clearer.
In summary, I didn't have a good impression with this one. I was hoping for better noise cancelling.

reviews.title: Surprisingly great
reviews.body:
I read some negative reviews before I bought these and they worried me a little but I thought they were a little nitpicky for headphones in this price range. I bought these specifically for work, since I need a high level of concentration to do my job and environmental noise breaks my focus. So noise cancellation was key for me. I also bought a pair of Blackshark Pros in the same order because I needed a headset geared towards gaming. I was not expecting these headphones to cover all the bases and you shouldn't either.

That said, here are my impressions...

PROS:
- The noise cancelling is great! There are dual gas-powered concrete saws operating outside my window as I write this review and I can't hear either of them with the noise cancellation mode on. You can immediately tell the differences when you switch to normal or transparent mode.
- These are very comfortable. The ear cups are very soft and I can barely feel that I have them on.
- Pairing was easy with both my phone and my computer.
- Charging is fast, even with a standard charging cable. I used them for music and Teams calls for several hours right out of the box. When they got to 40%, I put them on a standard USB-C charging cable for an hour or so. When I picked them up again, they were fully charged.
- The sound is excellent, especially at this price point. The bass is perhaps a tad muddy but it really sounds comfortable to my ears. Highs are crisp but not overwhelming. Mids are clear. Overall, these headphones provide me with a very satisfying listening experience.
- The headphone controls all work as expected.
- You can plug these into a wired port, although I don't know why you would.
- They fold up into a nice little case that comes with it.
- The Bluetooth range seems good. I'm able to walk around my 1-bedroom apartment while maintaining solid audio.

CONS:
- Even at the highest tension, the headphones can become loose and slide down my head. Not a big deal if I'm sitting still but not so great if I'm moving around. This isn't a deal-killer though, since I mostly sit on my butt at work.
- I did experience a little glitch with the volume control where the Windows master volume wouldn't control the headphone volume. That seems to have worked itself out after my first use, however.
- They aren't "reference" or "studio" headphones. You're not going to hear every detail of the music in its original form. However, I didn't expect them to. I bought these for casual listening and for that purpose, they beat every pair of earbuds and headphones I've had up until now.

Overall, I'd highly recommend these headphones. They are perfectly suited for casual listening and really strongly-featured for the price range. I seriously had to wrack my brain to come up with the few "cons" I found but I hope you'll take those with a grain of salt because I will probably never think about these minor complaints again. Buy these headphones if you're looking for a great casual wireless listening experience!

Ever notice how in most movies, people are talking so quietly that you turn the volume up to hear what they're saying then suddenly...the television is blasting another scene that's a person screaming or an explosion and it wakes up the entire neighborhood? reviews.title: Incredible price point - enters high end territory without the price tag
reviews.body:
I have to admit - I am audiophile and headphone “nerd” as my wife calls it. I have bought (and returned 20+ headphones). I had the Max over the head (sold 5 days later - too heavy, sweats, uncomfortable).

These are borderline alternate universe stuff. The first. The price. Come on. These guys are doing stuff at this price point that amaze me. I use my headphones (in priority) as follows 1. Zoom 2. Music 3. Transparency

1. Zoom calls can be sneaky test for headphones. Not only do you need a good chipset and well designed firmware to work with a plethora of laptops, mobile devices etc but you also need microphones that work. This headset amazed me. I thought if I could get half the performance of higher end units I would say it’s fine. I was wrong. People tell me I sound natural and clear. Transparency works well. Connectivity is solid. No issues on M1 MBP.

2. Music. Come on Soundcore. What are you hiding in these? Bass. Mids. Highs. All come in perfectly. I really think there is more behind the scenes going on for these to sound this good. Compared to XM4s these have more bass (controlled) and not muddy. The mids are solid not over done and the highs are crisp and clear. I don’t run my units at 100% volume so I can’t comment about that but at medium volume these blow my mind. I returned every headset I have and kept these.

3. Transparency and ANC - solid and works well. I think some more tuning in firmware will improve ANC. When I have it on I don’t hear my kids. So it works. What else can you ask for? It’s the ultimate test. :)

Overall - these are scary good. I have the blacks but once the blue are in stock will pick up a pair of them too. Just amazing. Great job Soundcore. Keep it up!!!

reviews.title: The weirdest and most inconsistent pair of headphones I've tried
reviews.body:
I wanted to test these out in a variety of different settings before writing this review. Thus far I tried them in a coffee shop, at the gym and also at home.

First the good : these do,have some noise cancelation capability. However, they don't hold a candle to my Bose noise canceling 700s that I refuse to ever take out of the house. The price on these headphones is also a plus. For the most part, they're fairly comfortable as well(more on that below). The battery life is also good and a single charge did last me through hours of listening.

The bad: I wanted these to totally block out sound around me while doing whatever I was doing. I understand that most heads won't block out 100% of sound however, these definitely let through a decent amount of noise which is surprising and also disappointing. The fit is also a major complaint of mine: the ear cups are fine but, I find the band of the headphones slip and this leaves a feeling of them sliding and not being secure. Recently, the pair of headphones also started to make a very odd shaky/reverberating sound when I wear them and if I tilt my head down which I can't figure out. There is also a button on the left side of the headphones that controls the option of the sound setting to normal, noise cancelation or transparency. Soundcore couldn't have picked a more irritating spot to place this button as every time I try to adjust the left headphone, my finger or thumb seems to touch this button changing the setting.

I wouldn't repurchase these headphones personally. They're not horrible but there are better options out there.

Beware of water shoes that have holes in the shoe itself as they will allow shale, rocks, sand, Etc. to get into your shoe and cause you grief. Thick Treads also trap rocks/shale and cause you problems too. These treads will not trap anything and they did a great job gripping the wet surfaces I walked around on while on my trip. These are perfect for my needs and were very cheap too. They look like they will hold up well for weekly use of 3-4 days a week during the Summer Boating Season this year.

reviews.title: OK, but nothing amazing
reviews.body: Like many of the other reviewers, as part of a Bzzagent campaign, I also received a sample of the Pike Place ground coffee to try out.  When Pike was first introduced at Starbucks a couple years ago, I had a cup every Wednesday as part of their introduction campaign and even now it is my go-to choice if their other daily brewed selections aren't interesting to me.  Freshly-brewed in the store, it indeed is very smooth and pleasant without tasting especially burned or bitter.  I had high hopes when I heard Pike would be part of the line available in the grocery.  However, I think there is just something lost in the translation from store to grocery bag.  I have brewed several cups using both a drip pot and drip filter and just find the resulting coffee rather bland.  I suppose this could be attributed to the pre-ground beans roasted god knows when.  At least in the brick and mortar Starbucks, the beans are (typically) fresh with a clealy indicated roasting date.  This is probably the coffee snob in me talking, but coffee is at its absolute best when freshly roasted beans are ground just prior to brewing.  The resulting grounds have a rich dark almost wet look to them from the coffee bean oils, which produces an intense and flavorful coffee.  The exact opposite is true of the Pike's grocery bag--light brown and very dry.  Not that it's a bad thing, again for the casual drinker, this is a "good" coffee--nothing that is particularly intense or memorable.  This is the type of coffee I'd probably serve at a holiday dinner with mixed company.  However, this isn't something I'd keep on hand for my own use--I'm going to stick with my mail orders for freshly roasted beans from Peet's Coffee.

reviews.title: Coffee Prosumer Says "Rebranded McDonalds Coffee!"
reviews.body:
Some background on my coffee history: I got my start in being a coffee nut when I volunteered to help out in a friend's coffee shop. He trained me on a beautiful italian espresso machine, taught me to adjust the grind and tamp to get good espresso, about different roasts, and the simple marvel of the french press. His shop closed not long afterward, but I took my knowledge and love of coffee with me. I've gone through several methods of brewing coffee, including the AeroPress, french press, stovetop "espresso" maker, etc. I currently have a Gaggia espresso machine at home, but my current favorite coffee vessel is a simple Bodum drip vessel with a gold filter (boil the water yourself, pour over grounds). Simple, easy to clean thoroughly, and makes a very good cup of coffee.

When I heard that McDonalds coffee was getting good reviews, and that people were supposedly more satisfied with their coffee than with Starbucks (not an impressive feat in and of itself, but impressive enough for a fast food chain), I decided to give it a try. I wasn't impressed. What I got was a 2 dimensional caricature of the real thing. It was almost coffee, but it was missing a lot of the subtle nuance I was used to tasting, even in mass-produced "office coffee". The only good thing I could say about it was that it was inoffensive. It had none of the bitter nastiness associated with cheap brew.

Then Starbucks came out with the Pike Place Roast. I guess they heard about those customer satisfaction surveys, and some bonehead decided that it'd be a good idea to try to reverse engineer McDonalds coffee and pass it off as this new special house blend. That's the only explanation I can think of for how similar Pike Place and McDonalds coffee taste. Like a 2 dimensional caricature of the real thing.

Bottom line:

-Like coffee, without the complexity.
-Inoffensive.
-Almost exactly like McDonalds coffee.

I just pretend like Pike Place Roast doesn't exist. That way I don't get headaches trying to figure out why Starbucks makes coffee that tastes like it comes with the golden arches on the cup.

reviews.title: Pike's Place Roast....Uh...no....
reviews.body:
I'll only get a Vente Pikes Place Roast if it's all Starbucks has and I'll never every buy the beans at the store. To me it lacks a full flavor and characteristically has a bitter/acidic after taste. Because I dislike Pike's Place roast so much I bought a french press and bought some original House blend. To my horror, House now tastes very similar to Pike's Place. I'm going to retry the Italian blend next.

I will give credit though where credit is due. If Starbucks roasts and brews Pike's Place like they're supposed to the coffee tastes OKish. But often times, I either get burnt tasting coffee, acidic tasting coffee, or coffee that has a lingering aftertaste of soap suds.

Let me just leave you with a qoute from the House Blend package before the quote disappears as the flavor has:

"When we opened our first store in Seattle's Pike's Place Market, we wanted a House Blend that captured the signature expression of our roasting style--glistening, dark chestnut beans loaded with flavor. Years later, it's still why people come through our doors"

Question Starbucks,

1.> If House is still your signature expression of your roasting style, why'd you leave it behind?
2.> If House is why people walk through your doors, why are you serving Pike's Place?

Different strokes for different folks i suppose.  I can't stand bitter ale beer.  What you call "weak" is in essence actually in reality "smooth" in my world, this coffee is definitely not weak. This coffee can be strong tasting if made correctly.  Some are misguided as are most coffee drinkers are nowadays thinking that "bitter" coffee is better coffee or regular tasting coffee.  When in fact normal coffees taste more like this veranda blend.  It wasn't until recently that people started "thinking" that bitter coffee means better coffee, wrong.  I believe people have to be crazy to not like this blend!?  If made correctly and ground from fresh beans, this is very delicious very smooth very tasty awesome ultra delicious almost chocolatey coffee!  When ground from fresh beans this has a chocolatey beautiful aroma that is a must smell! This blend surely beats all regular supermarket ground coffees by a landslide and definitely is a superior coffee in every way among all other coffees for both flavor and caffeine.

reviews.title: meh... not a fave, prefer the other blonde
reviews.body:
When Starbucks came out with the "blonde" roasts, I got pretty excited because I prefer lighter roasts (as do 40% of coffee drinkers, according to the barista at the store)... light roasts are a little earthier, not as burnt tasting. So I scored a bag each of the Willow and Veranda.

This one, the Veranda, didn't do a lot for us. Subjectively speaking, it was so smooth it was boring... it had no snap, and was kind of mixed and mushy, not a definitive flavor. It's supposed to have "delicate nuances of soft cocoa and lightly toasted nuts" - really? We missed that.

On the other hand, we really liked the Willow, which had a brighter citrus-y note and was more flavorful. The taste was (for lack of better words) clear, defined. You buy a light roast to taste the bean, not the roast. The Willow was flavorful, not acidy, and had a clean finish.

Your tastes may vary, but if you like a snappy light roast, or a "breakfast roast" the Veranda probably won't be your pick, but do try the Willow.

reviews.title: Coffee Without the Actual Coffee Flavor; but Plenty of Caffeine(!!)
reviews.body:
This doesn't taste like coffee as we commonly expect today. It's more like ground coffee you can buy in a supermarket or even tea that's been brewed for quite a long time. Think Folger's or Maxwell House--or the stuff you get at Denny's.

Here's a VERY telling statistic: As of June 2014, this "coffee" ranks #79 at Amazon under Grocery & Gourmet Food > Beverages > Coffee > Coffee SUBSTITUTES. I'm not making this up; apparently the majority of Amazon customers see this as a "coffee substitute."

If you're going to drink "weak" coffee without a lot of strong coffee flavor, you might as well save yourself quite a bit of money by buying non-$tarbucks. Buy whatever's cheap in a can at the supermarket, and you'll probably be just as happy.

Also note, the lighter the roast, the higher the caffeine content. (I think that is why lighter roast coffees are popular with some folks.)

reviews.title: A smooth and balanced coffee. Not acidic, sour, or bitter.
reviews.body:
OLD REVIEW, SEE EDITS: A smooth and balanced coffee. Not acidic, sour, or bitter. So far, this is the only Starbucks-brand coffee I can say is truly good. I drink all coffee black, so I can taste all the subtleties. I absolutely love the smell of these ground beans, which have a very nutty and buttery aroma. Some of that delight makes it through into the coffee, but as with all coffees, the aroma beats the drink.

I'm on a search for something even better, but for home-brew ground coffee, this is one of my two current favorites. Note that I do like dark, bold roasted coffees sometimes, but Starbucks are usually burnt and bitter tasting, especially when brewed at their stores. My other current favorite which is quite different is Gevalia's dark Italian Roast (Tassimo).

EDIT: A few months after I wrote the review above, Starbucks silently changed the sourcing and/or the roasting for this blend. It is now nearly a medium roast, not light. It used to actually look golden when ground, but now is medium brown (like nearly all coffees). It also doesn't have nearly the level of buttery and nutty flavor I recall it used to. So, it's still good, but not outstanding.

I have found two special varieties of Starbucks beans I prefer, so look those up. My current favorite from Starbucks is Costa Rica Premium Select, with their Kenya Premium Select as second.

reviews.title: Soft as a Spring Day
reviews.body:
.

Recently on a relaxing vacation, I discovered that I had neglected to bring my favorite coffee. Although I usually avoid buying coffee in a supermarket, I was stuck. So I shopped a local grocery store to purchase enough coffee for my vacation. I looked for a Kona blend with a higher percentage Kona than I usually find without luck. Then I spotted this Starbucks blend that I have seen advertized and decided to try it.

Starbucks Blonde Veranda coffee is a light roast coffee that is advertized as having lighter body and mellow favors. Starbucks claims that roasting for less time frees "nuances" of cocoa and toasted nuts.

Not as sharp and energetic as my favorite dark roasts, yet still flavorful. Blonde Veranda Blend is soft and gentle like cool drink on a summers day.

I enjoyed this experience and recommend Starbucks Blonde Veranda Blend for those who like light roast coffee, and maybe, for those who love dark roast, as an occasional treat.

reviews.title: Excellent Corporate Laptop Backpack
reviews.body:
I love this laptop backpack. I read through all the reviews on Amazon.com and selected this one based on the many positive reviews so am adding my own to help others.

I am a 44 year old sales executive and wanted something very functional but something also very "corporate looking" that I could bring into client meetings without looking like I just walked off a college campus somewhere. Candidly, I also wanted something masculine and the Swiss-Army brand fit the bill. In terms of construction the material is very well put together, tough and durable. I have also found it to be very water resistant (hesitant to say waterproof because I have never really tested it unprotected in a full out downpour). The backpack is quite comfortable to wear even when heavy, as I test in my daily 15 minute walk from the train to my office. The inside is very functional and well organized, with several pen-pockets (there is nothing as maddening as trying to find a pen in the bottom of a full backpack), another pocket I use to hold my business cards, a phone pocket, and several other utility pockets. Also love the port at the top for earphones to feed through since I often listen to my iPhone when walking to work; this allows me to have the iPhone in the backpack rather than in my hand and just go through one of my playlists.

The side zipper for the laptop is very handy and keeps the laptop separate from everything else. The side zipper makes it super easy to take the laptop in and out and there is a velcro strap within the pocket to secure the laptop. I also love the pack's ability to send the laptop through the airport screener without removing it and have used that functionality several times without any questions from the TSA.

Excellent product. Completely satisfied.

reviews.body: Review written from the perspective of tech-dependent road warrior and compared to several Ogio bags that I have had previously that worked great. This bag looks good, and I bought it largely b/c of the TSA-friendly zipper option to open up the bag. However, with Pre-Check, I've never actually used that feature and have been really disappointed with the bag otherwise. If you have a lot of small cables, back up batteries, thumb drives, connections, dash mounts, biz cards, etc, there is really only ONE zippered pocket for this and it's inside one of the main compartments. If you like putting your laptop bag on top of your roller bag for going through the airport, the top handle is in fashioned in such a way that it will fall off unless you're holding both the roller and laptop bag handles. The side water bottle slots have loose elastic and are very shallow, and I've never had any size bottle stay put. I also have stitching coming out in several places after a couple years of (fairly hard) use. Not a good product.

reviews.title: Ideal backpack for work or travel
reviews.body:
Ever since I got a full time job, I've only been using SwissGear backpacks. They've all served me well, and this one is no exception.

I use this backpack daily for work. I'm an avid photographer and keep a bridge camera and P&S with me in this backpack at all times. I keep my work laptop (or personal laptop if using for personal travel) in the assigned slot for laptops. The padding and straps are excellent. I can carry this backpack around for quite a while and still don't feel any strain.

When I'm making short trips for a couple of days or so, this backpack is all I need to carry. There are ample compartments and enough room for me to put a couple of days worth of change of clothes and toiletries in one compartment, cameras and headset in another, and of course the dedicated compartment for laptops is where I place my laptop.

The front-most compartment can be used for placing other things like eyeglass cases, pens, and other things.

All in all this is a great backpack! Perfect for my daily work, perfect for short trips, and even for longer trips I still carry this backpack (in addition to other pieces of luggage depending on what the situation dictates for the longer trips).

reviews.title: First "nice" backpack, would buy again.
reviews.body: Whoever designed this backpack loves all of us and wants us to be happy. I had shied away from SwissGear bags because of the price, but it was on sale and I'm hanging my head in shame for not buying this earlier. Super roomy bag that holds everything, but holds its shape well when you don't need to carry much. The ScanSmart pocket for laptops worked at DCA in August 2014, and I can't wait to try it again. One pocket goes to ScanSmart, the second opens for notebooks and other things, there's a third that's wider and shallower (under the logo), and the front pocket has a place for everything (keys, pens, lip balm, all the things that bounce around and usually get cluttered). There is also a small pocket for a phone, camera, or iPod behind the SwissGear logo--accessible to you, but hidden from anyone who isn't welcome in your bag. Maybe these are standard features for SwissGear bags, but the tiniest things make such a difference. The shoulder straps and back make it unusually comfortable to carry a heavy load. My only complaints are that the water bottle pockets are not quite as deep as I'd like, and the logo on the back portion can cause clothing to develop pills. Great bag.

reviews.title: Good quality shampoo
reviews.body:
We have been using this product for about 3 years now. I have relatively short hair [#2 and #6 on the clippers], but my wife has hair down to her waist. I use this product all the time and she uses it about half the time. Both of us appreciate the quality that we would expect with TRESemme and note that it's the first shampoo that we have agreed on in 35 years of marriage. It doesn't dry out the hair, it's gets the hair very clean, lathers up fantastic, and washes out completely.

No complaints, even though we both have our share of silver. Many shampoos will leave silver hair looking dull or even yellowed. However, with this shampoo, both of us have bright and shiny silver and are quite pleased.

And to top it off, it's very inexpensive to use.
